Hottest Black Friday Tech Deals
Get an RTX 5080 PC from HP's HyperX gaming brand with Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, with plenty of space to upgrade. Also features Wi-Fi 7.
Read moreRead less▼
The Corsair Xeneon Edge is a 14.5-inch display designed to serve as an extension for your desktop and give you a small screen to host your most important apps. Its versatility means you can mount it practically anywhere — horizontally under your main monitor, vertically beside your primary display, or as a digital status panel inside your PC case.
Read moreRead less▼
Get a 25-piece electric screwdriver for PC maintenance or any DIY task. Comes with a 1,500mAh battery, LED, and extension rod.
Read moreRead less▼
Apple's base MacBook Neo has an A18 Pro chip, 256GB of storage, and 8GB of RAM. A solid alternative with a more powerful SoC.
Read moreRead less▼
The Dell XPS 13 with an Intel Core 5 320, 8GB of RAM, and 256 GB of storage.
Read moreRead less▼
This T-Force G50 Evo offers sequential read speeds of 5,000 MB/s and write speeds of up to 4,800 MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
Returning to its lowest-ever price, get a 32-inch curved QHD (2560 x 1440) gaming monitor with a 165Hz refresh rate for just $189, a massive $140 saving.
Read moreRead less▼
This external power button has a 2-meter (~78 inches) cabl, along with a splitter that lets you connect both to your case's front panel buttons. It also includes adhesive pads and zip ties.
Read moreRead less▼
Now with M.2 NVMe SSD dock!
The most expensive of the bunch, this optical CD/DVD writer from SUIDEK upgrades the SATA dock to an M.2 NVMe SSD dock, but keeps the SD card reader, USB-A, and USB-C hub.
Read moreRead less▼
* The listed previous prices can vary based on retailer, as many use different metrics, like 90-day rolling averages or ‘estimated value’ due to ongoing shortages and price hikes.
LIVE: Latest Updates
8Bitdo’s upgraded SNES-inspired SN30 controller is $33 & offers drift-resistant hall effect sticks
8BitDo's controllers are, broadly speaking, excellent. Its SN30 controller carries with it a clearly SNES-inspired look, with modern features like dual analog joysticks and compatibility across PC, Android, Mac, Windows, and Steam. The controller itself has been out for quite some time, but recently 8BitDo upgraded the SN30 to feature magnetic Hall Effect joysticks.
With its SNES-inspired design, this controller will entice gamers of a certain age. But its appeal goes beyond its looks, with Hall Effect joysticks and support for the Switch 1 and 2, PC, macOS, and basically any OS that supports games and Bluetooth.
Read moreRead less▼
Luckily, it's this upgraded Hall Effect-equipped version of the controller that's gone on sale. You get a suite of modern controls, like clickable L3 and R3 buttons, rumble, motion controls, and Bluetooth. Just note that given the size and layout of the SN30, the only thing it omits is analog triggers.
After receiving a firmware update, the pad can also be used on the Nintendo Switch 2 across any title that supports a Pro Controller. This gives it a wide range of versatility across platforms, but do be warned: the smaller size of the pad can take a while to get used to, and for those with larger hands, you might find this to be a little uncomfortable. But, at this price point, it's difficult to argue with the value on offer here. I own two of these controllers, but sadly the fancy transparent versions aren't on sale this time around. These pads are perfect for playing old retro platformers and beat-em-ups like Streets of Rage 4. — Sayem Ahmed
Trade your cash for cache with these discounts on the AMD 9950X3D and 9950X3D2 at Amazon
If you want chart-topping gaming and productivity performance in a single CPU, AMD's 16-core X3D chips are uncontested. They both provide gaming performance on par with the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, top the charts in multithreaded productivity applications, and are in a close second place to Intel's Arrow Lake Refresh in single-threaded apps. Both CPUs are on deep discount for Black Friday, with the dual-CCD Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 hitting an all-time low at $759.
Okay, now AMD's chart-topping Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 might not be the CPU to choose if you're looking for overall value, but if you're after a multithreaded productivity workhorse that stands on par with Intel's best, while also offering the gaming performance of the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, it might be worth a look. Yesterday we spotted that the cache-abundant CPU hit an all-time-low price, with a $140 discount at Amazon, making its price a little bit more palatable. If you're not in need of AMD's biggest and best, then you can also grab a solid $115 discount on the 9950X3D.
The Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 is AMD's first dual-CCD CPU with 3D V-Cache. It sports 16 cores and 192 MB of L3 cache, and it can boost up to 5.6 GHz.
Read moreRead less▼
The Ryzen 9 9950X3D features 128MB of L3 cache, which enables it to claim the title of the fastest gaming chip on the market. It features 16 Zen 5 cores and 32 threads of computing power, reaching a peak clock speed of 5.7 GHz.
Read moreRead less▼
Both CPUs feature 16 Zen 5 cores and 32 threads, along with AMD's stacked 3D V-Cache. The main difference is that the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 has that stacked across on both of its two CCDs, while the Ryzen 9 9950X3D only has the stacked cache on a single CCD. To accommodate the extra cache, the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 also has a 100 MHz reduction in maximum boost clock, topping out at 5.6 GHz compared to 5.7 GHz on the 9950X3D.
The pair of CPUs feature a total of 16 cores and 32 threads, based on AMD's Zen 5 architecture, and utilize a stacked 3D V-Cache, which gives both chips an edge in gaming. If you're looking at the Ryzen 9 9950X3D2, the difference between the two is that the aforementioned cache is spread across both CCDs, instead of just the one on the 9950X3D. The 9950X3D2 also has slightly lower clock speeds, boosting to 5.6 GHz instead of the 5.7 GHz seen on the 9950X3D. To help you pick, we've dropped a bunch of performance charts below.
There's a 4% difference between the 9950X3D2 and 9900X3D in productivity workloads, and generally speaking, most people won't notice the difference between the two, as in gaming workloads, the chips are pretty much identical. If you want to save some cash, and some cache, choose the 9950X3D. If you want top-class performance at a top-shelf price, choose the 9950X3D2. — Sayem Ahmed
This is the cheapest 2TB PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSD we've seen so far: pay 18 cents per gigabyte for ultra-fast storage
SanDisk’s 2TB Optimus GX Pro 8100 PCIe 5.0 SSD got a $95 discount and hit an all-time low of $349 over at Amazon. The drive itself boasts up to 14,900 MB/s read speeds and 14,000 MB/s write speeds, almost completely saturating the bandwidth available on its Silicon Motion SM2508 PCIe 5.0 x4 controller. The Optimus GX Pro 8100 uses Kioxia's BiCS8 218-layer TLC 3D CBA NAND, paired with 2GB of DDR4-3200 memory for use as a cache for fast, bursty work.
All-time low price.
Expand your internal storage with SanDisk's 2TB Optimus GX Pro 8100 PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSD. This speedy drive offers 14,900/14,000 r/w speeds and has a 5-year warranty.
Read moreRead less▼
The overall price of the SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 means that you'll be grabbing this incredibly fast storage at a mere 18 cents per gigabyte, which is stellar value for a PCIe 5.0 drive such as this, and it's one of the lowest prices we've seen a 2TB PCIe 5.0 drive drop to this Black Friday weekend.
When we benchmarked the 8TB version of this SSD, we found that under certain conditions, it managed to beat out Samsung's 9100 Pro. In addition to being super quick and cheaper than its closest rivals, you can also expect to get a five-year limited warranty in case things go awry. – Sayem Ahmed
Equip yourself with a monstrous 16TB HDD, priced at just 2 cents per-gigabyte
Getting a good HDD deal in this market is a rare thing, and this deal we spotted yesterday over at Newegg for an external 16TB Seagate HDD works out to just two cents per gigabyte. Yes, it uses a USB 3.0 interface, but for cold storage of larger files, images, or video, you don't really need blisteringly fast transfer speeds in the first place. Coming in at $399.99, Seagate's External HDD might be the answer to all of your storage woes, or just offer you necessary extra room.
The Seagate Expansion Desktop drive is a 16TB HDD that connects via USB 3.0. It's formatted to ExFAT by default, allowing it to work with virtually any platform, straight out of the box. The device is powered by an included AC power cable, and connects to your system over a Micro-B to USB-A connector.
Read moreRead less▼
The Seagate 16TB drive inside is usually easily shuckable, though do take care in doing so if that's your intention: Usually we'll see a white-labelled drive, and it's easy to accidentally damage the HDD while doing so. However, if you're brave enough to void your warranty, it could be a worthwhile endeavor. Getting a 16TB HDD anywhere else will cost much more, so if you're up for a bit of risk-reward, it could make for a solid extra internal drive, or suitable for use in a NAS.
The Micro-B to USB-A connector is a touch outdated in 2026, but if it's still going to be fast enough for transferring files. If you shuck the drive itself, expect standard SATA power and data connectors instead. It's difficult to argue with the price-per-gigabyte on this deal, so if you're looking to upgrade your storage this holiday, don't sleep on this Newegg deal. — Sayem Ahmed
Intel's Core Ultra 7 270K Plus hits $249.99, with a free 360mm AIO and two additional games
Intel's Core Ultra 270K plus lives on our list of the best CPUs for gaming for a good reason; not only is it adept at crunching through the latest games, but it's also our top pick for anyone looking for a top-shelf productivity workhorse. Intel's latest and greatest CPU is listed at $269 at Newegg, but it also comes with a stackable code, knocking the price down to $249 with a handful of free gifts: A Rosewill 360mm AIO liquid cooler, in addition to an Intel Gaming Bundle where you can pick from two free titles, including Total War: Warhammer 40,000, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, and more.
Get Intel's latest and greatest processor, the 270K Plus. The 8p/16e core processor has plenty of oomph to plow through any workflow and games well, too.
Read moreRead less▼
The Intel Core Ultra 270K Plus manages to go toe-to-toe in gaming performance with AMD's Ryzen 7 7800X3D, and is one of the best CPUs available now in productivity workloads. Sporting a total of 24 cores, split into 8 P-Cores and 16 E-Cores, the configuration actually matches the same core config as the much pricier Core Ultra 9 285K. Boasting clock speeds of up to 5.5GHz, this is a seasonal offer you don't want to miss out on. — Sayem Ahmed

articles.title: Cómo liberar espacio en un celular Android: el truco de Google Fotos
articles.text:
Google Fotos permite liberar espacio en un celular Android al borrar del dispositivo las fotos y los videos que ya tienen una copia de seguridad en la plataforma. El contenido seguirá disponible en la aplicación y en photos.google.com, siempre que haya conexión a internet y se inicie sesión en la cuenta.
Antes de aplicar este truco, hay que comprobar que las imágenes y los videos se hayan respaldado correctamente. Google Fotos crea una copia de seguridad en su biblioteca, aunque las fotos y los videos con menos de 30 días continúen almacenados en el teléfono.
La función elimina archivos locales del celular, no las copias guardadas en Google Fotos. Por eso, antes de confirmar la limpieza, es importante revisar que las fotos que se quieren conservar aparezcan en la biblioteca de la plataforma.
Cómo aplicar el truco de Google Fotos para liberar espacio en Android
El primer paso es descargar e instalar la aplicación de Google Fotos en el teléfono o la tablet Android. Luego, hay que abrirla e ingresar a la Cuenta de Google correspondiente.
Dentro de la aplicación, se debe presionar la foto de perfil o la inicial de la cuenta. Allí aparecerá la opción “Libera espacio en este dispositivo”, que permite conocer cuánto almacenamiento se recuperará antes de borrar los elementos del teléfono.
Para eliminar los archivos que ya fueron respaldados, hay que seleccionar “Libera del dispositivo”. La aplicación quitará las copias locales de fotos y videos, por lo que dejarán de ocupar espacio en la memoria interna del celular.
Después de aplicar esta opción, las imágenes y los videos seguirán disponibles en Google Fotos y en photos.google.com. Desde allí será posible verlos, editarlos, compartirlos, eliminarlos y administrar el contenido de la biblioteca.
Sin embargo, las fotos y los videos eliminados del teléfono no aparecerán en la galería integrada del dispositivo. Tampoco podrán verse sin conexión a internet ni si no se accede a la aplicación de Google Fotos.
Además de liberar espacio, la plataforma cuenta con una herramienta de administración de almacenamiento para identificar contenido que podría eliminarse, como fotos desenfocadas, capturas de pantalla y videos de gran tamaño.
Si una foto o un video se borra por error, se puede revisar la papelera de la aplicación de Galería del teléfono. Para recuperarlo, hay que abrir la galería, presionar “Menú”, ingresar a “Papelera”, elegir los archivos y seleccionar “Restablecer”. Las imágenes volverán a aparecer en la galería del dispositivo.
Los pasos pueden variar según el modelo de celular. Si el archivo no aparece en la papelera, es posible que se haya eliminado definitivamente.
Esto ocurre si estuvo en la papelera durante más de 30 días, si se vació la papelera o si se borró de forma definitiva desde la galería sin haber creado antes una copia de seguridad.
Google Fotos advierte que el contenido podría eliminarse si la cuenta no registra actividad durante dos años o más. Por eso, activar la copia de seguridad y sincronización permite conservar las fotos y los videos y recuperarlos con mayor facilidad.
Cómo liberar espacio de Gmail
Liberar espacio en Gmail es posible al eliminar correos con adjuntos grandes y vaciar las carpetas de Papelera y Spam. La cuenta de Google incluye hasta 15 GB compartidos entre Gmail, Drive y Google Fotos, por lo que el problema puede estar también en otros servicios.
Para localizar mensajes pesados, hay que usar el buscador de Gmail desde una computadora con comandos como has:attachment larger:10M. Esta búsqueda muestra correos con archivos adjuntos superiores a 10 MB para decidir cuáles borrar.
Después de seleccionar los mensajes, se debe presionar Eliminar y entrar en Papelera y Spam para vaciarlas. De lo contrario, esos elementos seguirán contando contra el almacenamiento. Google advierte que, tras una limpieza grande, la actualización del espacio disponible puede demorar entre 48 y 72 horas.

articles.title: Microsoft Store App Found Delivering Vinci RAT Capable of Remote System Control
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a cyber attack in which a threat actor leveraged a Microsoft Store application to deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) called Vinci RAT.
The intrusion, according to eSentire, begins with a redirection to a bogus site for a sniping tool ("snipp.codes-team[.]com"), from where a Microsoft-signed installer called "Snipping-Tool.exe" is downloaded. Executing the binary leads to the installation of Setup Assistant, an Electron-based application published on the Microsoft Store by ETPS Ltd.
"The application was heavily obfuscated, maintained communication with C2 [command-and-control] infrastructure, monitored the victim's Downloads folder, and supported execution of C2-supplied PowerShell and JavaScript," eSentire said.
"This access was used to launch a malicious PowerShell stager, establish persistence through a scheduled task, and retrieve a previously undocumented PowerShell-based RAT."
Once installed, Setup Assistant acts as a backdoor and is designed to run obfuscated JavaScript that allows it to contact the C2 server at "setup-assistant[.]com" and retrieve arbitrary PowerShell or JavaScript code, ultimately resulting in the deployment of the RAT by means of a stager.
Vinci RAT, as the malware is called, is equipped to fingerprint the host, enumerate installed security tools, facilitate remote and reverse shell access, deliver files, and execute shellcode, DLL, EXE, and PowerShell payloads.
Interestingly, the arbitrary PowerShell or JavaScript execution is triggered by means of two methods -
- Monitor for file names in the victim's Downloads directory by matching them against a predefined list specified in a C2-retrieved configuration ("MSTeamsSetup.exe" and "Reader_install.exe"). If a match is found, it sends an HTTP POST request to the C2 server and executes the response.
- The C2 server initiates an update action via the URL setup-assistant[.]com/api/update-status?device=<victim_id>"
The Vinci RAT stager is responsible for running a PowerShell command that disables the Windows Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI), generates a unique victim identifier, establishes communication with a C2 server ("monkeysholder[.]info/api.php"), set up persistence via a scheduled task that runs every 10 minutes, and downloads the RAT payload.
Further analysis of the root domain "codes-team[.]com" has identified additional sub-domains that suggest that the threat actors are spoofing software download pages for legitimate applications like Microsoft Teams and Roblox -
- roblx.codes-team[.]com
- teams.codes-team[.]com
- teamsmac.codes-team[.]com
- teams-bing.codes-team[.]com
As of writing, Setup Assistant is no longer accessible on Microsoft Software. It was first released on June 1, 2026, while the "codes-team[.]com" domain was registered in late March 2026.
It remains unclear whether the threat actors themselves took down the app in response to the public disclosure or whether Microsoft removed it, as eSentire noted that the tech giant had failed to take action despite reporting the app through its abuse form on November 10, 2026, responding that it was "not a violation of our terms."
"The campaign highlights how attackers are combining search-engine redirection, fake software download pages, obfuscated Electron applications, and trusted software distribution channels to gain persistent access to victim environments," the Canadian cybersecurity company said.

articles.title: How to Keep Your Security Picture Current When Attackers Move at AI Speed
articles.text:
Most security metrics are not built to be used. They are built to be shown. Somewhere between the quarterly review and the next status update, a set of numbers gets assembled that looks reassuring in a room and tells almost no one what is actually happening across the environment that week. Someone pulls them together the week before, cleans them up, and presents a picture of a program that is, as of that one morning, fine.
This is not a failure of effort. Security teams are doing the work, often times more of it than anyone outside the team realizes. The problem is that the reporting cycle rewards the snapshot, and a snapshot is a memory, not a measurement. It tells you how things looked on the day you looked. It says very little about the weeks in between, and risk does not keep to a reporting schedule.
Gathering the Picture Is the Hard Part, and It Is Getting Harder
The conversation about security metrics usually jumps straight to which numbers matter. That skips the part that actually hurts. Before anyone can report a single metric, someone has to go and gather it, and today that is a genuinely painful job.
The information needed to describe a security posture is scattered across dozens of systems that were never meant to talk to each other. Cloud accounts, identity providers, endpoints, code repositories, ticketing tools, each one holds a piece. Pulling those pieces together usually means logging into one console after another, exporting spreadsheets, taking screenshots, and stitching it all by hand into something presentable. It takes days. It eats the time of people who were hired to do security, not data entry. And by the time the picture is assembled, parts of it are already out of date, because the environment kept changing while the deck was being built.
So the metric that lands in the review is not really a measurement of where things stand. It is a measurement of where things stood, filtered through however long it took to collect. (And filtered, quietly, toward whatever looked defensible that week.)
Attackers Are Not Working on a Quarterly Cadence. With AI, They Are Faster Than Ever.
Here is why the stale snapshot has gone from a weakness to a real liability. The people trying to get in have changed speed.
AI has handed attackers a serious acceleration. Reconnaissance that used to take a skilled operator days now runs in minutes. Phishing that used to read as obviously fake now arrives fluent and personalized at scale. Known weaknesses get found and probed almost as fast as they appear. The attack side has automated the slow parts, and the result is adversaries who move in hours, iterate constantly, and do not pause politely between your reporting cycles.
Now put the two timelines next to each other. On one side, a picture of your security that is gathered by hand, a few times a year, and is slightly stale the moment it is finished. On the other, an adversary moving at machine speed, every day, including the long quiet stretch between your last review and your next one. That gap was always uncomfortable. Against AI-accelerated attackers, it is the whole game.
The Real Shift Is From Reporting to Visibility
The fix is not a better slide. It is being able to see where you actually stand, continuously, without a person having to go assemble it first.
That is worth saying plainly, because it is easy to confuse with detection. This is not about catching the attacker in the act. It is about never losing sight of your own environment in the first place, knowing what you have, what is covered, what changed, and where the gaps are, as a living picture rather than a quarterly photograph. Continuous visibility into the real environment, pulled straight from the systems that already hold the data, is what turns a security posture from something you reconstruct under deadline into something you can simply look at, any day, and trust.
This is the problem Anecdotes was built to solve. Instead of a person logging into one console after another and rebuilding the picture by hand, it connects directly to the systems a company already runs, the cloud accounts, identity providers, code repositories, and the hundreds of other tools where the real state actually lives, and pulls the information straight from the source. The picture assembles itself and stays current, so the question stops being how many days it will take to gather and becomes simply what the data says right now. And to be clear about what that is and is not, it does not chase the attacker for you. It makes sure you are never the last to know what your own environment looks like.
When the picture is always current, the work changes shape. Nobody spends the week before the review gathering. The number is just there, today's number, and the team spends its time acting on what it says instead of proving it exists.
Start With One
None of this requires rebuilding everything at once, and anyone who says it does is selling something. Pick one thing worth seeing clearly, coverage, say, or how long exposures stay open. Connect it to the source so it keeps itself current. Watch it for a month, and let it tell you something uncomfortable.
Security is not a thing that is true on review day. It is true, or it is not, on an ordinary Tuesday, when no one is looking and last quarter's slide is gathering dust in a shared drive. And on that Tuesday, the attackers are not waiting. The teams that stay ahead are not the ones with the best-looking dashboards. They are the ones who can see where they stand at any moment, without having to go dig for it first.

articles.title: This Lenovo LOQ notebook with Arc B390 graphics is just $799 this Black Friday — get a gaming-ready Panther Lake laptop for a super low price
articles.text:
This Lenovo LOQ notebook with Arc B390 graphics is just $799 this Black Friday — get a gaming-ready Panther Lake laptop for a super low price
It's hard to find a good cheap laptop these days, but this one qualifies
Need an entry-level gaming laptop this Black Friday? There's been slim pickings this year as the AI supply crunch sucks up more and more silicon, and most gaming laptops worth anything are now over $1500. But Lenovo's LOQ Essential gaming laptop could make a great first PC for the gamer in your life or serve as a powerful basic notebook PC for a good price. This system is just $799.99 at Best Buy right now, but it's got real gaming cred thanks to its cutting-edge Core Ultra X7 358H CPU with Arc B390 graphics.
Yes, the Arc B390 is an integrated GPU. But it has real gaming chops that should deliver playable experiences at 1080p medium or high settings in a wide range of games, and you can augment its performance with XeSS upscaling and Xe Multi Frame Generation in compatible titles. For a first gaming system or a workhorse laptop that can game on the side, the Arc B390 is a perfect fit. And again, this Lenovo system is just $799.99.
Lenovo's LOQ Essential gaming notebook gets you into the game with a powerful Arc B390 iGPU. A 1200p 165Hz screen, 16GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD round out this budget-friendly gaming laptop.
In our own testing of the Arc B390 aboard another Panther Lake system, we found that this iGPU outperforms all comparable graphics processors in its class. Even in the demanding Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, our tests demonstrated playable baseline performance at 1080p Low settings. And as we mentioned, you can add XeSS upscaling and frame generation to the mix to boost performance further.
Lenovo uses a 165Hz, 1920x1200 IPS panel on this system with a max brightness of 300 nits, so it's well matched to the capabilities of the Arc B390.
Beyond the Arc B390, the cutting-edge Core Ultra X7 358H gets you 16 Panther Lake cores (4P + 8E + 4 LPE) with max boost frequencies of 4.8 GHz, so this system is just as ready to tackle tough general workloads as it is gaming. You also get surprisingly high-end connectivity with a Thunderbolt 4 USB Type-C port, three USB 3.2 Type-A ports, HDMI, and even an Ethernet jack. For a final touch of gaming flair, this laptop has an RGB LED keyboard, too.
There are a couple compromises with this system to hit such a low price. The 16GB of LPDDR5X-8533 onboard memory is soldered, so you won't be able to upgrade it down the line. And the 512GB SSD is quite small for a 2026 laptop. But in the midst of the AI supply crunch, those are reasonable compromises for such a cheap laptop with otherwise cutting-edge specs.
If you need a cheap basic laptop or a first gaming laptop for a lucky recipient this holiday season, this LOQ Essential is a great deal at just $799.99 this Black Friday. Get it while you can.

articles.title: Pourquoi ChatGPT finit-il (trop) souvent par faire exactement ce que vous lui avez demandé de ne pas faire ?
articles.text:
Vous lui avez demandé de faire court ou de ne jamais utiliser de listes à puces, mais ChatGPT a fini par oublier vos consignes. Dans notre nouvelle vidéo, on vous explique pourquoi les IA perdent le fil de nos conversations et comment éviter d'en arriver là.
Il y a quelque chose d'assez exaspérant à devoir rappeler à ChatGPT une consigne qu'il a lui-même reformulée quelques minutes plus tôt pour vous assurer qu'il avait bien compris. Plus frustrant encore, vous pouvez retrouver la trace de cette consigne en remontant le fil de votre conversation. Alors pourquoi faudrait-il la lui répéter ? Après tout, elle est toujours là, sous vos yeux comme sous les siens. Du moins, c'est ce que l'on pourrait croire.
Ce que vous voyez de votre conversation n'est pas forcément ce que voit ChatGPT
Contrairement à nous, qui pouvons relire l'intégralité de nos échanges, les modèles d'intelligence artificielle ne peuvent traiter qu'une quantité limitée d'informations à la fois. Cette capacité, que l'on appelle la fenêtre de contexte, ne se mesure ni en nombre de mots ni en nombre de messages, mais en tokens, ces petites unités de texte qui peuvent correspondre à un mot entier, à une partie de mot ou encore à un signe de ponctuation, et auxquelles nous avons déjà consacré un dossier.
Or, à mesure que vous échangez avec ChatGPT, vos messages, les informations extraites des documents que vous lui transmettez et ses réponses (y compris celle en cours de génération) se disputent la place disponible dans cette fenêtre. Une partie de cet espace est aussi consacrée à des éléments qui n'apparaissent pas à l'écran, comme les instructions qu'OpenAI fournit au modèle pour encadrer son comportement et les tokens supplémentaires que génèrent les modèles de raisonnement pour préparer leurs réponses.
Pour éviter de saturer la fenêtre de contexte, le service peut alors être amené à faire le tri dans les échanges précédents, en résumant ou en écartant une partie de leur contenu, quitte à perdre au passage quelques informations qui avaient pourtant leur importance à vos yeux. Votre première consigne peut ainsi toujours figurer dans l'historique affiché à l'écran sans que le modèle y ait encore accès au moment de vous répondre.
Plus de tokens ne veut pas forcément dire moins d'oublis
En toute logique, on pourrait donc penser qu'il suffit d'augmenter la taille de la fenêtre de contexte pour résoudre le problème. Mais si les capacités de traitement des modèles de langage ont énormément progressé ces dernières années, au point de dépasser le million de tokens pour plusieurs d'entre eux, leur aptitude à exploiter les informations dont ils disposent dépend aussi de leur position dans le contexte (tout ce à quoi le modèle a accès au moment de répondre : instructions, historique des échanges, extraits de documents, etc.).
En 2024, des chercheurs ont ainsi montré que plusieurs modèles de langage parvenaient plus facilement à retrouver une information lorsqu'elle figurait au début ou à la fin d'un long texte plutôt qu'au milieu. Baptisé Lost in the Middle, ce phénomène a depuis été observé chez des modèles plus récents et pourrait expliquer en partie pourquoi une IA peut passer outre une consigne à laquelle elle a pourtant toujours accès.
L'augmentation de la taille des fenêtres de contexte se heurte par ailleurs à des considérations économiques. Chaque nouvel échange peut nécessiter de traiter à nouveau une bonne partie de l'historique de la conversation. Or, plus la fenêtre de contexte est grande, plus le volume de tokens à traiter à chaque échange peut être important et plus les besoins en puissance de calcul risquent de peser sur les dépenses des éditeurs d'IA, même s'ils disposent de systèmes de cache pour réutiliser une partie des calculs précédents.
Quelques habitudes à prendre pour éviter de perdre le fil
Puisque les modèles de langage tendent à mieux exploiter les informations situées en fin de contexte et que la gestion des conversations longues privilégie souvent les échanges les plus récents, le simple fait de rappeler une consigne à ChatGPT au moment de lui soumettre une nouvelle demande peut l'aider à mieux la respecter.
Vous avez aussi tout intérêt à consacrer une conversation à chaque sujet et, lorsque les échanges s'éternisent, à demander à ChatGPT de les résumer pour repartir dans une nouvelle discussion, non sans avoir vérifié au préalable que le résumé reprend bien toutes les informations dont vous aurez besoin par la suite. De la même façon, si vous souhaitez faire analyser un document volumineux à une IA, préférez le scinder en plusieurs parties et consigner les résultats intermédiaires dans un document à part.
Quant aux consignes que vous avez l'habitude de donner à ChatGPT quel que soit le sujet de vos échanges, vous pouvez les renseigner dans les instructions personnalisées, accessibles depuis la rubrique « Personnalisation » des paramètres du service. Si rien ne garantit à 100 % que le chatbot s'y conformera en toutes circonstances, vous n'aurez au moins plus à les ressaisir chaque fois que vous entamez une nouvelle conversation.

articles.title: Por qué no se puede programar mensajes en WhatsApp y cómo solucionarlo
articles.text:
WhatsApp ahora permite programar mensajes tanto en Android, iPhone y en la versión Web. Sin embargo, es posible que no te aparezca esa nueva opción. En estos casos, es recomendable actualizar sistemas operativos y la misma aplicación.
Para actualizar el sistema operativo, debes ir a los ajustes del celular y buscar el apartado que haga referencia a esta necesidad. En cuanto a la aplicación, debes ingresar a la tienda de aplicaciones, buscar WhatsApp y así, verificar si hay alguna actualización pendiente.
En el caso de WhatsApp Web, es recomendable actualizar el sistema operativo del computador.
Si después de verificar todas las actualizaciones disponibles, sigue sin aparecer dicha función, es posible que la plataforma de mensajería la habilite proximamente para tu dispositivo. WhatsApp despliega sus novedades de forma gradual.
Cabe mencionar que esta función de programar mensajes se encuentra presente en la versión 26.46.74 de la app.
Cómo actualizar mi celular Android
Antes de empezar, conecta el equipo a una red Wi‑Fi estable, verifica que tenga al menos 50 % de batería y realiza una copia de seguridad de tus archivos importantes.
Luego abre Ajustes, ingresa en Sistema y selecciona Actualización del sistema; los nombres pueden variar según la marca.
Pulsa Buscar actualizaciones y sigue las indicaciones en pantalla. Si existe una versión disponible, descarga e instálala sin interrumpir el proceso. Al reiniciarse, revisa que tus aplicaciones funcionen correctamente y actualízalas desde Google Play si es necesario.
Cómo actualizar un iPhone a la última versión de iOS
Para actualizar un iPhone a la versión más reciente de iOS, primero realiza una copia de seguridad en iCloud o en una computadora. Luego, conecta el dispositivo a una red wifi y a una fuente de alimentación para evitar interrupciones durante la descarga.
Abre la aplicación Ajustes, ingresa en General y selecciona Actualización de software. El iPhone mostrará la versión instalada y, si corresponde, la actualización disponible para ese modelo. Pulsa Descargar e instalar e ingresa el código de desbloqueo si el sistema lo solicita.
Antes de confirmar, revisa que haya suficiente espacio de almacenamiento. Si falta capacidad, el iPhone puede ofrecer eliminar aplicaciones de forma temporal y reinstalarlas al finalizar el proceso.
Es posible activar las actualizaciones automáticas desde Ajustes, General, Actualización de software y Actualizaciones automáticas. De esta manera, el iPhone podrá descargar el software y completar la instalación durante la noche, siempre que esté conectado a wifi y cargándose.
Cómo actualizar la app de WhatsApp
Para actualizar WhatsApp, abre la tienda de aplicaciones de tu celular y busca “WhatsApp Messenger”.
En Android, ingresa a Google Play Store; en iPhone, abre la App Store. Si hay una versión nueva disponible, aparecerá el botón Actualizar. Púlsalo y espera a que finalice la descarga e instalación.
Antes de iniciar el proceso, verifica que el teléfono tenga conexión estable a wifi o datos móviles y suficiente espacio de almacenamiento. WhatsApp recomienda mantener la aplicación actualizada para acceder a las funciones más recientes y recibir correcciones de errores.
Puedes activar las actualizaciones automáticas desde los ajustes de Google Play o App Store. Así, el teléfono instalará las nuevas versiones cuando estén disponibles, sin necesidad de buscar la aplicación manualmente.
Cómo programar mensajes en WhatsApp
WhatsApp permite programar mensajes desde iPhone, Android y WhatsApp Web. Para hacerlo, abre la conversación, redacta el texto y selecciona la opción para definir la fecha y la hora de envío. La función permite fijar la entrega desde 10 minutos hasta 14 días después.
Los mensajes programados permanecen cifrados de extremo a extremo y se envían a la hora elegida, incluso si el teléfono está apagado o sin batería. Antes del horario establecido, el usuario puede revisar los envíos pendientes y eliminarlos si cambia de opinión. El destinatario recibirá el mensaje como cualquier otro, sin ninguna marca especial al recibirlo.

articles.title: I’ve been testing laptops for 25 years, and these Black Friday deals on the impressive and fun MacBook Neo and the ultra-light Dell XPS are making my head spin
articles.text:
I’ve been testing laptops for 25 years, and these Black Friday deals on the impressive and fun MacBook Neo and the ultra-light Dell XPS are making my head spin
Battle of the platforms
The question of which budget laptop you should buy is always a tough one, but if you're in the market for more value-friendly computing portables, Black Friday is your time to lean in and open your wallet. In a surprising turn of events, the MacBook Neo, which has bounced from a starting price of $599 up to $699, is now, thanks to an Amazon deal, back to $599 (was $699). But to make things more complicated, there is another very attractive Black Friday offering on the other side of the platform aisle: the Dell XPS 13-inch laptop, which is currently starting at $549.99 (down from $749.99).
Yes, the prices are close, but these two excellent laptops have more in common than dollars and cents — along with some notable differences — that may help you decide which laptop is right for you or as a treasured gift for someone else this holiday season.
• Browse all today's best Black Friday deals
If you're thinking about only buying the best, then the MacBook Neo is probably your first choice. It's true, the specs might sound a little too budget: an A18 Pro chip last seen in an iPhone, just 8 GB of RAM, and 256GB of storage to start. Still, when I put the laptop through its paces, I found it more than capable of standing toe-to-toe with the MacBook Air M1.
The Dell XPS 13 inch (2026 edition) is similarly configured, with 8GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and a mid-range Intel Core 5 230.
Both systems have essentially integrated graphics, but the Neo has distinct cores assigned to graphics operations. Check out both deals below.
Intel Core 5 320 | 8GB LPDDR5X | 256GB SSD
Running Windows 11 Home, the Dell XPS 13 features a 13.4" Touch QHD+ display, two Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, and DisplayPort 2.1 and Power Delivery. Other configurations are available from Dell, which boosts the storage and memory, but this is the cheapest. For basic office duties, it'll handle it well.
Things get more interesting when you look at portability. The Dell XPS 13-inch weighs just 2.2lbs. The MacBook Neo, by contrast, weighs 2.7lbs. Neither is a heavyweight, but if portability is your number one priority, you might lean toward the Dell XPS.
What's interesting here is that, despite the XPS's lighter weight, it actually bested the Neo in our battery tests, with approximately 16 hours, compared to the MacBook Neo's 13 hours.
While I'm a fan of the MacBook Neo's color choices, including the playful Citrus, the Dell XPS 13-inch is certainly sleek and sexy.
The screen differences are where things get really interesting. The Dell XPS has a slightly larger 13.4-inch display as compared to the MacBook Neo, but only the XPS offers touch. Now, Apple finally does have a touch-screen computer in its lineup, but it's not the affordable Neo, instead, the brand-new MacBook Pro PROLED XDR gets that feature.
Display: 13 inches
Processor: A18 Pro
RAM: 8GB
Storage: 256GB
The MacBook Neo packs a 13-inch Liquid Retina display, an A18 Pro chip, 8GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and up to 16 hours of battery life, all for $599, which is fantastic value. Discounts have been better in the past, but I think these will be rarer to see over the coming months and this price likely won't be beaten over Black Friday.
Naturally, this leads us to platform. You see, it's not unusual for a Windows 11 system to offer a touch display, so ultra-portable Windows users almost expect it, and it's a nice addition on a sub-$600 laptop deal.
If price is important enough for you to choose one platform over the other, the XPS is, with this Black Friday deal, $50 cheaper than the MacBook Neo. However, only one of these laptops was deemed the best budget laptop you can buy.
So, if you're a die-hard Windows fan, this Del XPS 13-inch sounds like the right laptop for you. But if you want the best and are aware that this MacBook Neo Black Friday Deal is soon to run out, then the choice is probably obvious

articles.title: Hackers Trojanize Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK Downloads to Deliver Remote Access Malware
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a software supply chain attack that has tampered with Q-Dir and DesktopOK installation files distributed via the official SoftwareOK website.
"Evidence indicates that malicious files were generated not only when users downloaded the programs directly from the official download page but also during the update process of previously installed legitimate programs," South Korean cybersecurity company AhnLab said.
Q-Dir, also called the Quad Directory Explorer, is a free, lightweight file manager for Windows developed by SoftwareOK. According to its website, DesktopOK is a free Windows utility designed to save and restore desktop icon positions.
The unauthorized modifications are designed such that the malicious activity is challenging to detect when running the programs, while simultaneously retrieving and deploying a Python-based remote control malware (RAT) from an external server.
Once installed, the RAT payload is capable of executing shell commands and Python code, transferring files, capturing screenshots, and collecting system metadata based on commands issued by the attacker.
The following product versions have been confirmed to be poisoned, given the discrepancies in the SHA-256 hashes of the installer files and the presence of additional code that triggers additional file downloads and automatic execution -
- Q-Dir 12.85.0.0
- Q-Dir 12.84.0.0
- Q-Dir 12.83.0.0
- DesktopOK 12.85.0.0
- DesktopOK 12.82.0.0
The exact mechanism that allowed the installation files to be replaced with a trojanized version remains unknown.
"The malicious installer runs the legitimate Q-Dir or DesktopOK to lower the user's suspicion, while simultaneously downloading and installing a Python RAT package from an external server," AhnLab said.
Specifically, this involves downloading two payloads from "mail.c1a2[.]top" -
- 7zr.exe, the legitimate 7-Zip tool to decompress files
- dsv2_py39_agent.7z, a package containing the RAT and Python runtime environment
The attack chain is fairly straightforward in that it uses the 7-Zip tool binary to extract and run the Python RAT. The malware then sets up persistence on the host by means of a scheduled task that impersonates Microsoft Edge to fly under the radar. The task is configured to execute the RAT by launching a Python script named "py_client_dsv2.py."
Upon execution, the RAT establishes communication with its command-and-control (C2) server ("8.210.69[.]51:9876") to receive tasks and run them. It supports the following features -
- Shell command execution
- Python code execution
- File upload and download
- Screenshot capture
- Operating system and system information
It also gathers a list of running processes and compares it against an internal list of various security products used in South Korea and abroad, including AhnLab, ESTSecurity, Hauri, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Trend Micro, Avast, McAfee, ESET, Symantec, Kaspersky, Bitdefender, Sophos, Fortinet, Elastic, and Malwarebytes.
Information about identified security programs is transmitted to the C2 server, so as to help the attackers better plan the next stages of the attack or serve payloads that can bypass detection.
The activity has not been attributed to any known threat actor. However, AhnLab said it identified Chinese language comments in the source code, suggesting that the malware authors or attackers may have used a Chinese-speaking environment.
"Users who are currently using Q-Dir or DesktopOK, or who have recently installed or updated these programs, should verify the hash values of the downloaded files and check their systems for any traces of RAT installation or execution," AhnLab said.
"However, simply uninstalling and reinstalling the program may not remove a Python RAT that has already been installed. Therefore, you should also check for suspicious Python execution environments, scheduled tasks, related files, and traces of external network communication, update your antivirus engine to the latest version, and then perform a full system scan."

articles.title: Get a perfect Alienware 4K OLED 32" display with RGB subpixels for $150 off — 165 Hz refresh rate, 1000-nits HDR, and Dolby Vision support with the AW3226Q
articles.text:
Get a perfect Alienware 4K OLED 32" display with RGB subpixels for $150 off — 165 Hz refresh rate, 1000-nits HDR, and Dolby Vision support with the AW3226Q
Searching for that one monitor that's essentially perfect? Look no further, and the price is a steal.
Usually, buying a monitor involves some sort of compromise: maybe it's not the brightest, or the refresh rate is low, or the text is blurry, etc. How about one that is essentially pitch-perfect? The Alienware AW3226Q, a 32" 4K OLED display with a 165 Hz refresh rate, RGB subpixel layout, and DisplayHDR 400 True Black and Dolby Vision certifications, can be yours for only $549.99 from the Dell store, or $150 off its regular price.
If you're keeping track of features and thinking that this monitor looks about perfect, you're absolutely correct. A resolution of 3840x2160 at 32" is about perfect for a balance between perceptual sharpness and graphics card load in gaming — plus, while ultra-wide displays are excellent for gaming, their curved nature doesn't quite lend itself as well to productivity tasks.
The Alienware is a sharp, colorful OLED display with 4K resolution, 165 Hz refresh rate, and Dolby Vision support.
Make no mistake, though: this isn't a "work monitor." First off, the 165 Hz refresh rate is supported by Nvidia G-Sync and FreeSync Premium Pro compatibility for smooth motion in games, and the peak HDR brightness is 1000 nits, letting you enjoy gorgeous vistas with natural highlights and sun — like, say, in STALKER 2, at least before a mutant chews your face off. As with most any OLED panel, the pixel response time is effectively zero, making for a blur-free experience, and the color gamut covers 99% of the DCI-P3 color space.
The pure RGB subpixel layout is worth expanding on, with good reason — most forms of anti-aliasing, namely but not only for text in Windows, assume left-to-right RGB for each color component. Until relatively recently, OLED monitors had acceptable-to-poor text rendering, because they used unorthodox layouts like RGWB or RGBW pixel arrangements. Meanwhile, this one? Our reviewer called it "easily on par with the best professional displays [he's] reviewed."
The thin frames, height-, tilt-, and swivel-adjustable stand, and built-in USB hub with USB-C power delivery round out the main specifications. Grab the Alienware AW3226Q OLED monitor for only $549.99 at Dell's store.

articles.title: Cómo programar mensajes en iPhone si no puedo hacerlo desde WhatsApp
articles.text:
WhatsApp inició recientemente el despliegue global de la función para programar mensajes en iOS y Android. Sin embargo, al tratarse de un proceso progresivo, es probable que muchos teléfonos aún no tengan acceso a este beneficio.
Ante esta limitación —y para evitar el uso de aplicaciones de terceros que comprometen la privacidad—, los usuarios de iPhone cuentan con una alternativa directa dentro del propio sistema operativo. A través de la aplicación nativa Mensajes, iOS permite redactar textos con anticipación y programarlos mediante la herramienta Enviar más tarde, sin instalar software adicional.
Requisitos y funcionamiento del sistema
Antes de configurar un envío diferido en el iPhone, es necesario considerar las condiciones técnicas establecidas por Apple:
- Uso obligatorio de iMessage. La función opera exclusivamente en conversaciones de iMessage (disponible a partir de iOS 18 y en versiones posteriores como iOS 26 y iOS 27).
- Plazo máximo de anticipación. Los mensajes pueden programarse con un límite de hasta 14 días de antelación.
- Privacidad frente al destinatario. La persona que recibe el mensaje no tiene forma de saber que el texto fue programado previamente.
- Entrega sin conexión y cifrado. Una vez confirmado el envío diferido, el texto se cifra y se almacena temporalmente en los servidores de Apple. Gracias a esto, el mensaje se entregará a la hora exacta aunque el iPhone y el resto de los dispositivos del remitente estén apagados o sin internet. En cuanto se concreta la entrega, el registro se elimina de los servidores de Apple.
Cómo programar un mensaje paso a paso
Para dejar un texto preparado y definir su hora de salida desde el iPhone, siga este procedimiento:
- Abra la aplicación Mensajes en el iPhone e ingrese a la conversación deseada (o inicie un chat nuevo).
- Pulse el botón Agregar (ícono +) ubicado a la izquierda del campo de texto y seleccione la opción Enviar más tarde.
- Toque la hora predeterminada que aparece sobre el cuadro de escritura para desplegar el selector y elija el día y la hora exacta de entrega. El borde del campo de texto pasará a mostrarse con una línea discontinua.
- Escriba el contenido del mensaje y pulse el botón Enviar.
El globo del mensaje quedará visible en la conversación con un borde de línea discontinua y el horario indicado en la parte superior. Una vez alcanzada la hora programada, el globo adoptará su color sólido habitual y la línea discontinua desaparecerá.
Cómo editar, reprogramar o cancelar un envío
Mientras el mensaje no haya sido entregado, el remitente mantiene el control total sobre su contenido y horario. Para realizar cualquiera de estas modificaciones es indispensable contar con conexión a internet.
Abra la conversación correspondiente en Mensajes y desplácese hasta la parte inferior de la pantalla (los textos programados pueden aparecer debajo de los mensajes ya enviados). Desde allí, ejecute la acción necesaria:
- Editar el texto. Mantenga presionado el globo del mensaje, toque Editar, realice las correcciones y pulse el botón Enviar cambio para guardar la nueva versión (o Cancelar cambio para revertirla).
- Cambiar la fecha u hora. Pulse Editar junto a la fecha ubicada encima del mensaje programado, seleccione Editar horario, defina el nuevo momento de entrega y toque fuera del recuadro para confirmar.
- Enviar de inmediato. Pulse Editar junto a la fecha del mensaje y seleccione Enviar mensaje para despacharlo al instante.
- Cancelar y eliminar. Mantenga presionado el globo del mensaje y elija Eliminar. Si la eliminación se realiza antes de la hora fijada, el envío se anula definitivamente y el destinatario no recibe ninguna notificación.

articles.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
articles.text:
Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday.
Three of the attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major disruptions reported. The victims have not been named, and it is not known who is behind the attacks.
Florian Schütz, who directs Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre, gave the figures in an interview with public broadcaster SRF.
All five cases were reported in recent days. Small and medium-sized companies were among the organizations hit, and they came forward voluntarily.
The agency's first notice, a security advisory published on Tuesday, said the agents had compromised the victims' IT systems in every case known at that point. Neither the notice nor yesterday's broadcast interview explains why the count changed.
"These cases represent a shift in the cyber threat landscape," the advisory said.
The targeted operators are in at least two sectors. Electricity, drinking water, and telecommunications suppliers are examples of what Switzerland counts as critical infrastructure, according to a news agency report on the interview.
The attacks involve what the Swiss agency calls agentic offensive frameworks, AI agents that find security weaknesses and carry out attacks on their own. Its advisory named ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI as examples of agents reachable over the internet, not as the tools used in the five cases.
The agents are often used to scan for known, unpatched weaknesses and can run many attacks in parallel, the agency says. When defenses respond, the agents switch methods, leaving companies significantly less time to detect an intrusion and respond.
The number of AI attack tools freely reachable online has nearly doubled since October, according to the agency. The figure counts available tools, not attacks or victims.
Raphael Reischuk, co-founder of Switzerland's National Test Institute for Cybersecurity, expects a larger wave of attacks and says companies underestimate the risk.
Italy's national computer security incident response team, CSIRT Italia, described mass compromise campaigns in an official bulletin this week. In the cases it observed firsthand, AI-directed autonomous agents broke into a large number of systems within a few hours.
The agents adapt their actions within seconds, run in parallel without human input, and chain vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and compromised credentials together, the bulletin says. It names ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI, and DeepSeek Harness, an open-source agent whose Red Team Mode uses a built-in prompt to get past the underlying model's safety limits.
Each action on its own looks like normal user or API traffic. Detection depends on context: where requests come from, how often they arrive, how much data moves, and the order in which things happen.
Britain's National Cyber Security Centre reported the same pattern in agency guidance this week. "Since September 2026, the NCSC has seen a marked rise in AI-assisted cyber attacks," it said.
Some incidents caused downtime on internet-facing services, and others gave attackers a foothold for further agent-driven activity. The weaknesses are old ones: credentials committed to code repositories, misconfigured infrastructure-as-code, default or missing authentication, and weaknesses in APIs.
What has changed is the speed, persistence, and low cost of the attacks, the British agency says. The frameworks are also noisy, which makes them easier to detect.
The European Commission has already been hit. Attackers using ARTEX broke into its human resources, medical reimbursement, and translation systems, the Commission has confirmed, in an earlier intrusion first detected on October 22.
What Defenders Should Do
The strongest common advice from the three agencies is to shrink the time attackers have. Their recommendations overlap:
- Install critical security updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours of release (Switzerland), and patch flaws already being exploited first (Italy).
- Disconnect or isolate internet-facing systems that cannot be patched quickly (Italy).
- Reduce what is reachable from the internet, using geo-blocking, allow lists, and authentication in front of services (Switzerland, UK).
- Require MFA or passkeys on everything reachable from the internet, and grant the lowest privileges that work (Switzerland).
- Watch for unusual behavior and data volumes (Switzerland), and correlate logs: agent activity shows up as bursts of requests and high error rates (UK).
- Put bot challenges on high-value endpoints, and use decoys such as honeytokens to catch and slow agents (UK).
- Load Italy's published indicator feeds into monitoring tools, noting that the indicators change quickly and are valid only for their stated timeframes (Italy).

articles.title: SanDisk’s lightning-fast Optimus GX Pro 8100 2TB NVMe SSD is 21% off and $0.18 cents per GB – $349 for a PCIe 5.0 M.2 SSD is about as good as it gets for Black Friday
articles.text:
SanDisk’s lightning-fast Optimus GX Pro 8100 2TB NVMe SSD is 21% off and $0.18 cents per GB – $349 for a PCIe 5.0 M.2 SSD is about as good as it gets for Black Friday
Expand your storage with this speedy Sandisk 2TB PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSD that’s only $0.18-cents per GB
Black Friday is in full swing, and there are deals on just about everything you can imagine. We’ve already seen some stellar storage deals and want to share one of the best we’ve found. SanDisk’s WD Black SN8100 clone, the 2TB Optimus GX Pro 8100 PCIe 5.0 SSD, is on sale for almost $95 off its typical price and at an all-time low, according to Amazon. For $349, you can get one of the faster 2TB drives. At less than $ 0.18 per GB, it’s one of the least expensive 2TB PCIe 5.0 drives available right now.
The GX Pro 8100 uses a Silicon Motion SM2508 PCIe 5.0 x4 controller found on other ‘budget’ high-end PCIe 5.0 drives. The SM2508 focuses a bit more on efficiency, keeping thermals well managed, but is still fast for a PCIe 5.0 drive. It also includes 2GB of DDR4-3200 cache for improved burst and sustained speeds. The storage chips are Kioxia BiCS8 218-layer TLC 3D CBA NAND, also found in the WD Black SN8100. Together, these reach speeds up to 14,900/14,000 MB/s (read/writes), nearly saturating PCIe 5.0 bandwidth. IOPS are listed up to 2.3/2.4M random r/w.
All-time low price.
Expand your internal storage with Sandisk's 2TB Optimus GX Pro 8100 PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSD. This speedy drive offers 14,900/14,000 r/w speeds and has a 5-year warranty.
SanDisk offers a long 5-year limited warranty in the U.S and the drive is rated up to 1,200 TBW, which is quite common for top-tier PCIe 5.0 drives. In other words, you’ll have to work incredibly hard to burn through all the write cycles, especially within the warranty period.
Whether you use it as your primary OS drive or to store your most frequently accessed games, the SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 2TB is an excellent option for a new PC or even upgrading your current storage. At an all-time low price of $349.99 and $0.18 per GB, it’s not only fast (faster than the Samsung 9100 Pro), but the price is right, too.

articles.title: MrBeast regalará 100 autos en una transmisión en vivo: fecha y hora
articles.text:
MrBeast regalará 100 autos este domingo 29 de noviembre de 2026 durante una transmisión en vivo, según anunció el creador de contenido en X
El evento comenzará a las 2 p. m., hora del este de Estados Unidos, y estará disponible a través de Whatnot. “¡Acabo de comprar 100 autos y este domingo los regalaré todos GRATIS en una transmisión en vivo de Whatnot!”, publicó.
El anuncio estuvo acompañado por una imagen en la que MrBeast aparece frente a varios vehículos reunidos en un espacio cerrado.
Cuándo será el evento de MrBeast
La transmisión será el domingo 29 de noviembre a las 2 p. m. en la costa este de Estados Unidos.
En México, el vivo comenzará a la 1 p. m. En Perú y Colombia, iniciará a las 12 p. m. En Argentina, la transmisión comenzará a las 2 p. m., mientras que en España será a las 20.00. Para participar, MrBeast indicó que los usuarios deben descargar la aplicación mencionada y conectarse al vivo.
Qué autos dará MrBeast
MrBeast no detalló las marcas ni los modelos de los 100 vehículos que regalará durante la transmisión.
En la fotografía difundida por el creador se observan autos de distintos tamaños y colores, además de camionetas y vehículos recreativos.
La imagen muestra parte de los vehículos estacionados en un recinto iluminado, donde también aparece un auto deportivo rojo elevado sobre una plataforma.
MrBeast abre convocatoria para trabajar en su equipo
MrBeast abrió una convocatoria para sumar creativos especializados en YouTube Shorts a su equipo de producción.
La búsqueda apunta a personas capaces de idear, grabar y desarrollar videos verticales con una mirada propia, aunque alineada con el estilo del creador estadounidense.
El puesto, denominado YouTube Shorts Creatives, incluye tareas de planificación, filmación, publicación y análisis de contenidos. La empresa no detalló la remuneración y solo indicó que ofrece un salario competitivo.
No exige currículum ni carta de presentación como requisito obligatorio, ya que busca evaluar el criterio creativo y la capacidad de analizar videos.
Para postularse, los interesados deben completar un formulario con datos personales, país, ciudad, teléfono y correo electrónico. De manera opcional, pueden adjuntar enlaces a perfiles de LinkedIn, portafolios, sitios web, reels o canales de YouTube. También existe la posibilidad de incluir un currículum.
Luego de enviar la solicitud, los candidatos reciben dos preguntas por correo electrónico y un enlace para cargar una respuesta audiovisual. El video debe durar cinco minutos o menos y debe grabarse sin leer un guion. La compañía aclaró que no evaluará la calidad técnica de la producción, la edición ni la presencia frente a cámara.
El desafío principal consiste en elegir algunos Shorts de MrBeast, explicar qué elementos funcionaron en esos videos y proponer cambios. Las respuestas deben enviarse mediante un enlace no listado de YouTube o a través de Loom. Donaldson aseguró que ya contrató a cinco personas mediante procesos similares.
MrBeast dará asesoría financiera a creadores de contenido
Una alianza entre Mastercard y Beast Industries, la empresa fundada por MrBeast, tendrá a MrBeast como figura central y pondrá a disposición de creadores de contenido y consumidores interesados herramientas, experiencias y formación para transformar ideas digitales en proyectos propios.
Programas de tarjetas de marca compartida, beneficios exclusivos y recursos destinados a la educación financiera forman parte de la iniciativa.
La meta consiste en brindar a quienes cuentan con presencia en redes sociales instrumentos para convertir su alcance e influencia en oportunidades económicas concretas, desarrollar negocios y reforzar sus conocimientos financieros.
Inicialmente vinculada a los videos de YouTube de MrBeast, Beast Industries extendió sus actividades a sectores como los medios, los productos de consumo, las plataformas tecnológicas y los servicios móviles y financieros.
Esa expansión incluye la colaboración con Mastercard, que pretende llevar la marca del creador a nuevas experiencias para su comunidad.
Según sostuvo Jeff Housenbold, director ejecutivo de Beast Industries, la compañía apunta a innovar y a ayudar a las personas a adquirir habilidades prácticas, ganar confianza y concretar proyectos que puedan parecer difíciles de llevar adelante.

articles.title: Linux Mint 27 está a caminho e estas são as novidades
articles.text:
Linux Mint 27 está a caminho e estas são as novidades
Distribuição Linux Mint 27 "Adrien" beta já está disponível, trazendo suporte prolongado (LTS) até 2031 e kernel 7.0.
Você já pode testar a nova versão de uma das distribuições Linux mais amigáveis da atualidade: o pacote beta do Linux Mint 27 “Adrien” foi liberado para download. A novidade tem o ambiente de desktop Cinnamon 6.8 com suporte completo ao Wayland como destaque, mas há mais atributos interessantes.
Antes de irmos ao que há de novo, convém deixar claro que esta é uma versão com suporte prolongado (LTS) e que, por isso, receberá atualizações pelo menos até 2031. Vale destacar também que a novidade é baseada no Ubuntu 26.04 LTS e vem com o kernel Linux 7.0.
O Cinnamon 6.8 foi introduzido neste mês de novembro e se destaca por trazer aprimoramentos nos gestos de touchpad e de tela sensível ao toque, além de avanços no gerenciamento de conexões de rede, tudo isso sem abrir mão de sua interface leve e intuitiva.
Outro avanço notável é que, nesta versão, o ambiente de desktop passa a ter suporte completo ao Wayland, o moderno servidor gráfico que vem substituindo o tradicional X11 em diversas distribuições, como Ubuntu e Fedora.
Note, porém, que o X11 ainda é padrão no Linux Mint 27 beta. O Wayland deve ser ativado pelo usuário.
O Linux Mint 27 beta também traz novos aplicativos nativos como parte do projeto XApps, que visa disponibilizar ferramentas que funcionem independentemente do ambiente gráfico escolhido pelo usuário. Os destaques são estes:
- Clockenstein: app de calendário, suportando tanto agendas locais quanto integração com o Google Calendar e serviços compatíveis com CalDAV;
- Superlight: monitora o sistema para exibir o status de recursos como CPU, GPU, memória RAM, temperaturas, rede e armazenamento;
- Velocitty: é uma ferramenta de terminal com suporte a múltiplas abas, paletas de cores, SSH e execução automática de comandos na inicialização;
- Unfold: é um gerenciador de arquivos compactados leve e compatível com vários formatos, como RAR;
- Xepub: permite ler e-books no formato EPUB, suportando recursos como marcações, anotações e tradução de palavras.
O Linux Mint está há algum tempo com o recurso de hibernação desativado por padrão. Isso porque essa funcionalidade foi desabilitada no Ubuntu, distribuição que é a base do projeto, vale relembrar. A boa notícia é que a versão 27 marca o retorno da opção de hibernar.
Vale deixar claro que a hibernação é diferente da suspensão, pois salva a sessão em uma área do SSD / HD e desliga o computador. Já a suspensão faz a máquina entrar em baixo consumo de energia, mas sob o risco de a carga de bateria acabar se esse modo for mantido por muito tempo.
Mas os próprios desenvolvedores do Linux Mint alertam que o retorno do computador da hibernação pode ser lento e que esse modo exige uma boa quantidade de espaço livre de armazenamento (swap) para funcionar.
Há vários outros atributos no Linux Mint 27, entre eles:
- Nemo: o gerenciador de arquivos agora conta com um painel que permite ao usuário conferir o conteúdo de áudios, imagens e vídeos sem precisar abri-los;
- Screenshot: a ferramenta de captura de tela foi reescrita, permitindo registrar janelas com ou sem sombras, por exemplo;
- Papéis de parede: agora é possível definir um wallpaper diferente para cada monitor;
- Notificações: o usuário pode ativar ou desativar notificações individualmente para cada aplicativo.
Você pode baixar a imagem ISO do Linux Mint 27 “Adrien” em um dos links da página de anúncio da versão beta. Depois, use uma ferramenta como o Rufus para criar um pendrive de instalação ou de teste (modo “live”).
Ali, você pode escolher versões com o ambiente Cinnamon retratado aqui, com Xfce ou com MATE.
O site OMG! Ubuntu faz um alerta importante: a distribuição conta com um novo instalador que não oferece configuração simplificada de dual boot com Windows ou outra distribuição. Para isso, é necessário fazer particionamento manual.
Leve em consideração também que estamos falando de uma versão beta, que está mais sujeita a falhas ou instabilidades, portanto. Nesse sentido, a dica é baixá-la somente para testes, não para usá-la como sistema principal.
O lançamento da versão estável do Linux Mint 27 é esperado para o fim de 2026 ou início de 2027.

I tested 6 AI mini PCs from GMKtec, Geekom, Minisforum, and MSI for local LLMs — here's what to buy for Black Friday
Only a select few mini PCs can run offline LLMs to a useful standard
AI mini PCs are here - and in a big way. For Black Friday, plenty of these local LLM machines have got discounts. In the last year, I’ve seen a dramatic difference in the abilities of the mini PCs that have arrived on my desk. For a start, many are getting a little less mini, both in size and performance, but the real change is what these machines can now do.
In the past, I’ve run benchmarks and real-world application tests and recorded the performance results. It’s all been very linear. However, with the machines I’ve selected here, each can be put to work using local LLMs and app integrations to perform real tasks such as file sorting, creating websites, and document analysis.
I’ve picked the best mini PCs I've reviewed for running AI workloads, from GMKtec, Geekom, MSI, and Minisforum. And for more savings on computing, we're live-tracking all the best Black Friday mini PC deals.
My top AI mini picks
The EVO-X3 was one of the first Strix Halo machines I looked at, and my first realisation was that these AI-enhanced mini PCs didn’t just increase processing power, but also what was possible. Through LM Studio, I got my first real taste of running a local LLM properly.

It's not in the deal, but worth paying full price.

UK price: now £1215 (now £1349)
Read moreRead less▼
Which one should you buy?
This list features the mini PCs I’ve looked at this year and would recommend to anyone looking to run local LLMs. While there are limits due to RAM for some of these machines, LLMs and model managers are adapting, and the potential, along with upgrade options, makes all of these sound choices.
✅ Buy the GMKtec EVO-X5 Pro if… Money is no object, and you want the best machine for running local LLMs right now.
✅ Buy the GMKtec EVO-X3 if… You want a system that you can easily expand. The slim profile, ease of use, and price make this a powerful option.
✅ Buy the MSI PRO MAX EDGE AI+ 11M if… You want a solid mini workstation with plenty of AI potential to aid your work.
✅ Buy the VZMORE AX9 Max AI if… Experimenting with the potential of AI and its integration with apps interests you, and you’re working on a budget.
✅ Buy the GEEKOM A9 Max (2026 Edition) if… You want to run a local LLM but also need a solid machine for everyday admin and creative work.
✅ Buy the Minisforum MS-S1 Max if… You’re looking for a real bargain. Having launched over a year ago, the current pricing makes this a relatively affordable premium option.
Why I recommend them
As one of the machines awarded a Highly Recommended award, the GMKtec EVO-X3 showed what local AI can mean. In the review, I commented: “The EVO-X3 is impressive and shows the full potential of local AI.”
At the same time, this wasn’t the first machine with this potential. After a year of testing an increasing number of these AI-enhanced machines, I was starting to get a flavour of exactly what was possible.
The EVO-X3, along with the newer EVO-X5 Pro, MSI PRO MAX EDGE AI+ and Minisforum MS-S1 Max, are all at the upper end of the AI mini PC market, and these machines really highlight the potential of running local AI models.
Over the last few months, that potential has helped me sort through thousands of images, cataloguing and organising them in an easy-to-archive format. Over the next year, I have further administrative tasks that would have taken me months to complete, and while they aren't quick, I can leave these machines to do the grunt work.
At their present prices, these machines are out of reach for most of us, even with the Black Friday deals. However, there are cheaper options.
The current cost of memory doesn’t help the pricing, but the GEEKOM A9 Max (2026) and VZMORE AX9 Max AI can both handle impressive processing out of the box and give you a taste of the potential.
2027 will inevitably bring another leap in performance for running these local models, but for now, these machines offer some of the best options for performance and potential Black Friday savings.

articles.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
articles.text:
Details have emerged about a new zero-day vulnerability in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution.
The proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, which has yet to be assigned a CVE identifier, has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT.
"I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests," a security researcher who goes by the online alias "ek0ms savi0r" said. "No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface."
The shortcoming affects Cacti Core 1.2.31, the latest version, when the guest account is enabled. It's worth noting that the guest account is disabled by default starting with Cacti version 0.8.7.
At a high level, the vulnerability allows an attacker to abuse the guest access to write an unvalidated value (i.e., non-numeric text) into a setting called "preview_graphs_per_page" via "auth_profile.php?action=update_data." The configuration parameter controls how many graphs are displayed per page when viewing graphs in Preview Mode.
The crafted value takes the form of arbitrary SQL strings that can be turned into a second-order SQL injection by taking advantage of the fact that Cacti does not validate that the user-provided input is actually an integer value. This, in turn, opens the door for arbitrary SQL query execution when the graph preview page ("graph_view.php") is loaded with default filters.
The SQL query demonstrated by "ek0ms savi0r" is an UPDATE statement to modify a record in Cacti's poller table. In the final stage of the attack, the realtime poller endpoint ("graph_realtime.php") is invoked from the same guest session, which causes the modified row from the poller table to be read and passed as input to PHP's popen() function without any allowlist or sanitization checks.
The researcher has pointed out four failures that ultimately make it possible to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution -
- The guest can write a numeric setting as an arbitrary string
- The stored default bypasses request validation
- Cacti's PHP PDO database driver accepts stacked statements through the SQL LIMIT clause
- The poller executes a database-stored command string
Successful exploitation of the flaw can allow an attacker to compromise the Cacti server and provide a pivot point to the target network as it exposes sensitive data, or even suppress alerts by modifying the poller table.
"Because Cacti often stores credentials and connection details for routers, switches, servers, and other devices across a network, an attacker who reaches this level of command execution can gain a foothold reaching far beyond the monitoring server itself," watchTowr said in an advisory.
In the absence of a fix, users are advised to disable the guest account and restrict access to the Cacti web interface to mitigate potential risks. It's also essential to review poller configuration entries for unexpected command values and apply the fixes as soon as they become available.
