articles.title: Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences
articles.text:
The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else.
Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”
Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”
Days later, the board gave the administration what it wanted. “It is my Great Honor to report that the United States of America now fully owns and controls 10% of INTEL,” Donald Trump posted to his social platform. “The United States paid nothing for these Shares, and the Shares are now valued at approximately $11 Billion Dollars. This is a great Deal for America.”
President Trump was similarly jubilant on Monday, announcing that he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board of directors to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang. The proclamation was a shock. But it wasn’t entirely without precedent.
Fifteen months earlier, the Trump administration had interfered with the leadership decisions at another major chipmaker, court documents allege. Then, as now, allegations swirled that the company’s CEO was too close to China. Then, as now, the Trump administration dealt itself into the company’s financial future.
It’s part of a broader shift within the government in general and the Commerce Department in particular, a former member of that department tells WIRED. Out are old metrics “like creating jobs or the US being more competitive or owning more of the market share,” this ex-Trump administration official says. When dealing with private companies, a single overriding concern is: “Are you going to give back to the government in cash?”
Documents unredacted as part of a shareholder’s lawsuit against Intel’s board show how far the administration has been willing to go to get what it wants. The lawsuit’s allegations were previously reported by WP Intelligence.
“The Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threats,” the lawsuit alleges, “caved to the government’s extortion.” A second case, asking for internal records, was filed in April by the same shareholder, Richard Paisner, against Nvidia.
“It’s just straight-up coercion,” says Scott Lincicome, a vice president at the libertarian Cato Institute. “The company starts making decisions not based on what’s best for the company in the short or long term, what’s best for shareholders, but what’s best for politics and what the government is demanding.”
“That’s not what you want from any company,” he adds. “When you’re talking about the world’s most innovative companies and these kinds of bleeding-edge technologies that have not only huge economic implications but national security ones, then that’s a huge problem.”
Representatives for Intel declined to comment for this story. The White House, Commerce Department, and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.
The parallels between Nvidia’s government-assisted autogolpe and Intel’s alleged forced sale aren’t exact. In the Intel case, Trump all but accused the company’s boss of being compromised by Beijing; in the Nvidia situation, the president reportedly dismissed concerns from his own intelligence agencies about the executive’s connections to China. But both instances show a growing fusion of private enterprise and public office.
During the Biden administration, Intel won awards for up to $11 billion in government grants and contracts, much of it under the CHIPS Act, which was meant to help build semiconductor manufacturing and assembly plants in America and bolster domestic research.
At the time, there was some grumbling inside the Commerce Department, which administered the CHIPS and Science Act grants, about funding what was seen as a “failing incumbent” in the semiconductor space, says the former official. (Intel had, in recent years, fallen on hard times.) But by March 2025, Intel had received about $2.2 billion of the grants. That’s when President Trump told Congress that the CHIPS Act was “a horrible, horrible thing.” The rest of Intel’s money was put on hold, tied to hitting certain milestones, while the administration said it was renegotiating the deals.
The same month Lip-Bu Tan was hired as Intel’s new CEO. Soon after, his ties to China made him a Trump target, when Reuters reported that Tan had invested in “hundreds of Chinese tech firms,” some with connections to Beijing’s military. Tan’s former firm, Cadence Design Systems, pleaded guilty to violating US sanctions by selling semiconductor designs to a restricted Chinese military university, and agreed to pay more than $140 million in fines. Tan was never personally charged, but the violations happened while he was the CEO.
Two weeks later, the president was watching Maria Bartiromo’s show on the Fox Business Network. It mentioned a letter a senator had sent Intel about the China ties. Trump posted, “The CEO of INTEL is highly CONFLICTED and must resign, immediately. There is no other solution to this problem.”
Tan went to the Oval Office on August 11 to see if there was, in fact, another solution. He got 40 minutes with the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
Tan claimed his experience in China was a strength, not a detriment. According to the book Regime Change, Tan argued that there was no way he could’ve known about every one of the deals his many companies made; Trump, who had his own sprawling business empire, surely knew what that was like. Tan promised to give up his holdings in China, according to a letter Tan shared with Intel’s board, and put any proceeds into a blind trust.
“The primary goal was to eliminate any worries about Lip-Bu himself, his Cadence background, and his investments with China,” according to a source with knowledge of the matter. But there were major financial concerns for Intel, too. “We had declining revenues and needed money.”
Neither Tan’s letter, excerpted in the complaint, nor Trump’s social media posts praising the CEO after the meeting mentioned anything about giving the government a chunk of the company. Yet Trump later insisted that a deal had been cooked up right then and there. “He came in, he saw me, we talked for a while. I liked him a lot, I thought he was very good,” the president told The Wall Street Journal. “I said, ‘You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel.’ And he said, ‘I would consider that.’”
“I should’ve asked for more. It was so easy,” Trump later recalled.
According to the court filing’s review of Intel’s internal documents, Shapiro—a former partner at the New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz—made a verbal offer on August 18. Ultimately, in exchange for the cut of Intel, the Trump administration would free up the $8.9 billion US government grants that it had already won. They wanted about a tenth of the company’s stock for free, in exchange for Washington keeping the commitment it had already made.
Then came the call in which Shapiro insisted there was no room for negotiation. “The board needs to consider,” he said, according to Intel’s summary of his remarks included in the court documents, the “benefits of having a friend in this administration and what the administration can do to help Intel (including with customers).”
Intel’s board met, and decided they hated the deal. “The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the company,” minutes of the meeting, reprinted in the lawsuit, noted.
But they went ahead with it anyway. Paisner’s lawyers say in the court documents the board took the offer thrust forward by the administration. Intel’s attorneys disagree, arguing in their motion to dismiss that there was some back-and-forth deal-making, and it made the agreement more favorable to the company. The grants became “immediately available” while “strategically aligning the interests of Intel’s stockholders and the US Government.”
On August 25, Lutnick released a video with Tan, sitting side-by-side on cushioned chairs. “I really look forward to have the US government be my shareholder,” Tan turned to Lutnick and said. “And we can work together and make Intel great again.”
Inside the company, the video was “a surprise to everyone,” according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter. Some employees joked that it was reminiscent of a “hostage video.”
Not long after that, Nvidia—led by Tan’s friend Jensen Huang—made a $5 billion investment in Intel. “I love seeing their stock price go up, making the USA RICHER, AND RICHER,” Trump posted. “Who would not want to make deals like that?”
Deals, plural. On the day Tan was hauled to the Oval Office, Trump announced that his administration had been negotiating separately with Huang. The Nvidia leader was beyond eager to sell more of his semiconductors to China. “And I said, if I’m going to do that, I want you to pay us as a country something,’” Trump said. They settled on 15 percent of all sales of the H20 model chip. Months after that, they cut a second deal: a 25 percent bounty on sales of Nvidia’s even-more advanced H200 chips.
In their lawsuit against Nvidia, Paisner’s attorneys argue the surcharges amount to “unlawful taxes,” and that the board’s “decisions to enter into such agreements are the product of mismanagement and breaches of fiduciary duty.”
In court, NVIDIA’s lawyers insisted that the company “did not enter into any illegal ‘agreement’ with the government but instead engaged with the government and stated that it would comply with federal regulations.” Moreover, the attorneys say Paisner is trying to make a political point, rather than a legal one. “When asked about his purpose in bringing this action,” they write, “Paisner was candid: ‘It’s to make a public point of how NVIDIA conducts itself.’”
The attorneys wrote this in May, months before Nvidia’s and Huang’s recent drama. Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said on the company’s quarterly earnings call that it did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” citing his “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” (Not to mention mounting evidence that the company’s most sophisticated chips were making their way to China, in violation of US law.) But, according to The New York Times, after days of pressure from top administration officials, the company and the government essentially struck a deal Sunday night to reinstate Huang.
“Don’t think for a second that politics ever play a role in this company, not even a little bit,” Huang said during his first company-wide meeting after rejoining the company, WIRED reported. “We are the most apolitical company. I don’t love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”

articles.title: Looking to shake up your home office? This electric standing desk from Cubiker is down to just $79.99 at Amazon for Black Friday
articles.text:
Looking to shake up your home office? This electric standing desk from Cubiker is down to just $79.99 at Amazon for Black Friday
Alternating between sitting and standing has never been so cheap thanks to Black Friday - this Cubiker 48-inch electric desk is currently discounted
You don’t have to spend a fortune to get a comfortable and flexible home office setup, especially with Black Friday around - because this Cubiker electric standing desk has been reduced from $89.99 to $75.99 on Amazon.
Today’s best Cubiker standing desk deal
The 48 x 24-inch model features a white steel frame, maple-effect desktop, and electric height adjustment. It’s got three memory presets and is tested for up to 100,000 lift cycles.
Why we recommend the Cubiker standing desk
The Cubiker’s electric motor adjusts the desktop height between 28.3 and 46.5 inches, and it’s got three programmable height presets for switching positions at the touch of a button.
That’s useful if you regularly alternate between sitting and standing, or share a workspace with someone who prefers a different desk height.
The 48-inch surface means you’ve got plenty of room for a laptop, monitor, keyboard, mouse, and everyday office accessories, while the steel frame supports up to 176lbs. A straightforward control panel and relatively compact footprint also make it a practical option for smaller home offices. It’s rated for 100,000 lift cycles, and the motor operates at less than 45 dB, so you won’t be disturbed by lots of noise.
Amazon customers have given the Cubiker desk an impressive 4.6 out of five stars across more than 4,500 ratings.
At this price, though, some compromises are inevitable. The desktop is made from joined sections of material rather than one solid board. Over time, that means that the desk may develop weaker joints, and you may notice visible seams. Also note that the 176 lb weight capacity makes it less suitable for particularly heavy workstation setups.
Price context and historical value
At $75.99, you're saving $14 against the usual $89.99 price. That’s a 16% discount. Amazon also lists a variety of other Cubiker designs with varying levels of discount, too, so browse around if this particular model isn’t suited to your needs.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy it if... you want an affordable electric standing desk that’s ideal for everyday home working and shared working spaces.
❌ Skip it if... you need a sturdy desk for heavy equipment or a wider desk that can easily accommodate several monitors.

articles.title: Firefox va bientôt vous imposer sa nouvelle interface sans possibilité de revenir à l'ancienne
articles.text:
Mozilla a récemment introduit une nouvelle interface pour Firefox et prochainement, vous n’aurez plus d’autre choix que de l’utiliser. Le réglage caché qui permet de retrouver l’ancien agencement de Firefox va disparaître. Malgré les critiques, Mozilla maintient son nouveau design et propose quelques options pour l’ajuster.
À partir de Firefox 162, attendu le 8 décembre, ceux qui ont désactivé l’interface Nova auront une petite surprise puisque cette dernière reviendra par défaut. L’annonce publiée sur le forum Mozilla Connect a déjà suscité plusieurs centaines de réponses.
Thèmes unis, mode compact, forks : les options si Nova vous déplaît
Nous rapportions en septembre que Firefox 157 inaugurait Nova et ses coins arrondis, avec toutefois la possibilité de revenir en arrière sur l’ancienne version. Pour le moment, il suffit d’ouvrir about:config, la page des réglages avancés, et de passer la ligne browser.nova.enabled sur false. Le déploiement étant terminé, Mozilla va verrouiller cette option et explique vouloir éviter des comportements inattendus. Les mécontents reprochent à Nova ses formes trop arrondies, ses espacements plus larges et une personnalisation réduite.
Mozilla a tout de même ajouté des thèmes aux couleurs unies, sans dégradés, dans la rubrique « Classic Themes » de la page about:addons. On y trouve un gris imitant Proton, l’ancien design, ainsi qu’un thème Firefox OLED. Le panneau de personnalisation du nouvel onglet comporte également un sélecteur. La disposition, les formes et les espacements d’avant ne reviennent pas pour autant. Ce sont pourtant les coins arrondis qui ont largement été pointés par la communauté. Pour gagner de la place, le mode compact, désormais pleinement pris en charge, s’active dans les paramètres, sous Apparence. Avec Firefox 161, les onglets verticaux, rangés sur le côté de la fenêtre, suivent ce réglage. Avec cet affichage, le trait horizontal des onglets conteneurs laisse de nouveau place à un repère sur le côté. Pour rappel, ces onglets cloisonnent les cookies et les connexions, par exemple entre vos activités professionnelles et vos achats.
- Gratuit et open source
- Protection renforcée contre le pistage
- Nombreuses extensions et personnalisations
Nous rapportions cette semaine que Firefox 161 permet d’activer son VPN intégré site par site. S’y ajoutent un « Fire Button » pour effacer tout ou partie des données de navigation, la saisie automatique du code de sécurité des cartes bancaires, l’accès aux groupes d’onglets enregistrés depuis le menu et un raccourci personnalisable pour copier l’adresse d’une page. L’import de l’historique Chrome est amélioré et des bugs sont corrigés (restauration de session, plein écran sous Windows, blocages de Spotlight sur macOS, appels vidéo en basse résolution).
Pour contourner Nova, il est possible de modifier userChrome.css, un fichier qui personnalise l’apparence du navigateur. La manipulation atténue les arrondis, mais demande des connaissances techniques et peut cesser de fonctionner après une mise à jour. Il y a également la version ESR, à support prolongé, qui permet d'échapper à Nova jusqu'en septembre prochain, mais celle-ci n’intègre pas les nouvelles fonctionnalités. Enfin, il est également possible d’opter pour un fork comme LibreWolf, Waterfox ou Zen.

articles.title: Cette barre de son Samsung notée 5/5 tombe à 800 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La barre de son Samsung HW-Q990H "5 étoiles" à 800,00 €
Actuellement notée 5/5 par notre rédaction, la Samsung HW-Q990H délivre un rendu sonore puissant et équilibré avec des effets surround précis. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 800,00 € chez Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 8 % et 71,27 € d'économie.
La Samsung HW-Q990H reprend les bases de la formule home cinema sans-fil du constructeur sud-coréen en y ajoutant quelques ajustements logiciels. Ce système complet vise une spatialisation poussée dans le salon avec des enceintes arrière et un caisson sans-fil. L'ensemble avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de ses séances d'écoute.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la barre de son descend à 800,00 € chez Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit environ 8 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours fixé à 871,27 €. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 71,27 €.
Une immersion 11.1.4 canaux pour le cinéma à domicile
Ce système audio s'appuie sur une configuration complète à 11.1.4 canaux pour envelopper la pièce d'écoute. Comme l'explique notre test complet, les 23 haut-parleurs répartis entre la barre, les deux satellites arrière et le caisson de basses créent une scène sonore vaste et dynamique. Le traitement audio assure des effets surround précis et des dialogues parfaitement intelligibles, même au cœur des scènes d'action les plus denses.
Samsung HW-Q990H
Points forts
- Sonorité puissante et équilibrée.
- Effets surround immersifs et précis.
- Caisson de basses compact, puissant et réactif.
- Dialogues clairs et intelligibles.
- Prise en charge des flux 4K/120 Hz et VRR.
- Bonne qualité de construction.
Points faibles
- Effets Atmos qui manquent un poil de hauteur.
- Petit afficheur.
- Nouveautés 2026 anecdotiques.
Connectique moderne et gestion des flux vidéo récents
La connectique HDMI prend en charge les flux vidéo 4K/120 Hz ainsi que le VRR, ce qui permet de relier directement des consoles de jeu récentes sans sacrifier la fluidité de l'affichage. L'écoute musicale reste équilibrée, avec un caisson de basses réactif qui apporte l'assise nécessaire sans traîner. Le laboratoire a relevé un afficheur en façade assez étroit et des effets de hauteur Dolby Atmos légèrement en retrait, des détails qui n'entraveront pas l'usage des amateurs de grand spectacle sonore.
Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus : l'autre option face au Samsung HW-Q990H
La Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus mise sur une approche monobloc sans enceintes arrière séparées, pensée pour limiter l'encombrement dans la pièce. Elle délivre un son précis et musical tout en intégrant une spatialisation virtuelle performante.
Le modèle de Sennheiser coûte 10,00 € de moins que l'ensemble Samsung au prix du jour. Face à la Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus qui privilégie la compacité, le système Samsung HW-Q990H conserve un net avantage sur l'immersion grâce à ses véritables satellites arrière et à son caisson dédié.
Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus
Points forts
- Rendu sonore équilibré, riche et d’une précision admirable.
- Effets Atmos et surround bluffant de réalisme.
- Calibration acoustique efficace.
- Connectique et connectivité complètes.
- Compatible avec de nombreux formats sonores 3D (Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, MPEG-H, 360 Reality Audio…).
- Très bon niveau de finition.
Points faibles
- Latence conséquente en communication Bluetooth.
- Pas de prise en charge des flux 120 Hz et VRR.
- Une interface TV aurait été le nec plus ultra.

articles.title: The Swiss Army knife of DVD drives is back on sale, USB docking hybrid also available with a built-in M.2 SSD slot or SATA hard drive dock — $28 for the DVD writer and hub, $37 gets an added SATA dock, or pay $39 for the M.2 version
articles.text:
The Swiss Army knife of DVD drives is back on sale, USB docking hybrid also available with a built-in M.2 SSD slot or SATA hard drive dock — $28 for the DVD writer and hub, $37 gets an added SATA dock, or pay $39 for the M.2 version
Several essential peripherals-in-1 for media hoarders, with all models offering 20% off.
Now with M.2 NVMe SSD dock!
The most expensive of the bunch, this optical CD/DVD writer from SUIDEK upgrades the SATA dock to an M.2 NVMe SSD dock, but keeps the SD card reader, USB-A, and USB-C hub.
Desktops and laptops are almost certain to omit an optical drive in 2026. So, keeping a USB optical drive and docking solution around is a great idea to retain access to your collection of old software and media for generations to come. With the obvious utility value of one of these USB-attached optical drives we've selected a few flexible solutions on sale at Amazon that we felt we just had to share as they feature in the Black Friday sales: 
The External CD/DVD Drive for Laptop, DVD Player for Laptop, 8 in 1 USB 3.0 Ultra-Slim Portable at $28.79.
The External CD DVD Drive, Portable CD DVD Driver +/-RW Burner with 2.5-inch SATA, SD Card Reader and USB A Type C 2.0 Hub at just $37.59. This model adds the convenience of a SATA drive dock to the equation. 
There's also an External SUIDEK portable CD/DVD burner with USB hub and M.2 NVMe Dock for $39.99; this model swaps the SATA dock for an M.2 NVMe SSD dock, if you prefer.
- Check out the SUIDEK portable CD/DVD burner with USB hub and M.2 Dock
- Check out the SUIDEK External CD DVD Drive, USB 3.0 USB-C Portable CD DVD Drive for PC
- Check out the SUIDEK External CD/DVD DVD +/-RW Burner, Card Reader, and USB Hub
The cheapest SUIDECK drive offers you the core of optical drive functionality plus a handful of media connectivity options. This attractive portable device, with a silver metallic and black honeycomb finish, can read and write optical media at CD 24X and DVD 8X speeds. That's not all, as it also offers a USB 3.0 hub, 3x USB 2.0 ports, 1x USB 3.0 port, SD and TF card slot readers, and a USB-C port.
The compatibility of the SUIDEK External CD DVD Drive, USB 3.0 USB-C Portable CD DVD Drive for PC is also extensive. You can freely use CD±R/RW, CD-ROM, DVD±R/RW, DVD-RAM, VCD, and SVCD optical discs, the listing claims. Meanwhile, you can plug this into Windows 11, 10, 8, 7, XP, Vista, Linux, and macOS 10.6 or above, computers.
It was already cheap!
SUIDECK's portable USB connected optical and media reader peripheral also has USB HUB functionality. This has you covered for all sorts of old CDs, DVDs, and flash cards you might have in the back of your tech cabinets.
If SATA docking functionality is attractive to you, then you might want to look more closely at this next SUIDECK optical drive and dock. For $37.59, you will have a single portable device that can be used to read and write optical media at CD 24X and DVD 8X speeds. Again, there's a basic USB hub built in with 2x USB 2.0 ports, a USB-C port, plus SD and TF card readers. The literal cherry on top of this design, though, is the SATA 2.5-inch slot on top, which can be used for quick access to your old laptop hard drives or SSDs. I have several of these in my drawers, so having easy USB dock access is handy.
Windows 11, 10, 8, 7, XP, Vista, Linux, macOS 10.6 or above, are again the OSes supported.
A Swiss Army knife of media access?

articles.title: Plots de chantier, jets d’œufs : pas encore arrivés chez nous, les robotaxis ont la vie dure
articles.text:
Les robotaxis de Waymo circulent à Denver depuis le 1er septembre, avec plus de 100 voitures réparties sur environ 155 km² d’aire de service. Depuis, l’entreprise a comptabilisé au moins 30 attaques à l’œuf contre ses véhicules, toutes attribuées au même homme, et en a signalé sept à la police. Le parquet a refusé d’engager des poursuites pénales et renvoie le dossier au civil, sans autre suite à ce stade.
Une parade connue depuis San Francisco
Un rapport de police d’octobre décrit des plots de chantier disposés autour d’un robotaxi, de quoi immobiliser une voiture programmée pour ne rien heurter. La méthode a un précédent daté : à l’été 2023, les militants du collectif Safe Street Rebel, à San Francisco, neutralisaient déjà les Waymo d’un simple cône posé sur le capot. Le suspect de Denver ajoute les œufs : chaque voiture maculée repart en nettoyage, environ 2 000 dollars la séance, sans dégât permanent constaté. Le même rapport évoque un homme quittant les lieux au volant d’une Corolla grise.
La mairie, elle, défend son expérience : le maire vante des robotaxis « populaires et abordables ». L’entreprise revendique de son côté des centaines de milliers de courses par semaine à l’échelle des États-Unis, et Denver compte parmi ses terrains les plus récents. Depuis la mi-novembre, le régulateur californien lui interdit par ailleurs les autoroutes de l’État, et Waymo a suspendu ce type de trajets dans tout le pays.
Une « affaire civile », et une Europe toujours à quai
Le procureur a écarté le pénal : le contentieux entre Waymo et son assaillant relève pour lui d’« une affaire civile ». La ville n’a guère plus de prise, la loi du Colorado réservant à l’État l’essentiel de la régulation des véhicules autonomes. Reste la voie du procès civil, pour un préjudice qui se résume à ce jour à des frais de nettoyage. Sept signalements, zéro mise en accusation : le différend glisse vers le terrain des dommages et intérêts.
Rien de tout cela ne se joue encore sur une chaussée française. Waymo fait rouler ses voitures à Londres depuis décembre 2025 et y vise un lancement commercial au quatrième trimestre 2026. Les essais y ont commencé avec des superviseurs à bord, étape imposée avant les courses sans conducteur. Munich doit suivre d’ici fin 2027, et Madrid s’ajoute à la carte depuis octobre, avec 16 voitures autorisées pour des essais et de premiers passagers visés en 2027. La France en est encore au stade administratif : une filiale Waymo France a été immatriculée à Paris fin juin, sans essai, sans partenaire et sans date annoncés.
Pour l’Europe, l’épisode vaut mode d’emploi autant qu’avertissement : un homme, des plots et quelques boîtes d’œufs suffisent à perturber une flotte entière, et la réponse judiciaire se cherche encore, même aux États-Unis. Les robotaxis doivent arriver en Europe par Londres puis Munich, au mieux fin 2026 pour l’une, fin 2027 pour l’autre. D’ici là, les villes européennes ont sous les yeux un inventaire des frictions à prévoir, plots de chantier compris.

articles.title: Ontario man accidentally records himself stealing Ray-Ban Meta Glasses
articles.text:
Ontario police are searching for a man who accidentally recorded himself stealing a pair of Meta Ray-Ban Glasses.
On Thursday, South Simcoe Police took to social media to ask the public to identify a male suspect in a Cookstown eyewear store robbery on Nov. 11. According to police, the man brought a counterfeit pair of glasses to swap out with a genuine pair of Meta Ray-Bans. Once staff discovered the switch, they reviewed a device that had previously been paired with the smart glasses and found that the suspect had inadvertently recorded video of himself during the theft using the in-frame camera.
South Simcoe Police has since shared the video on its social media channels to see if members of the public can help identify the suspect. The organization is asking those with tips to contact either 705-436-2141 or 905-775-3311 with the reference occurrence number PW26000297.
All in all, it’s a pretty funny revelation in an otherwise serious situation. In general, there’s been a lot of valid privacy concerns related to Ray-Ban Meta Glasses for how they allow people to record others, especially women, without consent. This has led them to be dubbed “pervert glasses” by many. So, to see this thief inadvertently use the glasses for good — to catch himself in the act — is an absolute riot.

articles.title: Books, bikes, and The Burbs: These are Ars staff’s holiday gift picks for 2026
articles.text:
The holiday shopping season is upon us, and as is our custom, we’re here with a list of Ars staffers’ favorite recent purchases that could make good gifts. (Or maybe they might be a gift you get yourself!)
Rather than try to write a definitive “best gifts for your sister or brother” type of guide, we simply polled Ars staffers on stuff they’ve actually bought this year that they recommend. The thinking is that if we’re into it, hopefully some of you or your friends or family might be. As such, there’s no rhyme or reason to these selections, really; it’s just a list of stuff we bought that we’re happy about. It’s heavy on interesting books and cycling accessories, but there are some gadgets and the like in here, too.
For each gadget (or whatever else it might be), we have a brief description of how or why we’ve been using this particular thing and why we would recommend it. Our picks are ordered by price, from lowest to highest. Note, though, that the prices of these products are listed as they were when the list was written. Online retailers often adjust prices frequently, especially around Black Friday, so just a heads up: The price might be different by the time you read this.
Also, a callout to the Ars commentariat: If you have your own holiday buying recommendations, feel free to share them. We or some fellow readers might take your advice if you suggest something good! Happy holidays!
I understand the convenience and space-savings that e-readers bring. My 2011 Kindle Touch goes with me everywhere I carry my travel backpack, but I’m still a softy for physical books when I’m sitting at home on a lazy Sunday. What started as something of a fanfic send-up of LitRPGs has quickly blossomed into a massive sensation of a series filled with far more depth, heart, and character than the initial premise might indicate. Author Matt Dinniman has an accessible style that will grip any reader with a taste for whimsical adventure. Just be warned that if you leave the books under the tree, you might not see much of the recipient until New Year’s.
Two excellent books that help describe how the Internet’s undersea backbone became a globe-spanning reality were published in 2026. Together, they form a great gift pairing for anyone interested in how humanity first achieved near-instantaneous communication across the world’s oceans—and how the first trans-Atlantic telegraph cable paved the way for a global network of subsea data cables that now faces growing risks from geopolitical conflicts.
James Tabor’s Lightning Beneath the Sea dives into the astounding real-life story of how American entrepreneur Cyrus Field, lacking in expertise but driven by personal fervor, set out to achieve peace on Earth by laying a 2,000-mile telegraph cable made of copper across the Atlantic seafloor in 1866.
To pull off the feat, Field managed to convince some of the greatest innovators and scientific luminaries of his day, such as Samuel F.B. Morse, Lord Kelvin, and Michael Faraday, to join his venture. He also refitted the SS Great Eastern steamship, the largest passenger liner ship built to date, as a cable-laying vessel.
That first ocean-spanning telegraph cable gave rise to more such cables for transmitting messages around the world. Eventually copper gave way to a network of subsea fiber-optic cables that became the Internet’s undersea backbone, and the modern world also became interlinked with submarine power cables and underwater pipelines for carrying oil and gas.
But all that undersea infrastructure is now facing growing danger from the threat of deliberate sabotage, as described in Elisabeth Braw’s book Undersea War. Her book provides a sobering but enlightening look at why subsea cables and pipelines are becoming more tempting targets amid rising geopolitical tensions and conflicts—and how governments and companies are responding to recent cable-cutting incidents around the world.
It’s a little-remembered film for most people, but I absolutely love The Burbs. Sure, it’s more Halloween fare than Christmas, but last year I picked The Thing, so clearly “1980s movies for October” is my December viewing MO.
Starring Tom Hanks, Carrie Fisher, and Corey Feldman, this is a dry, hilarious send-up of suburban life with a horror-adjacent mystery that keeps you guessing. (It’s not scary, though.) I hardly ever hear anyone else talk about this movie, but I love it, and it only recently came out in 4K, so I’m taking this opportunity to shout it out.
If you’re a technically minded Ars reader looking for a nice book to snuggle down with over the holidays, David Woods’ How Apollo Flew to the Moon could be just the thing. (There’s also an audiobook version.) Woods has an accessible style that breaks down complex engineering challenges and their solutions into easily digestible chunks that clarify without oversimplifying. He uses that style to take readers on a detailed trip through the machinery of Project Apollo, from the launch facilities and Mission Control all the way to the specific mechanics of how to navigate to and land on the Moon—and, from there, how to return safely to Earth.
Ever wondered about the insane engineering that let the Saturn V’s first stage burn almost 15 tons of fuel every second as it powered the crew into orbit? Or how to pinpoint a spacecraft’s centimeter-precise distance from Earth on its way to the Moon? Or how Apollo crews tracked their own position with stellar navigation, using sextants and star sightings? Or what a REFSMMAT is, or how television transmissions from the Moon worked, or how they got those crazy lunar buggies onto the Moon’s surface? All these questions and more are given beautifully complete and technically satisfying answers, suitable for both the curious layperson and also the interested engineer. Grab this book and stun your family at Christmas with amazing Apollo trivia—as a bonus, you’ll have the knowledge to make your “We never landed on the Moon!” conspiracy theorist uncle so angry that he stops talking and watches football in grumpy silence! Everyone wins!
As someone who grew up in the classic era of 16-bit SNES RPGs, this 40th anniversary tribute to the series’ history is everything I could have ever wanted in a modern entry. I haven’t properly played through a Final Fantasy entry since the days of Final Fantasy X on PlayStation 2, but when friends kept nudging me that this was the perfect “Nick game,” I figured I should probably take a look. There’s a free six-hour demo available on supported platforms if you’re still on the fence about picking this one up, but don’t be surprised if you end up grabbing a copy for yourself.
For the past couple of years, I’ve been transforming my tiny office into a sanctuary in the evenings, since I do most of my writing (and gaming) in here then. It started with Govee Hexa panels, then came an RGB TV backlight, then colorful smart bulbs for the built-in light fixtures. I topped it off with the Star Light projector, which coats the ceiling in a soothing, ever-shifting, immersive stars-and-nebula effect.
It’s probably not for everybody, but my office is tiny, and I spend a lot of time here both for work and for fun. Tapping a button to completely shift the vibe is surprisingly effective at making it a room I don’t mind spending time in even after I’ve been working in it all day.
Easily my favorite impulse purchase of 2026, the FM-1 is a great gift for curious tinkerers and experienced musicians alike. At around $70 or less, you don’t have to break the bank to get fiddling. A perfectly decent stock synthesizer on its own, the real fun starts when you begin experimenting with the community firmware packages that transform the synth into anything from a multi-track groovebox to one of the more hilarious ways that I’ve ever tried to play Doom.
– Nick Indge
Under $300
Trek BellBeats digital bike bell and speaker – $125 One of the great things about cycling is the chance to be alone with my thoughts—just me and my bike. But that can be too much of a good thing on longer zone 2 rides and centuries. Sporting the size and shape of an old-school bicycle bell, the Trek BellBeats is a safer alternative to donning headphones while on the bike. BellBeats pair with your phone via Bluetooth and will play music at a volume loud enough to enjoy your tunes or hear navigation prompts, but they are not so loud that the music drowns out traffic (or the radar on your bike computer). They can be mounted on just about any non-aero handlebars, charge over USB-C, and offer up to six hours of playtime. And as a bonus, they double as a bicycle bell.
I use Bluetooth headphones most of the time, but frustratingly, they don’t work with voice chat on the PlayStation 5, and I needed a good-quality headset for my Friday night multiplayer gaming sessions.
I’ve always liked Fractal Design’s PC cases, so I decided to roll the dice on their affordable-for-the-quality, over-ear headphones. They support Bluetooth, but they also have a USB dongle, so they can be used for voice chat on game consoles, too.
I was surprised by how much I like them, and despite buying them just for the PS5, I’ve ended up using them in other contexts. Part of that is because they’re very comfortable, and the design avoids my glasses frames well.
I also like that, although they are gaming headphones with all the expected bells and whistles for that, they don’t have an over-the-top design.
If you’re in the market for mid-range wireless gaming headphones that look like something you could actually wear in public without embarrassment, these fit the bill so far.
– Samuel Axon
Povec C1 Performance Sunglasses – $250 Photochromic sunglasses are incredibly useful for outdoor workouts. Two of the most popular bike trails near me run through forest preserves, and the lighting changes steadily as the forest canopy closes in or spreads out. My default sunglasses are a cheap, $28 pair from Rockbros. Unlike other photochromic glasses, which change tints via a pokey chemical reaction, the Povec C1 uses a battery to switch between tints in a second. All the rider (or runner) needs to do is swipe the right temple and the lenses will darken or lighten almost instantaneously. The C1 charges via a small USB-C port, and the Povec claims 28 days of battery life with four hours of daily usage. I’ve used them off and on for about six weeks and have only had to charge them once.
The C1 comes in three frame colors and either Green Revo or Gold Revo glasses and is an excellent stocking stuffer for the runner, cyclist, or skier in your life.
– Eric Bangeman
$300 and over
Garmin Varia RCT715 radar camera tail light – $300 Last spring, a friend of mine was the victim of a hit-and-run while on a ride. Although she wasn’t seriously hurt, her brand-new bike was totaled. The driver got an unwelcome surprise a couple of days later when the police knocked on his front door and arrested him. My friend was riding with a Garmin Varia RCT715, a combination taillight and radar with a camera. The 1080p/30 fps camera captured the car’s license plate, making it possible for the police to identify the driver. More than 90 percent of my riding is on roads, and I don’t feel fully comfortable without my Varia. I have it paired with my Garmin Edge 1050 bike computer, but it will work with most other brands via ANT+. The Varia detects approaching vehicles at 140 meters, and I have it set to record video starting when a car is detected and for 30 seconds after it passes. Battery life is up to six hours, depending on whether the taillight is solid or flashing, and video is saved on a 16GB microSD memory card.
My YouTube algorithm has recently fed me videos of testers using an angle grinder to cut through decent bike locks in under a minute. I’ve never seen an angle grinder-assisted theft in person, but I’ve seen enough heaps of bike parts around town to know people’s rides are getting jacked somewhere. As someone known to be neurotic about leaving my bike outside my purview, I’m looking for added security measures to ease my stress. Enter the Hiplok, which, according to the tests I’ve watched, will turn multiple angle-grinder blades to dust. Do bike thieves carry several discs, and will they spend about 15 minutes trying to break this lock? I don’t know, but I have my doubts. At nearly $400, it’s about as expensive as it gets to secure your ride, but when your bike tops $5,000, it’s probably worth the added theft deterrence and peace of mind.
Santa left this one last year, and the rest of my handheld collection has felt neglected since. Sporting a Snapdragon 8 Elite (now dubbed the Dragonwing Q8) chip, excellent ergonomics, and a 6-inch 120Hz AMOLED screen, it’s the perfect balance between size and horsepower. The Android unit is capable enough to play most anything you can throw at it, without the bulk of a Steam Deck or the bloat of a Windows handheld. Thanks to things like Proton, FEX translation, and software like DroidDeck or GameNative, there isn’t much I can’t use it for. Streaming consoles or PC gaming? Check. Access to Steam, GOG, Epic, Rockstar libraries? Check. High-end native Android gaming? Yup. Emulate anything under the sun? You’re covered there, too. The latest Odin 3 Portal hardware revision gets a larger 7-inch screen and a base RAM configuration of 12GB over the original model’s 8GB. I may have to ask Mr. Claus about an upgrade…
– Nick Indge

articles.title: Un cuartel en Pozuelo, una estación en Torrejón y un satélite: así ha sido el primer ensayo militar de España con la red satelital de la UE
articles.text:
España ha hecho su primera conexión a través de Govsatcom, el programa de la Unión Europea (UE) que da acceso a comunicaciones seguras por satélite a organismos públicos. En este caso, se ha hecho una simulación con fines militares, por lo que ha estado coordinado tanto por el Instituto Nacional de Técnica Aeroespacial (INTA) como por el Centro de Sistemas y Tecnologías de la Información y las Comunicaciones (Cestic), ambos pertenecientes al Ministerio de Defensa.
La conexión ha sido exitosa, por lo que abre la puerta a su uso tanto con fines militares como civiles, siempre que requieran una conexión rápida en un lugar en el que no hay buen sistema de telecomunicaciones.
La simulación. En este caso se ha simulado la situación de una unidad militar desplegada en una zona sin cobertura de redes terrestres. Se ha situado en el acuartelamiento de Capitán Sevillano, en Pozuelo de Alarcón, mientras que el destinatario de las comunicaciones sería una estación del Cestic ubicada en Torrejón de Ardoz.
El INTA se encargó de dar soporte técnico, pero también actuó como intermediario con Govsatcom. Definió las necesidades de la unidad militar, teniendo en cuenta información como el volumen de datos, los tiempos de respuesta, la disponibilidad y la seguridad. Por su parte, los encargados del programa de la UE eligieron el servicio más adecuado para dichas necesidades y optaron por conectar el equipo con el SpainSat NG I, un satélite de comunicaciones seguras para las Fuerzas Armadas españolas, operado por Hisdesat.
A la hora de la verdad. Govsatcom reúne capacidades de comunicaciones por satélite comerciales y gubernamentales y las comparte con los Estados miembros. Los usuarios autorizados, como protección civil, guardias de fronteras u operadores militares, acceden a través de él y envían sus necesidades para que se les conecte con el servicio más adecuado tal y como ha hecho el INTA en este caso. Con todo esto, además de sus fines militares, podría ser útil durante emergencias o catástrofes naturales en las que los servicios de telecomunicaciones de Tierra hayan fallado.
SpainSat. Durante la simulación, se seleccionó el SpainSat NG I para ofrecer a España el servicio que requirió el INTA. No obstante, y a pesar de estar operado por una empresa española, Hisdesat, y financiado por el Ministerio de Defensa, el objetivo es que no esté solo disponible para España. Hisdesat pretende ponerlo a disposición de países aliados de la OTAN y de la UE y vender parte de la capacidad a otras entidades gubernamentales.
Airbus describe esta estrategia como útil para que los socios de España tengan superioridad de información. En definitiva, de eso va también Govsatcom. De unir fuerzas y ofrecer una red de telecomunicaciones colaborativa para que los servicios públicos de la UE puedan acceder a ella en ocasiones de emergencia.

Em vez de switches mecânicos tradicionais, adota teclas Tactile Mech-Dome de membrana com acionamento mais suave e silencioso, teclas de mídia dedicadas, iluminação RGB Lightsync em zonas e resistência a derramamentos de líquidos testada para até 60 ml. A presença do layout ABNT2 em versões nacionais facilita a digitação em português com acentuação nativa.
É uma alternativa coerente para quem não faz questão de switch mecânico e prefere silêncio, apoio integrado e preço mais contido. Funciona bem como primeiro teclado gamer ou para quem divide o PC com outras tarefas.
Comece definindo o espaço disponível na mesa e os gêneros de jogo que você mais joga. Modelos TKL liberam área para o mouse, enquanto teclados full-size mantêm o bloco numérico útil para produtividade e planilhas.
Em seguida, avalie a conexão (sem fio Lightspeed ou cabo USB), a altura das teclas (perfil baixo ou tradicional) e o tipo de resposta do switch (linear, tátil ou clicky). Também vale conferir o layout das teclas (ABNT2 ou padrão internacional) e a presença de controles de mídia dedicados.
Lightspeed é a tecnologia de conexão sem fio de 2,4 GHz da Logitech G desenvolvida para entregar baixa latência e estabilidade de sinal em jogos. Na prática, ela busca aproximar a resposta sem fio da experiência de um cabo USB, evitando atrasos perceptíveis em comandos rápidos.
O melhor teclado custo-benefício depende do seu orçamento e do tipo de uso: o G515 TKL Lightspeed se destaca entre os sem fio modernos de baixo perfil, enquanto o G413 SE atende quem busca um mecânico durável mais acessível e o G213 serve a quem quer gastar menos com foco em silêncio e conforto. Avalie o preço promocional no momento da compra e se você precisa de conexão sem fio ou se o cabo resolve bem o seu setup.
O Logitech G Hub centraliza a configuração de efeitos de iluminação RGB Lightsync, perfis por jogo, macros e atalhos das teclas. Em modelos compatíveis com o recurso KEYCONTROL, o software também permite criar camadas e atribuir múltiplas funções por tecla.
Teclados mecânicos costumam oferecer resposta mais consistente, durabilidade elevada dos switches e variedade de sensações (linear, tátil ou clicky) para jogos mais exigentes. Teclados de membrana, como o G213 com teclas Mech-Dome, entregam toque mais silencioso e preço menor, sendo suficientes para jogos casuais e uso misto.
A sigla TKL significa Tenkeyless, ou seja, um teclado sem o bloco numérico à direita. Remover essas teclas reduz a largura total do periférico, dando mais espaço para o movimento do mouse e deixando a mesa mais organizada.
Os teclados da linha Logitech G são compatíveis com Windows e macOS, variando conforme o modelo e o software de configuração. Em consoles como PS5 e Xbox, a conexão USB ou sem fio básica pode funcionar em jogos que aceitam teclado nativamente, mas recursos avançados como macros e perfis completos do G Hub dependem do computador e do suporte de cada jogo.

articles.title: Volvo empezó a entrenar robots humanoides en su planta de Bélgica para tareas físicamente exigentes
articles.text:
Volvo comenzó a entrenar robots humanoides en su planta de Gante, en Bélgica, para tareas repetitivas y físicamente exigentes. Es la primera fábrica de la automotriz sueca que prueba este tipo de máquinas, según informó la empresa el 26 de noviembre en un comunicado.
Los robots, fabricados por la división de robótica del grupo tecnológico sueco Hexagon, aprenden junto a los empleados y a la automatización existente. La tarea inicial consiste en colocar componentes en dos soportes con alta precisión.
El equipo de Volvo los entrena con aprendizaje por imitación: el robot aprende una tarea copiando cómo la hace una persona. Según la compañía, a medida que cada paso se compruebe, el trabajo será más difícil, con varias piezas a la vez, desplazamientos por la zona de producción e interacción con los sistemas automáticos de la planta.
Un robot de 1,65 metros que se mueve sobre ruedas
Según las especificaciones de Volvo, el robot AEON mide 1,65 metros, pesa 60 kilos y puede cargar 10 kilos. No tiene pies: se desplaza sobre ruedas, a hasta 2,4 metros por segundo, un ritmo similar a un trote suave. Usa cámaras y sensores para captar el entorno y manipular las piezas.
La empresa explica por qué eligió una forma humana. Los brazos robóticos fijos llevan décadas en las fábricas de autos y rinden en trabajos estables y repetitivos en un lugar fijo, pero algunas tareas que cansan el cuerpo requieren una flexibilidad que esos brazos no ofrecen.
“El diseño humanoide del AEON significa que puede encajar en nuestra producción tal como es hoy, junto a nuestros equipos y la automatización existente”, dijo Magnus Nilsson, director de Manufactura de Volvo. Agregó que el objetivo es que los robots asuman “las tareas físicamente más exigentes” para hacer el trabajo más ergonómico.
Arnaud Robert, presidente de Hexagon Robotics, afirmó que el propósito de la robótica humanoide es “generar valor de negocio” para los clientes. Ni Volvo ni Hexagon informaron cuántos robots hay hoy en Gante ni cuánto cuesta el programa, y el comunicado no menciona qué ocurrirá con los puestos de trabajo.
Un calendario con fecha: producción real desde mediados de 2027
El entrenamiento prepara un piloto en la fábrica durante el primer semestre de 2027, cuando llegarán más unidades a Gante para tareas más variadas. Volvo apunta a que los robots se usen en producción real desde mediados de ese año.
Otros fabricantes ya probaron humanoides
Volvo llega después de otras automotrices. BMW informó el 25 de junio que su robot Figure 03 empezará a trabajar en la planta de Spartanburg, en Estados Unidos, en tareas de secuenciación logística. Antes, el modelo Figure 02 completó allí un piloto en la carrocería, según el comunicado de BMW.
Brett Adcock, fundador y director ejecutivo de Figure AI, dijo en ese comunicado que los 11 meses de despliegue del Figure 02 demostraron que los humanoides “ya no son experimentos de laboratorio”.
Renault, por su parte, probó en su fábrica de Douai, en Francia, a Calvin, un robot desarrollado con la empresa francesa Wandercraft que agarra neumáticos de a dos, unos 30 kilos de una vez. La hoja de ruta de Renault, publicada en su revista corporativa el 26 de junio, prevé unos diez robots a fines de 2026 y 350 en fábricas de Francia y España a fines de 2027.

articles.title: What’s next for Kalyan Krishnamurthy after Flipkart? 5 possible paths
articles.text:
What’s next for Kalyan Krishnamurthy after Flipkart? 5 possible paths
From building a startup and backing founders to running another company, joining a board or advising the government, Kalyan Krishnamurthy has several paths open after nearly a decade at Flipkart’s helm.
Kalyan Krishnamurthy will step down as Flipkart CEO on December 4 after more than 11 years at the company, including nearly a decade as CEO. As the company searches for its next permanent leader, Chief Product and Technology Officer Balaji Thiagarajan will steer the ship alongside the board. What’s next for Krishnamurthy? For now, he’s keeping his cards close to his chest.
Krishnamurthy took over as CEO in 2017 and stayed on after Walmart acquired a controlling stake the following year. Before taking the top job, he managed Tiger Global’s India portfolio and represented the fund on Flipkart’s board. His work as an investor and operator offers some clues to what he could do next.
1. Build a startup around an ecommerce problem
Bharati Mujumdar, director of operations at executive search firm Venator Search Partners, sees scope for Krishnamurthy to start a technology company that serves retailers first and later expands into banking or other industries with large distribution networks.
“He would have sufficient experience in cutting edge tech, and he might want to set up a new and significant tech start up,” Mujumdar said.
Sunil Goel, managing director of executive search firm Global Hunt, said Krishnamurthy could build a business around a problem he encountered at Flipkart. He pointed to supply chain management, customer retention and verifying sellers or the products they list. A specialist could devote more time to one of those problems than a large marketplace can, Goel said.
Goel cited Delhivery as an example of how a logistics service built for ecommerce can grow into a large business in its own right. He said Krishnamurthy’s track record and industry relationships could help him raise capital if he chose to start a company.
Krishnamurthy has been specific about what interests him in retail technology. In July, he said the AI application he cared most about was getting products to customers faster. At a Walmart investor meeting, he described Flipkart’s technology work across shoppers, merchants and the supply chain. Software that helps retailers decide what to stock, where to hold inventory and how to fulfil orders would draw directly on that experience.
2. Take another CEO job
Mujumdar said running another large organisation might offer Krishnamurthy few new challenges after Flipkart. She pointed to Reliance as a possible exception.
Krishnamurthy’s comments in July offer a clue to the kind of operating role that might interest him. He singled out fashion, beauty, home products and everyday essentials as categories with room to grow online. A large retailer looking to expand its ecommerce business would give him a familiar set of decisions: which categories to enter, how to reach new shoppers and when to expand.
3. Return to investing
A move back to full-time investing would take Krishnamurthy into familiar territory after his years at Tiger Global. He continued to back startups while running Flipkart. YourStory reported that he invested in celebrity engagement platform Tring in 2020 and participated in software training startup Newton School’s Series A in 2021. In September, he was among the panellists behind an investment commitment to construction technology startup MiCoB on Vande Bharatam.
Mujumdar said growth or angel investing in ecommerce, logistics and retail would be a straightforward transition. She added that a full-time investing role might feel familiar after his years at Tiger Global.
4. Join a startup board
Krishnamurthy has argued that Indian startups need more independent directors. In 2024, he said managers and investors with a stake in a company can find it harder to question their own decisions.
An independent board seat at a founder-led company preparing to list or navigating a change in ownership would draw on both sides of his Flipkart experience. He first sat on the board representing an investor and later ran the company through Walmart’s acquisition of a controlling stake.
5. Advisor to the Centre or a state government
In 2021, while Krishnamurthy was CEO, Flipkart signed an agreement with the Union Ministry of Rural Development to help self-help groups sell nationwide through Flipkart Samarth. The agreement covered training, product catalogues and warehousing support. That same year, the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade formed an advisory council to help shape and drive adoption of the Open Network for Digital Commerce.
Krishnamurthy has also worked with state governments on getting small businesses online. In August, he met Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to discuss how more local producers could sell through digital platforms. Flipkart has partnered with the state’s One District, One Product programme since 2020 to help artisans, weavers and craftspeople reach online buyers. Karnataka offers a precedent for appointing an industry leader to an advisory role. In November, it named Mindtree co-founder Subroto Bagchi to chair its Vision Group for Skill Development.
There has been no public indication that the Centre or any state has approached Krishnamurthy. An assignment that would draw on his Flipkart experience is helping small producers with what comes after listing a product online: shipping orders reliably, managing returns and turning first-time buyers into repeat customers.

articles.title: GIGABYTE and Newegg Bring "AORUS VS40" to Southern California in November 2026
articles.text:
Friday, November 27th 2026
GIGABYTE and Newegg Bring "AORUS VS40" to Southern California in November 2026
GIGABYTE and Newegg will host AORUS VS40 at the Newegg Gamer Zone in City of Industry, California, on Saturday, November 21, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. PST. The event invites local collegiate PC gamers and hardware enthusiasts to celebrate 40 years of GIGABYTE by putting their skills to the test on the tournament floor and at gaming stations throughout the venue.
Gamers can flex their prowess in the AORUS VS40 tournament, which will feature 1v1 matches in VALORANT and League of Legend. The tournament systems will be powered by GIGABYTE's latest AMD X870 motherboards and premium AMD Radeon graphics cards. Between matches, attendees can test their reflexes in a speed challenge on GIGABYTE gaming monitors and explore GIGABYTE gaming laptops. Players can also collect stamps in an event passport as they complete challenges for a chance to earn prizes.
Register for AORUS VS40 on EventbriteA heat-press station will give attendees the chance to customize a tote bag. The event will also feature hourly prize drawings, limited-edition GIGABYTE merchandise, photo opportunities, and food and refreshments while supplies last.
Admission is free and an RSVP is required. The event is limited to 250 attendees. Registered guests should bring their Eventbrite confirmation and arrive early. Entry is first come, first served, subject to venue capacity.

articles.title: Canada’s National Bank launches no-fee accounts
articles.text:
Montreal-based National Bank has launched the No-Fee Everyday Account for customers who prefer digital banking.
With this account, customers receive unlimited electronic transactions with no fixed monthly fees and no minimum required balance. On top of that, account holders can get a two per cent bonus interest rate on the High Interest Savings Account.
National Bank also offers $250 cash back to those who deposit their pay into their No-Fee Everyday Account for three months in a row. To be eligible, recurring direct deposits have to be set up within 30 days of opening an account.
The No-Fee Everyday Account can be opened exclusively on National Bank’s website.

articles.title: iPad als Weihnachtsgeschenk: Diese Modelle sind ideal für Kinder – Schule, Alltag und Spaß
articles.text:
iPad als Weihnachtsgeschenk: Diese Modelle sind perfekt für Schule und Alltag
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Bei vielen Schüler:innen hat sich der Wunsch nach einem eigenen Tablet schon erfüllt: Laut Bitkom besaßen 54 Prozent der Sechs- bis 18-Jährigen schon im Jahr 2024 ein eigenes Gerät. In Haushalten, in denen schon ein iPhone oder Macbook vorhanden ist, kann ein iPad besonders praktisch sein, weil es sich nahtlos ins Apple-Ökosystem einfügt. Außerdem bietet es zahlreiche Funktionen, um die Nutzung durch dein Kind im Auge zu behalten. So kannst du unter anderem einen Kinder-Account anlegen, das iPad in die Familienfreigabe aufnehmen, Bildschirmzeiten festlegen und den App- und Webzugriff begrenzen. Wir erklären dir, welches iPad am besten zu deinem Kind passt und mit welchen Kosten du vor Weihnachten rechnen musst.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
iPad von Apple: Wann das Standardmodell ausreicht
Das Standard-iPad ist ein klassisches Einstiegsmodell und ideal für den Schulalltag. Es verfügt über ein 11 Zoll großes Display. Die Rückkamera mit zwölf Megapixeln filmt in 4K-Qualität. Die Frontkamera bietet ebenfalls zwölf Megapixel. Hinzu kommen Stereo-Lautsprecher und zwei Mikrofone. Die Leistung reicht für Lern-Apps, Notizen und Präsentationen in der Regel aus. Darüber hinaus eignet sich das Apple-Tablet für die meisten Spiele und Entertainment-Apps wie Youtube. Insbesondere für Grundschulkinder und alle, die ihr erstes Tablet bekommen, ist das Standardmodell somit eine gute Wahl.
Das iPad ist mit 128, 256 oder 512 Gigabyte Speicher und einem A16-Chip erhältlich. Laut Hersteller hält der Akku beim Surfen oder Streamen über WLAN bis zu zehn Stunden durch. Es unterstützt den WLAN-Standard 6 und ist optional als SIM-fähige Variante erhältlich. Zubehör wie der Apple Pencil und das Magic Keyboard Folio sind kompatibel. Apple bietet das iPad in Blau, Pink, Gelb und Silber an. Im Apple-Store kostet es Modell 499 Euro in der Basisvariante. Bei Amazon ist das iPad in allen Farben aktuell schon ab 444 Euro erhältlich.
Das zukunftssichere iPad Air für Schule und Studium
Das iPad Air die beste Wahl, wenn du eine leistungsfähige und möglichst langfristige Lösung suchst. Der M4-Chip, der auch in manchen Mac(book)s verbaut ist, bietet mehr Leistung als der A16 im Einstiegsmodell. Das Modell ist mit dieser Ausstattung erst seit März 2026 auf dem Markt und deshalb deutlich zukunftssicherer. Am besten eignet es sich für ältere Kinder in der Mittel- oder Oberstufe. Das iPad Air kann nicht nur bei Hausaufgaben in der Schule unterstützen, sondern dein Kind auch noch beim Start an der Uni begleiten.
Das Tablet ist mit Elf- und 13-Zoll-Display erhältlich. Die Rück- und Frontkamera entsprechen dem Standard-iPad, ebenso die Stereo-Lautsprecher und Mikrofone. Das iPad Air unterstützt allerdings den schnelleren WLAN-Standard 7 und ist als 5G-Mobilfunkversion erhältlich. Zur Auswahl steht es in Dunkelgrau, Türkis, Violett und Gold. Der interne Speicher beträgt maximal ein Terabyte. Laut Hersteller hält der Akku über WLAN bis zu zehn Stunden. Im Apple Store kostet das iPad Air ab 799 Euro. Bei Amazon startet der Preis schon bei 684,81 Euro. Dieser kann je nach Farbe variieren.
iPad kaufen: Was du bei der Auswahl beachten solltest
Apple hat noch weitere Modelle im Portfolio. Das iPad Pro ist auf rechenintensive Workflows wie Video- und Fotobearbeitung oder Grafikdesign zugeschnitten. Für die Schule reicht deshalb meist ein günstigeres Modell aus. Auch das iPad Mini ist für Hausaufgaben und Lernen weniger gut geeignet: Es ist das kompakteste Apple-Tablet und deshalb ideal für unterwegs. Gerade fürs Lesen ist der kleine Bildschirm aber weniger praktisch. Zudem liegt der Preis höher als beim Standardmodell. Als Weihnachtsgeschenk solltest du dich daher zwischen dem „normalen“ iPad und dem iPad Air entscheiden.
Außerdem kann es sich lohnen, mit dem Kauf noch etwas zu warten. Die Angebote von Amazon liegen derzeit zwar deutlich unter der unverbindlichen Preisempfehlung von Apple. Rund um den Black Friday am 27. November sind viele Elektronikartikel aber noch einmal reduziert. Solche Angebote lohnen sich besonders, da Apple aufgrund der anhaltenden Speicherkrise die Preise für einige Produkte deutlich erhöht hat. So kostet das iPad jetzt oft rund 100 Euro mehr als noch vor einigen Monaten. Wer noch mehr sparen möchte, greift zu einem gebrauchten Modell. Auch Kratzer oder Stürze sind hier leichter zu verschmerzen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 10.11.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: GTA 6 sur PC : les 60 FPS sont atteints, mais il y a un gros problème
articles.text:
Le pirate Cyberleek a diffusé une copie de la version Xbox Series X|S de GTA 6, avant d’en publier l’exécutable principal quelques jours plus tard. Depuis, des développeurs amateurs se sont lancés dans une course pour tenter de porter le dernier titre de Rockstar sur PC. Et autant dire que des résultats concrets sont obtenus. Certains parviennent même à atteindre le gameplay, mais à quelle fréquence d’images par seconde ?
GTA 6 : 60 FPS sur PC, vraiment ?
Ce jeudi 26 novembre 2026, le compte X GTA VI News a fait cette annonce : « Le portage PC de GTA 6 a officiellement atteint 60 fps…». Le dernier titre de Rockstar serait jouable en 60 fps sur PC ? Calmons nos ardeurs. En réalité, la barre des 60 fps a bel et bien été atteinte, mais durant une cinématique, lors d’une scène d’interrogatoire plus précisément, c’est-à-dire un moment où il ne se passe pas grand chose à l’écran. Comme le précise nos confrères de Frandroid, le compteur d’images par seconde est ensuite tombé entre 44 et 56 fps lors de cinématiques plus riches et intenses, avec des chutes vers 31 fps aux changements de plan. À noter que des internautes ont également repéré des bugs au niveau de l’éclairage et des yeux des personnages. Aucune phase de gameplay n’a été montrée.
En parlant du nombre d’images par seconde durant les phases de gameplay, il faut dire que les résultats sont pour l’instant peu concluants. Vice-Tay a annoncé une médiane de 21,6 fps lors d’une session de 30 minutes en bateau. Pour y parvenir, le projet a mobilisé une RTX 4090, tout en utilisant le profil graphique allégé de la Xbox Series S. De son côté, VIctory-7900XTX annonce atteindre environ 22 FPS dans une rue, mais ce résultat nécessite de désactiver certains correctifs normalement activés par défaut.
Il reste que ces différents projets partagent peu d’informations concernant les spécificités techniques qui leur ont permis d’atteindre ces fréquences d’images. Nous ne savons d’ailleurs pas si un générateur d’images a été activé pour simuler un affichage à 60 FPS.
Attention aux fausses informations et aux fichiers infectés
Sur le réseau social X, l’utilisateur LaunSSJ a expliqué qu’il jouait à GTA 6 sur son PC, en 4K et à 120 FPS. Comment cela est-il possible ? Comme le souligne une note de la communauté, le jeu tournait en réalité sur une console, et non sur un PC. Le signal vidéo était envoyé vers un ordinateur, qui utilisait un générateur d’images pour atteindre ce nombre mirobolant de 120 FPS. Par la suite, cette vidéo a été volée et présentée comme la preuve que GTA 6 pouvait tourner sur PC à 120 FPS. Les auteurs de ces publications mensongères ont également ajouté de faux outils de développement attribués à Claude pour donner davantage de crédibilité à leur démonstration. L’une de ces publications mensongères a tout de même récolté 77 000 likes. Quoi qu’il en soit, voici la vidéo de LaunSSJ qui est parvenu à faire tourner GTA 6 à 120 FPS, mais depuis une console distincte et grâce à un générateur d’images.
 GTA 6 4K 120 FPS (je m'amuse comme un enfant) pic.twitter.com/Oj8z2LZJGh
— Laun (@LaunSSJ) November 25, 2026
Rappelons enfin que des personnes mal intentionnées diffusent de fausses versions prétendument jouables de GTA 6 sur PC. Leur objectif est bien entendu d’inciter les internautes à les télécharger pour installer des logiciels malveillants sur leurs ordinateurs. Pour rappel, même avant la sortie du titre sur consoles, ce procédé était déjà utilisé.

articles.title: TSMC gives a sneap peak at AI Design Kit: Agentic AI with foundry expertise
articles.text:
TSMC gives a sneap peak at AI Design Kit: Agentic AI with foundry expertise
TSMC's ADK promises to cut accelerate chip development as nodes get more complex.
The semiconductor industry is in a paradoxical situation these days. On the one hand, AI drives demand for the leading-edge nodes from both established players and new entrants, with everyone trying to accelerate the development cycle. On the other hand, leading-edge nodes become more complex, which increases entry barriers and stretches design cycles. While the challenge seems to be insoluble, it looks like TSMC has found a solution.
At its 2026 Europe OIP Ecosystem Workshop in Munich, TSMC this week unveiled its AI Design Kit (ADK), a collection of process-specific technical information, implementation guidelines, and design methodologies that enables AI agents to automate and optimize chip development flows.
The ADK complements the foundry's traditional process design kits (PDKs) and enables AI agents to use TSMC's process-specific expertise, knowledge of electronic design automation (EDA) tools, and customers' proprietary design methodologies to automate physical implementation and optimization of chips. Ultimately, the initiative aims to reduce development cycles, improve design productivity, and simplify adoption of TSMC's advanced process technologies.
"The ADK complements our traditional PDK, and it brings in capabilities to augment the EDA and other design flows," said Aveek Sarkar, Head of Ecosystem and Alliance Management at TSMC. "Our goal with these agentic flows is to bring in the technology-specific learning we have at TSMC and layer that with your orchestration layer, with your design expertise, and to support the next generation of EDA or design flows and methodologies that you have."
Why AI?
While every new fabrication process from TSMC offers advantages in terms of power, performance, and area (PPA), it also considerably increases design complexity. Compared to TSMC's N5-derived manufacturing technologies (including various N4 nodes), the number of design rules has increased by 2.3X with N3P, 3.1X with N2P, and 3.6X with A14 (the first node to be supported by the ADK).
Meanwhile, the number of available standard library cells has increased by 2.8X, 5X, and 4.6X, respectively. Add to that a greater number of metallization stack options and plenty of EDA tool settings, and the number of possible design configurations becomes massive. As a result, conventional design optimization methodologies approach their productivity limits, according to TSMC. At the same time, some of TSMC's customers want to reduce their chip development cycles from 18 months to 12 months, Sarkar said.
| Technology | N5/N4P | N3P | N2P NanoFlex | A14 NanoFlex Pro | 
| Library | HD, HP | HD, HP, UHP | HD, HP, UHP + Boost Cells | HD, HP + Boost Cells | 
| Cell Count | 1.0x | 2.8x | 5.0x | 4.6x | 
| Rule Count | 1.0x | 2.3x | 3.1x | 3.6x | 
Usage of agentic AI could help chip developers to explore more design configurations within shorter timeframes, achieve more favorable PPA results from advanced process technologies, and potentially improve manufacturability and yields by implementing more extensive physical design optimization. Furthermore, it could reduce the amount of engineering work required to adopt a new fabrication process for a new design.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
"AI is bringing a significant benefit: faster design cycles, more verification coverage, faster time to closure," Sarkar said.
Do physical implementation faster
TSMC's early-phase AI Design Kit incorporates process-specific information, such as metal pitches, standard cell heights, routing track patterns, library cell naming conventions, and implementation guidelines, according to slides demonstrated at the event.
With the ADK, EDA agents — such as Cadence's InnoStack or Synopsys's Implementation Agent — can use a simple natural-language prompt and a large language model (LLM) to automatically generate a qualified automatic placement and routing (APR) reference flow for TSMC's A14 process technology. Such a flow includes project setup, library cell usage, placement and routing optimization, routing track and power grid creation, and wide-wire configuration. Traditionally, engineers could spend weeks on preparation of such scripts, but now APR scripts could be prepped with a natural language prompt, though TSMC did not disclose the actual time it takes to prep them (probably because it depends on design complexity and goals).
"Instead of spending weeks preparing APR scripts, EDA agents can take a simple prompt from users and the TSMC ADK and use a generative model to deliver a qualified APR reference flow," a spokesperson from TSMC said at the stage.
For more sophisticated design tasks, TSMC proposes an orchestration agent that resides at the customer's site and combines three sources of knowledge with clear ownership:
- Proprietary in-house design know-how, constraints, guidelines, and customized flow;
- Specialized EDA agents that know how to use EDA tools and their capabilities;
- TSMC's ADK that provides design reference package and technology-specific information on top of what EDA agent and tools know.
The orchestrator coordinates agents responsible for design diagnostics, power grid implementation, timing closure, design rule checks, and congestion mitigation. These agents analyze EDA tool output and automatically adjust parameters for subsequent iterations across floorplanning, placement, clock tree synthesis, routing, sign-off, and engineering change orders (ECOs). Such a methodology enables continuous design optimization 24/7 with less human intervention.
"The orchestrator then directs these agents to analyze the output of EDA tools and automatically adjust the settings for the next iteration across floorplan, placement, CTS, routing, sign-off, and ECO," the spokesman said. "This agentic AI flow drives the iterative design process 24/7, minimizing the turnaround time and maximizing productivity."
Complement, not replace
For now, TSMC's ADK primarily addresses physical implementation rather than chip architecture or logic design. The company has not demonstrated an autonomous design flow that takes a chip from an architectural specification to tape-out without human intervention. Nor has TSMC disclosed quantified PPA improvements, actual reductions in development cycles, or a commercial availability timeframe for its ADK.
It is noteworthy that TSMC's ADK neither replaces conventional PDKs nor substitutes for advanced AI-enabled EDA software from Cadence, Synopsys, Siemens EDA, or other developers. Instead, it provides process-specific knowledge that enables AI agents to make more informed decisions, while the actual physical implementation, simulation, optimization, and verification tasks remain the domain of specialized EDA tools. Thus, chip developers cannot use the ADK independently of traditional EDA infrastructure.
Strategic importance
For TSMC, the ADK could accelerate adoption of its latest fabrication processes, as customers could adapt their design methodologies to new nodes faster. Smaller fabless chip developers could also gain access to sophisticated physical design methodologies without the need to develop expertise comparable to that of prominent chip developers entirely in-house. Meanwhile, EDA and IP providers could benefit from closer integration of their products into process-specific design flows, whereas contract chip designers could offer shorter development times for their customers without significant additional investments.
There is also a potential customer lock-in aspect. While TSMC's proposed architecture preserves customers' ownership of proprietary design knowledge, extensive integration of foundry-specific physical design enablement collateral, EDA agents, and internal orchestration systems could make migration to another foundry harder and generally less likely as chipmakers get more accustomed to TSMC ADK (which is an exclusive capability for now and will remain an exclusive offering for a while). In effect, TSMC's competitive advantages will extend well beyond its process technologies, production capabilities, and conventional design ecosystem to include intelligence that emphasizes its customers' chip development methodologies.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.
