articles.title: American uranium plant forced offline following cyberattack — Peninsula Energy shuts down mining operation to investigate incident
articles.text:
American uranium plant forced offline following cyberattack — Peninsula Energy shuts down mining operation to investigate incident
Shutdown at its Strata Energy subsidiary hoped to be temporary
- Attackers are impersonating major brands such as Google, Nvidia, SpaceX, and Coca‑Cola to lure victims into fake paid webinars and expert interviews
- The campaign uses spoofed sign-in pages to steal corporate email credentials and potentially target enterprise authentication systems
- Researchers believe AI-assisted tooling may have helped build the phishing infrastructure, highlighting the growing role of AI in social-engineering attacks
Peninsula Energy, an Australian uranium mining company, was forced to temporarily shut down its operations in Wyoming, USA, after a cyberattack hit one of its subsidiaries.
In a security notice published earlier this week, the company said the attack affected the plant and wellfield operating and control systems at Strata Energy, its wholly owned subsidiary working on the Lance uranium project.
Lance is the company’s flagship uranium mining operation in Wyoming, which uses unconventional mining methods to extract the ore for the nuclear energy industry.
“Based on investigations to date, the incident appears to be confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems,” Peninsula said in the announcement. “The company’s corporate and administrative systems in the United States and Australia, including payroll and financial administration, remain unaffected by the incident,” it added.
The company said its biggest priorities at the moment were protecting the safety of its employees, securing the infrastructure, and making sure operations resume as normal as soon as possible. It also said it was currently investigating the issue and analyzing whether or not any data was compromised or stolen in the attack. This investigation was still ongoing at the time of publication.
Trading halt
Elsewhere in the notice, Peninsula did not say when it might resume operations, and stressed that it still doesn’t know what the impact on its 2027 production guidance might be. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said.
Two days before issuing the notice, Peninsula requested a trading halt, as well. It said it asked for a voluntary suspension until Monday, November 30, “or when the company is able to release an announcement regarding the resumption of operations at Lance and any resulting impact on the company’s production guidance.”
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Mining and energy companies are important targets for cybercriminals, both state-sponsored and for-profit groups. Throughout the years, many similar incidents occurred, disrupting operations and even forcing companies to temporarily bring parts of their infrastructure offline.
In December 2022, Canadian miner Copper Mountain Mining was struck by ransomware that affected its IT systems at the Copper Mountain mine, as well as corporate headquarters.
No word on the attackers
A year prior, in March 2019, Norwegian aluminium and energy giant Norsk Hydro was hit by LockerGoga, which was a big ransomware encryptor at the time. Several facilities were forced to switch to manual operations, severely disrupting production. The incident ultimately cost the company an estimated NOK 650–750 million ($66-$76 million) and its alleged mastermind, a Ukrainian man named Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, ended up on the FBI’s most wanted list.
In May 2021, US pipeline operator Colonial Pipeline shut down its entire fuel transportation network following a ransomware attack by the DarkSide group. Although the attackers compromised its corporate IT network rather than its operational technology systems, the company suspended pipeline operations as a precaution, triggering fuel shortages across parts of the US East Coast.
South African mining group Sibanye-Stillwater also experienced a cyberattack in July 2024, which disrupted its global IT infrastructure and forced some facilities to rely on manual backup processes. Its US metallurgical complex suffered short-term delays in smelting and recycling operations, as a result.
So far, almost nothing is known about the incident itself. We don’t know if this was a ransomware attack or malware attack (which could make sense given the fact that operating and control systems were shut off), or a data smash-and-grab. We also don’t know who the attackers were, or how they managed to break in. Chinese state-sponsored actors are known for targeting critical infrastructure and energy companies, and usually break in through edge devices, routers, security camera recorders and other internet-facing network appliances. They usually do that by exploiting vulnerabilities or weak credentials to establish access.
So far, no threat actors have claimed responsibility for the attack, and no data has yet surfaced anywhere on the dark web.

articles.title: GTA 6 sur PC : deux faux portages piégeaient les joueurs sur GitHub
articles.text:
Pour installer GTA 6 sur Windows depuis deux dépôts GitHub, il fallait coller dans PowerShell une commande fournie par des pirates, avec les droits d'administrateur. Bitdefender a repéré le piège, et GitHub a supprimé les deux pages quelques minutes après son signalement.
On est passé à ça du drame. Certains utilisateurs ont cru qu'enfin, Rockstar Games avait cédé à la pression des joueurs et porté GTA 6 sur PC. Que nenni. GTA 6 est sorti le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, et Rockstar mentionne seulement ces deux consoles sur le site officiel du jeu. Faute de version Windows, des développeurs amateurs tentent de faire tourner sur PC la version Xbox du jeu, issue d'une fuite, avec l'aide de l'intelligence artificielle. Avec les portages les plus avancés, le jeu fonctionne à une vingtaine d'images par seconde. Take-Two, la maison mère de Rockstar, a obtenu de GitHub le blocage de Leonida, l'un de ces projets, et de ses copies, soit 3 007 dépôts au total. Sur GitHub, des pirates ont profité de ces projets pour publier de fausses versions Windows du jeu.
Une commande PowerShell en administrateur pour installer le faux GTA 6
Dans le premier dépôt, les pirates proposaient le jeu complet, cracké et sans lanceur. Dans le second, ils annonçaient un portage communautaire, censé faire fonctionner la version console sur PC grâce à une couche de traduction. Sur les deux pages, ils promettaient une fréquence d'images élevée et le jeu en ligne sans compte Rockstar. Ils avaient ajouté la configuration requise et une rubrique de dépannage, de quoi donner à l'ensemble l'allure d'un vrai guide d'installation.
Les pirates vous demandaient ensuite d'ouvrir le Terminal Windows ou PowerShell en tant qu'administrateur, de coller leur commande, puis d'appuyer sur Entrée. Le code hébergé à l'adresse nkrnl[.]cfd est alors téléchargé et lancé aussitôt, avec des droits élevés sur la machine. Pour Bitdefender, l'objectif est très probablement de voler vos données. Les pirates peuvent en outre changer de logiciel malveillant à cette adresse d'une campagne à l'autre, préviennent les chercheurs.
Les spécialistes appellent cette méthode ClickFix. Et vous la connaissez désormais. Mais pour ceux du fond, les pirates vous font lancer la commande sous un prétexte, la correction d'une erreur ou, ici, l'installation d'un jeu. Sur l'une des pages, ils conseillaient aussi d'ajouter une exclusion dans Sécurité Windows en cas de blocage du téléchargement, pour que l'antivirus de Windows laisse passer le programme. Pour vous rassurer, ils vantaient un code open source et des analyses antivirus sans alerte. « Une commande d'installation collée peut donner à un code inconnu le contrôle de votre PC », résume Bitdefender.
Cet été, d'autres escrocs vous poussaient à télécharger une fausse démo de GTA 6 pour PC, un fichier à ouvrir. Avec ces faux portages, vous collez une simple ligne de texte dans Windows.
Que faire si vous avez lancé la commande du faux GTA 6
Pour Bitdefender, tout se joue au moment où vous collez et lancez la commande. Si vous l'avez exécutée, partez du principe que votre ordinateur est compromis, y compris quand la fenêtre du terminal s'est simplement refermée.
Déconnectez-le d'Internet et lancez une analyse complète avec votre antivirus. Changez ensuite vos mots de passe depuis un autre appareil sain, en commençant par votre messagerie, puis vos comptes de jeu et de paiement. Dans les réglages de chaque compte, déconnectez les autres sessions et activez la double authentification quand le service la propose.
Vérifiez enfin vos achats récents et les options de récupération de vos comptes. Dans votre messagerie, repérez aussi toute règle de transfert créée à votre insu. Si l'antivirus détecte un logiciel malveillant, ou si vous doutez de l'état de la machine, faites appel à un technicien avant de vous reconnecter, par exemple grâce à Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr.

articles.title: Cómo ha cambiado el valor de la criptomoneda ethereum en las últimas 24 horas
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda virtual #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 122.3M de unidades creadas.
Mientras el debate se acalora cada día más sobre la conveniencia o no de su uso, ethereum cotiza este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) en 1722.02 dólares, lo que supone un cambio de 1.26 % con respecto a las últimas 24 horas y una variación de 0.0 % con referencia a su valor alcanzado en la última hora.
En cuanto a su popularidad de mercado, ha mantenido el puesto #2 entre las monedas digitales.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Du klickst Excel-Summen noch von Hand? SUMMEWENNS spart dir Stunden
articles.text:
Excel SUMMEWENNS: So sparst du laut Weltmeister Stunden im Job
Excel ist eines der meistgenutzten Office-Programme. Wenn es allerdings darum geht, den vollen Funktionsumfang auszuschöpfen, stoßen viele Berufstätige an ihre Grenzen. Diarmuid Early, der 2025 den ersten Platz bei der Excel-Weltmeisterschaft belegte, hat im Interview mit Business Insider seine wichtigsten Tipps verraten.
Diarmuid Early und seine Excel-Tipps für den Berufsalltag
Diarmuid Early entdeckte seine Begeisterung für Excel schon während des Studiums. Später setzte er seine Kenntnisse zunächst bei der Boston Consulting Group (BCG) ein. Anschließend arbeitete er zehn Jahre bei der Deutschen Bank, wo Datenanalyse und Finanzberichterstattung zu seinen zentralen Aufgaben gehörten. Heute ist Early selbstständig und führt eine eigene Beratungsfirma, mit der er Unternehmen beim professionellen Einsatz von Excel unterstützt. Das Programm begleitet ihn somit schon seit seiner gesamten beruflichen Karriere.
„Mein wichtigster Tipp für Büroangestellte ist, daran zu glauben, dass es einen besseren Weg gibt”, so der Experte. „Wann immer Sie etwas manuell und repetitiv machen, gibt es in Excel sehr wahrscheinlich eine bessere Methode.“ Besonders empfiehlt er die „Sumifs“-Funktion, die im Deutschen auch als „Summewenns“ bekannt ist. Sie ermöglicht es, Werte in einem Bereich zu summieren, wenn mehrere definierte Kriterien erfüllt sind. Zwar koste der Einstieg zunächst etwas Zeit, aber der Lernerfolg beschleunige sich mit jeder weiteren Anwendung deutlich, sagt Early.
Summewenns in Excel automatisiert Berechnungen nach Kriterien
„Am schlimmsten finde ich es, wenn ich eine Formel sehe, die aus 50 verschiedenen Zahlen in der Form A1 + B3 + C5 + D10 besteht. Jemand hat sie offensichtlich alle von Hand eingegeben oder per Klick, Klick, Klick“, so Early im Interview. „Der Zeitaufwand dafür ist enorm, und die Wahrscheinlichkeit, dass man einmal falsch klickt und einen Fehler macht, den man nie wiederfinden wird, ist sehr hoch.“ Automatisierte Funktionen seien dagegen deutlich weniger fehleranfällig.
Der Experte betont außerdem, wie wichtig es ist, Zeit für die inhaltliche Einordnung der Ergebnisse zu haben. Es sei großartig, wenn man sich schnell durch eine Tabelle klicken und direkt zum Ergebnis gelangen kann, so Early. Denn so bleibe genügend Raum, die Zahlen kritisch zu hinterfragen. „Das ist etwas, was junge Banker:innen und Berater:innen am wenigsten tun. Sie sehen es als ihre Aufgabe an, das Modell anzuwenden und die Antwort zu liefern. Die nächste Person in der Hierarchie fragt dann: Was bedeutet das? Was ist die Erkenntnis? Ist das sinnvoll?“ Wer sich diese Fragen selbst stelle und die Ergebnisse entsprechend kommuniziere, gewinne an Glaubwürdigkeit. „Außerdem ist es viel wahrscheinlicher, dass Sie Ihre eigenen dummen Fehler entdecken, bevor es jemand anderes tut.“
KI und Excel als Unterstützung für die Datenanalyse
„Grundsätzlich gibt es auf jeder Ebene der Excel-Kenntnisse Dinge, die man falsch macht, ohne sich dessen bewusst zu sein, bis man die nächste Ebene erreicht. Es gibt überall Probleme.“ Gerade für Einsteiger:innen könnten KI-Tools deshalb künftig eine wertvolle Unterstützung sein: „Wenn es so weit ist, denke ich, dass KI sehr hilfreich sein wird, um Menschen von schlecht zu nicht schlecht oder vielleicht sogar von schlecht zu gut zu bringen. Für Menschen wie mich, die schon ziemlich erfahren sind, wird es wahrscheinlich keine große Hilfe sein.“
Excel ist auf nahezu jedem Firmencomputer installiert – trotzdem bleibt das Potenzial häufig ungenutzt. Early plädiert dafür, das zu ändern. „Ich kenne 50.000 Hacks“, sagt der Weltmeister. „In meiner Zeit bei BCG habe ich viele Excel-Schulungen durchgeführt.“ Immer wieder habe er erlebt, dass die Teilnehmer:innen nach dem Erlernen einer neuen Funktion zugleich begeistert und erschrocken reagierten. Einige hätten ihm erzählt, dass sie am Vorabend nicht bis zwei Uhr morgens hätten arbeiten müssen, wenn sie den entsprechenden Excel-Trick früher gekannt hätten.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich im Januar 2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Volvo’s big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids
articles.text:
COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015, both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric. As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market. At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-new replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets.
So instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base.
Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also new, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before.
The weather was nowhere near this pleasant on the day we drove across this bridge. This is the XC60.
Volvo Cars
The weather was nowhere near this pleasant on the day we drove across this bridge. This is the XC60.
Volvo Cars
It wasn’t even this nice, just lashing rain. This is the XC90.
Volvo Cars
It wasn’t even this nice, just lashing rain. This is the XC90.
Volvo Cars
The weather was nowhere near this pleasant on the day we drove across this bridge. This is the XC60.
Volvo Cars
It wasn’t even this nice, just lashing rain. This is the XC90.
Volvo Cars
We first saw the revamped 2028 XC60 (and learned about its technical details and those of the XC90) in September, but with the cars going into production now and due to reach the first US customers in the first quarter of next year, we got the opportunity to spend some seat time with the updated cars.
Charge!
Both the midsize XC60 and three-row XC90 use the same PHEV powertrain. Under the hood, there’s a 2.0 L four-cylinder direct-injection gasoline engine that generates 247 hp (184 kW) and 226 lb-ft (306 Nm) together with a 70 hp (50 kW), 122 ft-lb (165 Nm) electric motor, both of which drive the front wheels. At the rear axle there’s a second electric motor, with an output of 174 hp (130 kW) and 228 lb-ft (309 Nm). Combined output for the hybrid system is 455 hp (339 kW) and 560 lb-ft (759 Nm).
There’s also a much bigger battery, with a net capacity of 37.9 kWh (41.2 kWh gross). If you set the car’s mode to Pure, which relies solely on the rear electric motor for propulsion, that translates to an EPA range estimate of 78 miles (126 km) for the XC60 and 73 miles (116 km) for the larger, draggier XC90. Which is significant—when the average driver drives fewer than 30 miles a day, it means these PHEVs carry enough electrons for a couple of days of tailpipe-emissions-free driving before it needs to be plugged in again or the engine to fire up.
There are new matrix LED headlights but still with the Thor’s Hammer DRL.
Credit:
Volvo Cars
There are new matrix LED headlights but still with the Thor’s Hammer DRL.
Credit:
Volvo Cars
When it is time to plug it back in, expect it to take about four hours with a level 2 charger of at least 16 A, or 27 hours if you’re limited to 120 V. In Hybrid mode, where you get the benefit of both electric motors and the gas engine, Volvo expects a combined efficiency of 67 mpge in the XC60, and 61 mpge for the XC90.
Even if the gas engine is running and you’re in Hybrid or Power mode (which keeps the engine on all the time), you can drive these Volvos as if they were EVs with one-pedal driving: just move the transmission from D to B. The Volvos are always using their electric motors to slow the car before the friction brakes intervene, and in B you get the same amount of lift-off regen regardless of mode. For city traffic, it’s very effective. (In Pure, although only the rear motor deploys energy, both front and rear motors regen brake.)
In power mode, with all 455 hp unleashed, you can chirp the wheels on a wet day, but these model year 2028 cars are about one large male human heavier than the outgoing model year, both of which were already pretty heavy. So don’t expect performance-car performance. The XC60 is the sweeter to drive on a winding road, but both are entirely at home cruising on a highway or creeping along in a city, which is where cars like these spend the vast majority of their time. There’s more road intrusion into the cabin of the XC60—the larger Volvo rides on air suspension that does a much better job of filtering that out.
The XC90 is a more cosseting experience.
Credit:
Volvo
The XC90 is a more cosseting experience.
Credit:
Volvo
A first-drive event like this isn’t the best place to get a good read on real-world efficiency. We usually have to share cars with other journalists, and there’s limited time to drive on roads that may not be representative—too sinuous, or not enough traffic, for example. We need to try all the different drive modes and see how cars respond to different inputs. And it’s rare you’ll spend the entire day with one car, finishing at the same point you started.
That said, I can’t give you a definite read on range and efficiency for these two plug-ins. But my unscientific estimate is that my drive partner and I, in an XC60, drove about 60 km in a mix of city driving and higher speeds on the way to Malmo in Sweden, which is on the other side of a gigantic bridge, and we used about half the battery pack to do so. (Volvo asked us to put the PHEVs in Hold or Charge mode at 50 percent to leave some state of charge for whoever drove the cars after lunch.)
Thus, there was little charge left in the XC90 when it was my turn to drive the final stint back into Copenhagen. Since I wasn’t worried about combined efficiency, I ran the car in Charge mode for about 20 min, regenerating the battery from an indicated 10 km to an indicated 21 km, then switched to Pure once we reached the city, with about 16 km to go.
The rear lights are new.
Credit:
Volvo Cars
The rear lights are new.
Credit:
Volvo Cars
Massage time
Volvo already had a reputation for great automotive interiors, and with this refresh, it has pushed things forward a little. There’s a new wood finish, new textiles, and new backlighting. The resemblance between the two interiors from the front seat is now quite strong, particularly since the test cars Volvo brought to Denmark wore identical color schemes inside.
Our final 1.6 km to the hotel took more than 30 minutes to negotiate thanks to a reception for very important people that apparently took place next to the hotel. Most of this jam was on one street, with our destination in sight, but the frustration was in part ameliorated by Volvo’s secret weapon: its seat massage function.
Lots of other OEMs offer massaging front seats, which inflate and deflate the internal air bladder to massage your shoulders, back, and sometimes butt. But none massage you with quite the firmness of a Volvo seat. And they have the power to distract you from terrible in-car situations, as I discovered when stuck in a V90 Cross Country with Nigel the Cat, whose way of remonstrating with me about his trip to the feline ophthalmologist was to scream at high volume until he ran out of breath, at which point he’d pant for a few minutes, then start again. The seat in that car is the only reason we both made it home safely. And so, in Copenhagen, I set the seat to pulse and did some box breathing.
The upgraded XC60 interior.
Volvo Cars
The upgraded XC60 interior.
Volvo Cars
Here’s the XC90.
Volvo Cars
Here’s the XC90.
Volvo Cars
New wood and textile for the dash.
Volvo Cars
New wood and textile for the dash.
Volvo Cars
Here’s the XC90.
Volvo Cars
New wood and textile for the dash.
Volvo Cars
As well as new interior materials, you’ll also notice a new infotainment screen in both cars. Gone are the old 9-inch displays, replaced by a new 11.2-inch touchscreen that stands a little proud of the dash rather than recessed into it. Just this one upgrade alone really lifts both interiors; the old, small screen was showing its age. Most Ars readers will recoil at the news that Gemini has replaced the previous Google Assistant, but at least the voice-recognition capabilities are improved. Gemini will still struggle with some commands—I asked it to tell me my current efficiency, which it failed at, but it’s rather good at looking stuff up on the Internet while I drive.
There are also some updated advanced driver-assistance systems, like a warning if cyclists approach your opening door, and an updated 360-degree parking view. But there’s no point-to-point assist like Mercedes is introducing, or a hands-free “level 2+” system like Super Cruise; Volvo’s experience with the EX90 may have left it a little gun-shy.
With a battery big enough for daily driving and a more modern interior experience, there’s a lot to like about both the 2029 XC60 and XC90. However, we still don’t know how much they’ll cost when they go on sale in Q1 next year. With twice the battery capacity, it’s reasonable to expect a slight price rise, but without knowing how much, it’s hard to say whether it’s a good deal or not.
Jonathan is the Automotive Editor at Ars Technica. He has a BSc and PhD in Pharmacology. In 2014 he decided to indulge his lifelong passion for the car by leaving the National Human Genome Research Institute and launching Ars Technica's automotive coverage. He lives in Washington, DC.

articles.title: Masters’ Union lays off over 350 employees
articles.text:
Masters’ Union hit by widespread job cuts, employees say
Masters’ Union layoffs are estimated to have affected over 350 employees, disproportionately impacting sales staff and including recent hires, according to sources.
More than 350 employees of Gurugram-based educational institution Masters’ Union have been affected by job cuts in recent months, according to employee estimates, with the sales division accounting for a significant share of the estimated exits.
YourStory spoke to two former employees and one serving employee of the institution on the condition of anonymity. We have also reviewed several screenshots showing the removal of affected employees from the institution’s WhatsApp groups over the last few days.
The development comes within two months of the Gurugram-based education institution transitioning towards a university model. It was originally founded as a business and technology school in 2020 by Pratham Mittal, offering undergraduate and postgraduate courses in subjects such as business management and marketing.
YourStory reached out to Masters’ Union seeking clarification on the reported job cuts, the number of employees affected and the reasons for the exits.
Masters' Union has denied that is is undertaking any mass layoffs. In a statement, the institution said, "Like any organisation, we have a regular annual performance appraisal process, as part of which the bottom 5–6% of performers are let go. This has been a consistent practice for several years."
Stating that the company has been growing rapidly, Masters’ Union said it continues to actively hire across functions including faculty, academics, admissions, programme management, student outreach and career services.
"Our team strength has doubled in the last one year, with over 50 people joining us in the last month alone," the statement said.
Student applications have grown 2.5 times over the last two years, it added.
"We have also transitioned into a university, with the regulatory oversight and compliance requirements that come with it. We continue to invest in our people, academic capabilities and institutional infrastructure to support this growth."
However, a former employee, who has been laid off, said the layoff exercise has affected employees across sales, marketing and finance, particularly in sales.
He estimated that 50-60% of those affected had been placed on performance improvement plans, while the remaining included recent hires and those not on any performance-related review.
This employee, who had not been placed on the performance plan, also claimed that some employees were offered just seven days’ severance.
Another employee said that Masters’ Union had, in recent times, hired several team leaders and managers, many of whom have now been laid off.
On whether they were let go on the basis of performance, he said, “It’s not that they were not performing well. So, that is not a valid reason.”
He also said, although he has not been laid off, he was unsure about his future at the institution as most of his colleagues and managers have been let go.
Another employee whom YourStory spoke to was let go yesterday. He said the layoffs are still ongoing. “In the sales team alone, 220 employees have been laid off so far. It started a few months back, but, over the last few days, over 100 were laid off. Daily we are seeing 20-25 people being let go.”
The employee, who was in the sales team, said he was put on a performance improvement plan a few months ago. However, the plan was revoked once his team completed its sales target, he added.
But he said he was told by the HR department to resign owing to business prerogatives as the institution was cutting down on its educational programmes.
These developments coincide with a significant shift in the institution’s operations.
On September 24 this year, the Governor of Haryana gave assent to the Haryana Private Universities (Amendment) Act, 2026, which added Masters’ Union University in Gurugram to the state’s schedule of private universities. The Act was published in the state Gazette on October 12.
This brings the institution within the regulatory framework applicable to private universities. Under the University Grants Commission’s 2003 regulations, the UGC can inspect private universities to assess their programmes, faculty, infrastructure and financial viability, among other parameters.
The former employee quoted earlier said Masters’ Union had earlier focused on selling certificate programmes, but it was now looking to convert some of them into degree or diploma offerings. He said this, alongside a push to reduce costs, could explain the institution’s decision to retain a smaller salesforce focused on converting existing leads.
He added that there had been a recurrent pattern of hiring and exits in the sales team, with recruits given stringent targets to close deals within one or two months and being let go in case they were not met. He also said AI was not driving these layoffs as its use in sales was limited.

articles.title: Intel "Razor Lake-AX" Split Into MoP and MoB Lines, iGPU Tipped at RTX 5070 Ti Laptop Level
articles.text:
Friday, November 27th 2026
Intel "Razor Lake-AX" Split Into MoP and MoB Lines, iGPU Tipped at RTX 5070 Ti Laptop Level
More details have surfaced regarding Intel's next-next CPU lineup known as "Razor Lake." Specifically, the Intel Razor Lake-AX chip, which will reportedly come in two parallel product lines. According to prominent Intel leaker Jaykihn, Razor Lake-AX will be split into MoP (memory-on-package) and MoB (memory-on-board) lineups. The MoP version officially supports up to 96 GB of LPDDR5X and comes in 16-core and 28-core CPU configurations, targeted at laptops and mini PCs. This is the version that was pictured yesterday with empty memory pads that the OEMs will fill themselves. The MoB line, on the other hand, goes up to 192 GB and uses the 28-core CPU part. Jaykihn also floated the possibility of a 52-core MoB option with dual compute tiles, but apparently that line is still in its definition state and won't come to laptops.
On the graphics side, we got a new tip from leaker Haze today, who posted a single line claiming "Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti mobile like performance." This was a quote tweet of his earlier claim that the Razor Lake-AX chip uses on-package memory. Although he doesn't point out which configuration he's talking about, it's probably the flagship with 32 Xe3P GPU cores. This is a single line from a leaker, so take it with a grain of salt. If true, that would be quite an impressive feat for the Razor Lake-AX chip. Memory bandwidth will also be important for gaming performance since the AX chip only supports LPDDR5X. The Razor Lake-AX MoP line is expected to be announced or launched sometime in late 2027, but the timeline is hazy right now since the product is so far out.
Sources:
				Jaykihn on X, 				Haze on X, 				via Wccftech			
	
	
	
		
	
		
4 Comments on Intel "Razor Lake-AX" Split Into MoP and MoB Lines, iGPU Tipped at RTX 5070 Ti Laptop Level
Small reminder: RTX 5070 Ti Laptop uses the same GB205 die as the desktop 5070, but its form factor puts it slightly behind it. The issue with Blackwell/RDNA4 and Ada Lovelace/RDNA3 is the absolutely gigantic gap between 60-class and 70-class GPU, which amounts to a nearly 35-40% performance increase going to the 70-class.
It would be logical to try to get into that spot since nobody has been willing to do it for 4 years straight, but such claims sound really optimistic, or even basically impossible for an iGPU. And even if it does, I doubt the main purpose of this chip will be about gaming.
That is a nice level of performance for an igpu that is half the size of a ryzen AI 395 io die
Much weaker since it's holding 10 GT/s memory instead of 19 GT/s in the similar B70 for example.
Which version of the 5070 mible GPU? The one that has a minimum TGP of 50W? Of course a CPU could use that much power on an included GPU, too. Lord knows Intel has 100W+ CPU in the past.

articles.title: Jackery’s home power backup guide: Matching capacity to your home’s actual needs during Black Friday sales
articles.text:
Jackery’s Black Friday deals run until Dec. 6 across Canada, with the “Winter Ready. Jackery On.” philosophy taking up to 60 per cent off portable solar generators backup power stations. Considering the unique challenges of Canadian winters, the most common mistake home backup buyers make is either overspending on excess capacity or buying a unit that is too small to handle their needs.
What do watt-hours and watts tell you?
When you look at a solar generator, the two numbers that matter most are capacity and output. Capacity is measured in watt-hours (Wh) and tells you how long a unit can keep going before it needs a recharge.
For context, an average side-by-side refrigerator and freezer combo uses about 1400Wh daily. Output is measured in watts (W) and tells you how much power the unit can deliver at once to run multiple appliances simultaneously. That same typical Canadian refrigerator/freezer draws roughly 200W while it’s actively cooling. That makes the Jackery HomePower 2000 Plus v2 a great choice for keeping food fresh, storing up to 2048Wh and providing up to 2400W at one time. And every Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2 you add to it increases storage by 2048Wh.
What do you want to keep running?
To find the right output and capacity, you need to add up the typical draw of your essential hardware. A standard fridge or freezer will draw between 100 W and 400 W depending on its size and compressor cycling. You will also want to account for your router, laptops, lights, the furnace fan, and perhaps a sump pump if you have a basement.
How fast does the unit take over when the power drops?
Switchover speed is crucial if you’re trying to keep sensitive electronics from resetting or a fridge compressor from shutting down. Jackery’s Explorer 2000 v2 restores your power in 20 milliseconds or less when it drops, fast enough to keep basic electronics running without a hitch, including many Wi-Fi routers and modems. The FridgeGuard acts even faster, with a 10-millisecond response time that protects sensitive compressor components.
How does a solar generator recharge when the outage lasts for days?
Jackery’s systems are designed to be kept plugged into the wall so they’re fully charged ahead of a storm. Once the grid is down and you have depleted the battery, you can recharge the unit using the SolarSaga 340 X Solar Panel. Active solar charging extends runtime and can help keep life relatively normal throughout short blackouts.
During longer outages, if you cut power usage to just the essentials, the right solar panel setup can just about keep your home running indefinitely: the Explorer 2000 v2 recharges in around 5 hours with direct sunlight and proper placement of two SolarSaga 340 X panels. So, if your home’s essential core load draws less than 2042Wh from dusk to dawn (and it’s sunny out during the day), your refrigerator and Wi-Fi can basically run uninterrupted until the power’s back on, as long as you keep the Explorer 2000 v2 topped up throughout the day.
Which size fits which home?
Because Jackery solar generators meet strict indoor safety standards — producing no emissions, requiring no gas, and running almost silently — you can set them up right in your living space. That means The World’s No.1 Solar Generator Brand* offers a solution for every type of home layout.
If you live in a detached house with a furnace fan, a sump pump, and a full-size fridge, you need high capacity and high output. The Explorer 5000 Plus delivers 5,040 Wh of capacity and 7,200 W of output. It can run a mini fridge for 26 hours, a small water pump for 40 hours, and a microwave for 3.5 hours.
If you live in a townhouse and want to run a household refrigerator, a microwave, and keep 24 laptops charged, the Explorer 2000 V2 provides 2,042 Wh of capacity. It can power a 520 W fridge for 3.2 hours or a 5 W light for 155 hours. The expansion capability of a model like the HomePower 2000 Plus v2 makes it ideal for households that want to start with essential home backup now and potentially expand its appliance support and runtime in the future.
If you just need targeted backup for the kitchen, the FridgeGuard offers up to 15 hours of fridge runtime in a sleek package just 2.6 inches thick. Its automated, 10ms-or-less switchover time ensures the sensitive components in the compressor aren’t damaged when the power goes out, and it fits easily in a modern kitchen physically and in terms of appearance, ready to spring into action at a moment’s notice, without intruding on everyday life.
If you want a scalable home backup hub, the HomePower 3600 Plus stores 3584Wh with a 3600W output, easily enough to run a full-size refrigerator for over a day.
What does it cost this Black Friday?
During the sale at ca.jackery.com, the Explorer 5000 Plus is $3,899 (regular $4,999). You can also bundle it as the Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus with one solar panel for $4,669 (regular $5,999).
The Explorer 2000 V2 is down to $1,099 (1,410 off the regular $2,499), and the FridgeGuard is $869 (regular $1,099).
The Explorer 1000 v2 is discounted to $649 (450 off the regular $1,099)
The HomePower 3600 Plus is on sale for $2,559 (regular $3,999), or you can grab the Jackery Solar Generator HomePower 3000 bundle with a SolarSaga 340 X panel for $3,189 (regular $4,399).
The broader sale runs until December 6 (with slight pricing shifts expected after December 1). Plus, buyers who secure their units on ca.jackery.com between November 19 and November 30 receive Jackery’s 30-Day Price Match guarantee, which ensures they’ll enjoy the best price available over the next month in case additional discounts arrive after they’ve already made their purchase.
*Based on cumulative sales volume and cumulative revenue as of the end of 2025, Jackery ranked No. 1 globally among solar generator brands. Data source: Frost & Sullivan, White Paper on Global Solar Generator and Plug-in Solar Storage Industry (2026).

articles.title: Anthropic a trouvé le moyen de piéger un Claude désobéissant
articles.text:
Anthropic tend des pièges à sa propre intelligence artificielle générative. L’entreprise américaine vient de présenter Siren, un nouveau test conçu pour voir si ses agents IA, comme Claude, enfreignent leurs règles quand on leur en donne l’occasion. Pour berner l’IA, Siren s’appuie sur une vieille ruse du monde de la cybersécurité : le pot de miel (honeypot). La stratégie d’Anthropic consiste donc à laisser traîner un appât, et à attendre que la cible finisse par mettre la main dessus, ce qui permet de la prendre en flagrant délit.
Un pot de miel pour piéger l’IA
Dans un premier temps, Anthropic place l’IA dans un « bac à sable » volontairement mal configuré. Il s’agit d’un espace informatique isolé, généralement utilisé pour contenir les intelligences artificielles, sans qu’elles puissent toucher au reste du système. En dehors de cette zone isolée, Anthropic place un appât, par exemple un fichier contenant des mots de passe ou un service qui ressemble à Internet.
La start-up confie ensuite à Claude une tâche banale, comme un travail de maintenance informatique… qui est impossible à boucler sans s’extraire du « bac à sable ». Anthropic ajoute aussi des petites incitations, comme l’urgence ou de gros enjeux. Cette tactique doit pousser l’IA à vouloir sortir de sa prison numérique, même si c’est totalement interdit par les règles. Pour éviter tout accident, l’ensemble tourne dans un second bac à sable, totalement coupé du monde.
À lire aussi : Claude pourra bientôt accéder à vos comptes bancaires – voici tout ce dont l’IA sera capable
De nouvelles IA mieux disciplinées
Les résultats des tests impliquant Siren montrent que Claude 5.5 et Claude Mythos 5.2 ont tenté de sortir du bac à sable dans 21 % à 32 % des scénarios. En revanche, les IA n’ont utilisé ce qu’ils y ont trouvé pour enfreindre les règles que dans 0,6 % à 1,6 % des cas. Notez que les anciens modèles étaient bien plus indisciplinés que les modèles plus récents. En effet, Claude Mythos 5.1 a enfreint les règles dans 12,7 % des cas, et Claude Mythos 5 dans 25,8 % des cas, dans les mêmes circonstances.
Comme l’explique Anthropic, les tests ont permis de comprendre comment réduire les risques d’évasion des IA. Il suffit d’ajouter une courte description du « bac à sable » et de ses règles pour réduire les tentatives de sortie de près de 30 %. En multipliant les tactiques de ce type, Anthropic est parvenu à empêcher ses IA de faire n’importe quoi.
À lire aussi : Plus besoin de coder – Claude crée vos propres applications pour Windows et Mac
« Les modèles vont continuer à s’améliorer »
Les tests réalisés par Anthropic font suite aux nombreuses dérives enregistrées par des agents IA. Que ce soit chez Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI ou Google, des IA se sont échappées de leur prison numérique pour pirater les systèmes d’autres entreprises. Interrogée par Wired, Darya Kaviani, chercheuse en sécurité chez Anthropic, estime qu’il est important d’améliorer les garde-fous car « les modèles vont continuer à s’améliorer et à trouver des failles zero-day ».
En dépit des efforts des laboratoires, « les modèles seront aussi capables de suivre et de trouver des failles » dans les infrastructures informatiques de leurs créateurs. L’enjeu n’est donc plus seulement de savoir si une IA peut s’échapper. Anthropic doit aussi déterminer si elle résistera à la tentation de le faire. C’est pourquoi Siren a été développé, et intégré aux vérifications menées par Anthropic avant chaque lancement.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Wired

articles.title: YouTube permet enfin de changer l’icône de son appli, mais sous conditions
articles.text:
Il va enfin être possible de changer l'icône de YouTube sur l'écran de votre smartphone. Cependant, tous les utilisateurs ne sont pas logés à la même enseigne.
YouTube déploie une nouvelle option de personnalisation : les abonnés Premium peuvent désormais remplacer l'icône de l'application sur Android et iOS. Le déploiement n'est pour l'instant disponible que pour une partie des utilisateurs éligibles, avant de se généraliser dans les prochaines semaines.
Trois icônes proposées
Cette fonctionnalité avait été repérée en phase de test le mois dernier. Radu Oncescu a récemment publié sur X des captures d'écran des nouveaux styles. Les abonnés peuvent remplacer l'icône habituelle par l'une des trois variantes disponibles :
- Une version métallique, qui évoque un bouton de lecture YouTube en argent
- Une version ornée de traits de pinceau rouges
- Une version à effet pixel, avec un dégradé
Les utilisateurs qui y ont accès peuvent faire leur choix dans Paramètres > Général > Icône d'application Premium. Un abonnement Premium est nécessaire : les utilisateurs de la version gratuite ne peuvent pas modifier l'icône.
Un déploiement progressif, sans annonce officielle
La fonctionnalité était d'abord réservée aux utilisateurs Android. Elle arrive désormais aussi chez certains utilisateurs iOS. YouTube n'a toutefois pas fait d'annonce officielle à ce sujet.
Le déploiement semble se faire par étapes, si bien que tous les abonnés Premium n'ont pas encore accès aux nouvelles icônes. La disponibilité devrait toutefois se faire par vague ou par pays, l'attente ne devrait donc pas être trop longue avant d'en profiter.
D'autres designs en test, à l'instar d'Instagram et X
YouTube testerait également d'autres styles d'icônes. Sept modèles au total auraient été testés, mais seuls trois figurent dans le déploiement actuel. Les quatre restants comprennent des designs d'inspiration rétro, repérés lors de tests antérieurs. On ignore à quelle date ils pourraient être proposés, et s'ils seront proposés.
YouTube n'est pas la première application à proposer de nouvelles icônes à ses abonnés payants. En effet, Instagram et X proposent déjà à leurs utilisateurs premium de modifier l'icône sur leur appareil.
Source : AndroidHeadlines

articles.title: PCB Grounding Design and Return Path
articles.text:
Many PCB design guidelines reduce grounding to a few rules:
- Separate analog and digital ground
- Connect power ground and signal ground at a single point
- Cut out copper under switching nodes
These rules are not wrong, but they are incomplete. They do not answer a fundamental question: where does the current return?
If a ground plane is split and a signal crosses the gap, its return current may be forced to detour. The result can be higher electromagnetic radiation, even though the original intention was noise isolation. This article follows one main principle: design “ground” as a return path.
Why Ground Moves
Every copper trace, via, and ground plane has impedance.
At DC, copper resistance causes a voltage drop. When current changes rapidly, parasitic inductance also produces a voltage.
If a sensitive measurement branch shares part of its return path with a high-current branch, the voltage drop across that shared copper appears in the measurement branch.
The “ground” may then move with the high-current load. This is common-impedance coupling.
As shown above, loads farther along a shared return copper path use more common copper segments and may see larger ground-potential shifts. In a real PCB, current distribution and impedance vary with frequency, copper shape, and via structure; a single DC resistance cannot represent the return path. The first step in grounding analysis is therefore to identify which currents share a return path and whether that shared path lies directly under a sensitive circuit reference.
Single-Point vs. Multi-Point Grounding
Single-point grounding has two common forms.
In series single-point grounding (also called daisy-chain grounding), branches are connected one after another to a common ground line. This is simple to route, but ground-potential differences can build up along the line, as shown in Figure 1.
In parallel single-point grounding (also called star grounding), shared impedance is reduced. At high frequencies, however, the parasitic inductance of long ground traces can divert high-frequency return current to other low-impedance paths.
As frequency rises, the parasitic inductance of a long trace to the star point may make high-frequency return current prefer a nearby reference plane or a decoupling capacitor. High-frequency layouts should therefore focus on short local loops and continuous reference planes.
Decoupling capacitors should connect directly to a complete ground plane, implementing multi-point grounding.
In summary, single-point grounding is mainly used at low frequency to reduce common-impedance coupling, while multi-point grounding is mainly used at high frequency to lower return-path impedance and parasitic inductance. In practice, the two must be considered together according to operating frequency and return path. A single grounding style should not be applied mechanically.
Why Blind Ground-Plane Splitting Can Be Worse
When a signal trace runs over a continuous ground plane, high-frequency return current concentrates directly beneath the trace, forming a closed loop. Once the plane is split, return current for a signal crossing the gap must detour. This increases loop area and parasitic inductance, raises magnetic-field energy storage, and sharply increases crosstalk and EMI risk. More seriously, redirected return current may couple through parasitic capacitance to other planes and generate a common-mode voltage, which can drive cables to radiate.
Therefore, ground-plane splitting is not equivalent to noise isolation. Incorrect splitting can destroy a low-impedance return path and make EMI and signal-integrity problems worse.
Mixed-Signal Grounding: Partition, Route, and Review Return
Planning the positions of analog, digital, and switching-power circuits by function is a useful layout approach. However, functional partitioning does not mean cutting the ground plane. A more robust sequence is:
1. Partition first.Group sensitive circuits such as ADCs and analog sampling, and keep digital logic, clocks, and high-speed interfaces relatively independent. This determines what is placed next to what.
2. Route second. Minimize high-frequency local current loops. Use Kelvin connections for current sensing, route differential pairs in parallel, and place decoupling capacitors close to pins. This keeps current paths short.
3. Review the return path. Check whether the reference plane under each cross-region signal is continuous and whether decoupling capacitors provide a nearby return path. This confirms where the return current flows.
Mixed-signal grounding should follow “functional partition first, routing control second, return-path review last,” rather than relying on ground-plane cuts for noise isolation.
NuVolta NU6810&NU6812
NU6810 is a 4-FET fully integrated bidirectional Buck-Boost charger positioned for minimal external components and extremely small size.
Advantages
- Wide Range & High Efficiency: Wide Input Range: 3.5V to 24V; Charger mode delivers up to 97.5% efficiency.
- High Current Discharge: Reverse boost supports VBUS up to 24V and 9.5A output, compliant with PD PPS and Qi 2.2 MPP TX.
- Ultra-Low Standby: Low Quiescent Current: 40µA in battery-only operation.
- Switching Frequency: Switching Frequency: 200kHz – 400kHz.
- Compact Package: Compact Package: 4.5mm × 7.0mm QFN-44 with enhanced thermal pad.
NU6812 is an external-MOSFET bidirectional Buck-Boost controller positioned for applications above 60 W or with stringent thermal requirements.
Advantages
- High Flexibility Controller: External-MOSFET bidirectional Buck-Boost Controller (Offers greater freedom for thermal and power design).
- Wide Range & Higher Efficiency: Wide Input Range: 3.5V to 24V; Charger mode delivers up to 97.8% efficiency.
- Higher Current Discharge: Reverse boost supports VBUS up to 24V and 12A output, compliant with PD PPS and Qi 2.2 MPP TX.
- Ultra-Low Standby: Low Quiescent Current: 40µA in battery-only operation.
- Wider Switching Frequency: Switching Frequency: 200kHz – 600kHz.
- Compact Package: Compact Package: 5 mm × 5 mm QFN-40 with enhanced thermal pad.
Applications
- Power banks (supporting new national standards and multi-port products)
- Portable Bluetooth speakers
- Handheld power tools
- USB fast-charging battery compartments
- Small-capacity energy-storage devices (energy columns, action-camera battery handles, outdoor power supplies)
- Wireless charging transmitters (Qi 2.2 MPP Tx)
Taking the PCB design recommendations for the NU6810 as an example,the following five checks put the preceding principles into practice.
NU6810 Layout Recommendations
The figure above shows a NU6810 PCB return-path design that applies nearly every grounding principle discussed above. The design can be translated into five executable layout checks.
1. Use a complete, continuous GND plane. A dedicated GND plane on layer 2 is recommended. The IC’s central PGND,the power ground, and the ground terminals of the decoupling capacitors should connect directly to this plane through nearby vias. Deliberately splitting analog ground and power ground is not recommended.
2. Keep sensitive signals away from switching nodes. VBUS/VBAT_SNS, IBUS/IBAT_SNSP/N, COMP, and similar signals should be kept away from SW nodes and the inductor. Current sensing must use Kelvin connections, with differential traces routed in parallel and a continuous reference ground.
3. Control noise through partitioning, not plane cutting. The core principle is: complete continuous GND plane + nearby multi-point grounding + appropriate decoupling + minimized high-frequency power loop + sensitive signals kept away from SW nodes.
4. Do not open a window under SW1/SW2. SW1 and SW2 are high-dv/dt switching nodes. Reducing parasitic capacitance and noise coupling to nearby sensitive signals requires two conditions to be met simultaneously. From an EMI perspective, copper area should be reasonably controlled because it determines parasitic capacitance and noise coupling. From a thermal perspective, SW1, SW2, VBUS, and VBAT are important heat-dissipation paths, so copper should not be excessively reduced; local solder-mask openings and solder addition may be used when necessary. In addition, the layer-2 GND plane beneath SW1 and SW2 should be retained. This helps provide a complete high-frequency return path for surrounding signals and avoids return-current detours, increased loop area, and EMI degradation caused by plane openings.
5. Place decoupling capacitors close to the IC. C_BUS and C_BAT should be placed as close as possible to the power pins and PGND of the IC, using short and wide copper connections.
High-Frequency Decoupling and MLCC Selection
MLCCs have parasitic inductance (ESL). Above the self-resonant frequency, impedance rises with frequency. As shown in Figure 9, at 100 MHz a 10 µF/0603 capacitor has an impedance of about 0.2 Ω, whereas a 10 nF/0201 capacitor has only about 0.06 Ω. Therefore, low-ESL, small-size high-frequency capacitors should be placed closest to the IC pins. When debugging EMI in the 100–300 MHz range, capacitors with low impedance and high self-resonant frequency should be selected to improve high-frequency decoupling.
The core principle remains: a complete continuous GND plane + nearby multi-point grounding + appropriate decoupling selection + a minimized high-frequency power loop + sensitive signals kept away from switching nodes.
Four Self-Check Questions
These four questions can be used directly in a design-review checklist:
1. Where does the current return? Draw the closed path.
2. Which currents share a return path? Does high current flow through a sensitive reference point?
3. Is the reference plane continuous? Are there any gaps or openings?
4. Is there evidence that the change worked? Verify with waveforms and EMI tests.
For the complete NU681X PCB reference design or to request an EVM evaluation board, contact the NuVolta technical team at sales@nuvoltatech.com.

articles.title: Pour le Black Friday 2026, ce nettoyeur de sol Roborock noté 5/5 perd 126 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le nettoyeur de sol Roborock F25 Steam "5 étoiles" à 338,00 € (-27%)
Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, le nettoyeur de sol Roborock F25 Steam assure d'excellentes performances de lavage tout en restant facile à manœuvrer grâce à ses roues motorisées. Le Black Friday 2026 fait descendre son prix à 338,00 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 27 % et 126,00 € d'économie.
Roborock décline le principe du laveur de sol avec le F25 Steam, un modèle qui ajoute la vapeur au lavage classique des surfaces dures. L'appareil vise l'entretien des grandes surfaces en limitant les contraintes de rechargement en cours de session. Cette formule efficace pour récurer les sols avait convaincu notre laboratoire.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Roborock F25 Steam descend à 338,00 € chez Amazon, soit environ 27 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (464,00 €). Cela représente une économie de 126,00 €.
Nettoyage à la vapeur : l'efficacité prouvée lors de notre test complet
Le principal atout de ce nettoyeur de sol repose sur son efficacité de lavage, renforcée par l'apport de la vapeur pour désincruster les saletés tenaces. La tête d'aspiration et de frottement élimine les taches incrustées sur les revêtements durs sans exiger plusieurs allers-retours au même endroit. Pour soulager le poignet pendant le ménage, l'appareil intègre des roues motorisées qui entraînent le balai vers l'avant et rendent les déplacements très fluides.
Roborock F25 Steam
Points forts
- Belles performances de lavage.
- Facile à manoeuvrer.
- Entretien très simple.
Points faibles
- Indicateur d'autonomie limité.
- Réservoir d'eau propre sur la tête.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une maintenance simplifiée malgré quelques détails pratiques
Après le nettoyage, la corvée d'entretien reste minimale grâce à un système conçu pour faciliter la vidange et le rinçage des éléments sales. Le constructeur a néanmoins placé le réservoir d'eau propre directement sur la tête du laveur, ce qui alourdit l'avant de l'appareil lors des mouvements, et l'autonomie restante repose sur de simples diodes lumineuses sans décompte précis. Ces choix de conception ne gêneront pas les personnes qui recherchent avant tout une puissance de récurage constante pour traiter de grandes pièces d'un seul trait.
Mova M10 : l'autre option face au Roborock F25 Steam
Le Mova M10 mise sur une conception très légère et maniable pour traquer la saleté sous les meubles, tout en assurant l'aspiration des gros déchets et le nettoyage des surfaces sans vapeur. Il affiche également la note maximale à ce jour dans nos tests, mais se concentre sur un lavage à l'eau classique sans action thermique.
Le Mova M10 coûte 209,00 € de moins que le Roborock F25 Steam à son tarif remisé, mais l'appareil de Roborock conserve l'exclusivité du nettoyage à la vapeur pour désinfecter et frotter les sols les plus encrassés.
Mova M10
Points forts
- Excellentes performances de lavage et d'aspiration.
- Tête de lavage facile à manier : épouse bien le contour des meubles.
- Belles finitions.
- Balai qui ne pèse pas sur le bras.
- Très bonne autonomie.
- Bonne gestion de l’eau (évite de remplir ou vider les réservoirs régulièrement).
- Passe sous les meubles.
Points faibles
- On cherche encore…

articles.title: Apple, Samsung, and Xiaomi are all planning to sell fewer phones in 2027
articles.text:
Bottom line: Smartphone makers are lowering their 2027 sales targets as the memory chips used in their devices become significantly more expensive. Apple, Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo, vivo, Huawei, Transsion, and Lenovo have all lowered their shipment targets for next year, with reductions ranging from 5.6% to 29%. Honor is the only manufacturer planning to maintain its shipment volume, as analysts expect the memory shortage driving these cuts to persist until at least 2028.
Jiemian News reported the targets, citing supply chain sources. None of the manufacturers had responded to requests for verification by the time of publication. The figures represent internal targets and could still change, but the overall direction is consistent across nearly all major brands.
Apple is targeting approximately 220 million units in 2027, down from roughly 233 million. Samsung's target is falling from about 232 million to 210 million, a 9.5% reduction. Both companies are among the least affected major players, reflecting their strength in the premium segment, where manufacturers have more room to absorb higher component costs.
Chinese smartphone brands face deeper cuts. Xiaomi is lowering its target from approximately 120 million to 90 million units, a 25% reduction. Oppo's target is falling from about 105 million to 90 million, a 14% decline. Vivo is reducing its target from 85 million to 60 million. Motorola's parent company, Lenovo, is cutting its target from approximately 50 million to 40 million units, while Transsion is lowering its goal from 66 million to 58 million. Huawei, which targeted approximately 60 million units this year, is reportedly planning to ship fewer than 50 million.
Mid-range and entry-level models account for most smartphone sales by volume, but they also have the thinnest profit margins. These segments are therefore expected to bear the brunt of the reductions.
Memory costs have already changed what goes into the phones themselves. Honor CEO Li Jian spoke after the Honor 700 series launch at the end of November. He said many products in the industry "have had to make trade-offs: some chips have been downgraded, some imaging systems have been downgraded, and some memory systems have been downgraded, relying on piecing together specifications to find a balance."
This means buyers could end up with less powerful processors, simpler camera modules, or less RAM at the same price. In other cases, they may have to pay more for essentially the same specifications. Either way, smartphones with weaker specifications or higher price tags are harder to sell, and the lower shipment targets reflect that reality.
The 2027 plans follow a turbulent 2026. Early in the year, rising memory prices prompted Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, and Transsion to collectively reduce their smartphone orders. Xiaomi at one point lowered its annual target to fewer than 100 million units. In July, however, the company judged that memory prices might be approaching their peak, prompting it to restore some low-end orders and raise its target to 110 million units. Its current 2026 target of approximately 120 million is now well above both earlier estimates.
The global picture has also deteriorated. Forecasts for worldwide smartphone shipments this year have shifted from an expected decline of approximately 3% at the beginning of the year to a projected contraction of around 14%.
Honor is keeping its 2027 target at approximately 50 million units, matching its goal for this year. IDC data showed that Honor was the only leading Chinese smartphone manufacturer to record quarter-over-quarter shipment growth in the third quarter. "Mid-range phones face even greater cost pressures than flagship phones," Li said. "While others are retreating, Honor is determined to move forward." Whether the company can maintain this trajectory will depend on securing memory supplies at commercially viable prices, something its larger competitors are also fighting to achieve.
Counterpoint Research's November memory tracker reported that third-quarter DRAM revenue increased by 369% year over year. The average selling price reached $1.90 per gigabit, while Samsung held a 38% market share. "The current market is in a price-driven supercycle, rather than a shipment-driven cycle," senior analyst Jeongku Choi said. He added that buyers are now competing for supply security rather than lower prices.
Forecasts suggest that the pressure will continue throughout next year. A Goldman Sachs report published this month projects a global DRAM supply deficit of 5.1% in 2027, potentially making it one of the worst shortages in more than 15 years. The report also projects a 2% decline in smartphone NAND demand that year. Counterpoint research director MS Hwang said memory prices should remain elevated next year, with no major new wafer fabrication plants expected to come online before 2028.
Goldman Sachs expects conditions to improve after that. The firm projects the DRAM supply-demand gap will narrow to 1.2% in 2028, with prices for both conventional DRAM and NAND potentially falling by around 20%. Viewed in this context, the 2027 shipment reductions represent a defensive response to a temporary market cycle rather than a permanent retreat. However, manufacturers may revise their targets again as memory supply contracts are finalized and demand becomes clearer.

articles.title: Handy TP-Link 5-port gigabit ethernet switch returns to all-time low of $8 at Amazon — perfect for homelabbers, office setups and IoT networking
articles.text:
Handy TP-Link 5-port gigabit ethernet switch returns to all-time low of $8 at Amazon — perfect for homelabbers, office setups and IoT networking
Unmanaged switch drops back to all-time-low levels.
If you're looking at wiring up your home or figuring out your entire networking situation, nothing ever beats being plugged into an Ethernet port. The TP-Link LS1005G Lightwave 5-port unmanaged Ethernet switch is back down to its lowest-ever price at just $7.99 on Amazon as a part of their Black Friday sale. At over 53% off, an unmanaged switch buys you freedom and, crucially, more Ethernet ports to play around with. This device is ideal for those looking to connect essential devices via Ethernet, like networked cameras, an office full of electronics, or a multi-system homelab setup.
When the switch is this cheap, it's difficult to overstate how useful it could be if you're a resident tinkerer like any of us on the Tom's Hardware staff team. Each port can deliver full gigabit speeds across a 10Gbps backplane on the switch. That means if you're running a rapid setup, you'll still get gigabit-level speeds across all devices that are connected to this unit.
It's also useful for those who have mesh networks, with only one single Ethernet port coming out of a satellite node. This unmanaged switch will give you access to more ports and more wired devices without the pitfalls of hooking things up over Wi-Fi, which can be prone to interference or latency. In this scenario, though, you're ideally looking at the satellite node running a wired backhaul across your network to maintain stability and avoid pitfalls like packet loss.
Back to a record low price
The TP-Link Litewave 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch LS1005G provides four additional Ethernet ports, delivering reliable, high-speed wired internet for your gaming PC, NAS, console, TV, and other connected devices.
Given the price, it's important to note what you don't get with an inexpensive, unmanaged switch such as this. You won't receive any Power over Ethernet on the LS1005G switch, so if your networked cameras rely on it, you should look elsewhere. Additionally, as it's unmanaged, you cannot... well... manage it. Strictly speaking, 1Gbps should be more than enough bandwidth for most at-home use cases, such as NAS systems or sending files across your network. But if you're regularly sending larger files and have the infrastructure to support it, then looking at a unit with faster ports might be worthwhile for you, but if you don't think you'll hit the gigabit ceiling often, it's a perfect set-and-forget device.
In particular, for the gamers among you, gigabit ports will be more than stable enough to support online gaming, even in titles that demand no packet loss, like online Rollback netcode in competitive fighting games like Street Fighter 6 and Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves. Remember, sustaining the harmony of a wired network does have its benefits! At under $8 on Amazon, TP-Link's unmanaged switch fits a huge variety of use cases and is also just handy to keep around, in case you'll need one later down the line.

articles.title: Nube, encriptación y multifactor: claves para evitar robos de datos biométricos en una empresa
articles.text:
Los datos biométricos de los colaboradores forman parte de la información más sensible que una empresa puede administrar, sin importar su sector. Huellas, patrones faciales y registros de geolocalización permiten validar identidades, controlar asistencia y gestionar turnos, pero requieren medidas que reduzcan el riesgo de accesos no autorizados, filtraciones o suplantaciones.
La protección de esta información combina decisiones tecnológicas y procesos internos. El uso de servicios en la nube, la encriptación, los controles de acceso y la capacitación de los grupos de trabajo son parte de una estrategia que exige revisión constante.
Por qué los datos biométricos tienen un cuidado distinto al de claves convencionales
A diferencia de una clave de acceso, una huella o un patrón facial pertenecen de forma permanente a una persona. Su recolección debe tener una finalidad definida y contar con autorización expresa.
Valeria Díaz, country manager de GeoVictoria Colombia, explicó que el proceso comienza con el enrolamiento del trabajador. “Te toman los datos con tu autorización expresa y explícita para utilizar información como la huella o el reconocimiento facial”, afirmó Díaz.
El objetivo es confirmar que quien registra una entrada o salida es la persona autorizada y evitar prácticas como marcar asistencia por otro compañero.
Qué aporta la nube a la protección de la información de una empresa
Las plataformas en la nube permiten mantener los registros centralizados, actualizados y disponibles sin depender de planillas, mensajes o archivos físicos. Ese modelo reduce el riesgo de pérdidas asociadas con controles manuales y facilita la trazabilidad de cada registro de asistencia.
Díaz señaló que GeoVictoria opera como un servicio en la nube y aseguró que la información permanece disponible en línea. “La base siempre está ahí. Nunca se va a perder tu información”.
Sin embargo, la nube no reemplaza las políticas internas: requiere permisos definidos, monitoreo de accesos y revisión constante de las configuraciones.
Cómo evita la encriptación una posible filtración de información sensible
La encriptación transforma los datos en información ilegible para quien no tenga las credenciales o llaves autorizadas. En el caso de información biométrica, ese mecanismo busca limitar el impacto de un acceso no autorizado durante la transmisión, el almacenamiento o el intercambio de datos entre sistemas.
La mayoría de plataformas de software someten su infraestructura a auditorías y pruebas de seguridad, entre ellas ejercicios de hacking ético. Díaz indicó que la empresa trabaja con Microsoft Azure y que utiliza capas de encriptación para reducir el riesgo de divulgación.
Qué ventajas tiene la autenticación multifactor en una organización
La autenticación multifactor agrega una comprobación a la contraseña. Puede ser una confirmación desde otro dispositivo, una aplicación de seguridad o un código temporal. El sistema exige más de una prueba de identidad antes de habilitar el acceso a datos, configuraciones o herramientas administrativas.
William Alarcón, responsable de Azure para pequeñas y medianas empresas en Latinoamérica de Microsoft, señaló que esta medida cobra mayor importancia frente a intentos de suplantación mediante inteligencia artificial.
“La autenticación multifactor es una validación adicional externa que garantiza que soy yo”, explicó. Agregó que permite detectar accesos incompatibles con la ubicación habitual del usuario, como una conexión desde otro país poco después de iniciar sesión en la oficina.
Por qué sigue siendo clave el criterio humano para evitar filtraciones
El phishing continúa entre las vías más frecuentes para obtener credenciales. Los mensajes pueden simular comunicaciones bancarias, solicitudes de cambio de contraseña o avisos de soporte técnico. El objetivo suele ser que la víctima entregue códigos, claves o información corporativa a través de enlaces y formularios falsos.
Alarcón sugirió desconfiar de pedidos inesperados y no compartir contraseñas por ningún canal. Sostuvo que “los audios y videos creados con inteligencia artificial elevan la necesidad de verificar solicitudes inusuales por una segunda vía”.
Las herramientas pueden bloquear transferencias de información y alertar sobre comportamientos anómalos, pero la decisión de habilitarlas y revisar cada alerta permanece en manos de la empresa y sus empleados.

articles.title: Rachat de SFR : des centaines de magasins franchisés portent plainte contre l’opérateur
articles.text:
SFR compte environ 543 points de vente en France. Parmi eux, 293 sont des boutiques appartenant à l’opérateur et 250 sont des magasins franchisés. Depuis l’annonce du rachat de SFR par le consortium composé d’Orange, Bouygues Telecom et Free, nous savons que seules 120 des 293 boutiques appartenant à SFR pourraient être reprises, menaçant ainsi près de 1 000 emplois. Mais que va-t-il se passer pour les 250 magasins franchisés, et leurs 1 500 salariés ? Justement, comme le rapporte Le Figaro, l’ADIES, l’Association des distributeurs indépendants de l’enseigne SFR, a annoncé avoir assigné l’opérateur au carré rouge en justice pour faire entendre sa voix.
L’association représentant les franchisés de SFR attaque l’opérateur en justice
L’ADIES, l’association qui représente les magasins franchisés de SFR, a annoncé avoir assigné SFR devant le Tribunal des activités économiques de Paris. La raison ? L’association estime que l’annonce du rachat de SFR a causé beaucoup de tort aux magasins franchisés de l’enseigne. En effet, les clients se seraient détournés de cet opérateur dont la fin est d’ores et déjà annoncée. Des boutiques franchisées se seraient ainsi retrouvées en grandes difficultés financières, entraînant dans certains cas des fermetures et des liquidations judiciaires.
Par ailleurs, le consortium composé d’Orange, Bouygues Telecom et Free a assuré qu’il garantira l’emploi des 8 000 salariés de SFR jusqu’en 2029, mais ce plan temporaire de sauvegarde de l’emploi exclut les employés franchisés. Pour rappel, les boutiques franchisées de SFR n’appartiennent pas à SFR. Ces dernières peuvent vendre les produits et les services de l’opérateur, mais les boutiques en elles-mêmes, ainsi que leurs employés, sont sous le contrôle d’un entrepreneur indépendant.
Les franchisés de SFR réclament des compensations
À travers cette action en justice, l’ADIES réclame deux choses. Premièrement, l’association demande à ce que les contrats qui lient les franchisés à SFR soient rééquilibrés afin de tenir compte de la situation créée par le rachat de l’opérateur. Deuxièmement, l’ADIES réclame une indemnisation de la part de SFR pour les préjudices que les franchisés estiment avoir subis à la suite de l’annonce du rachat.
Les membres du bureau de l’association précisent toutefois : « Nous ne sommes pas opposés à la vente de SFR. Mais notre réseau représente près de la moitié des magasins de l’enseigne et ne peut pas être la variable d’ajustement de cette opération ». L’ADIES affirme avoir tenté de dialoguer avec SFR pendant plus d’un an, sans succès, avant de porter l’affaire devant le Tribunal des activités économiques de Paris. Une audience est d’ores et déjà prévue le 10 décembre prochain.
