articles.title: Iker, ingeniero español trabajando en Suiza: "Decidí irme de España y cobraba 50.000 € al año; el ahorro que puedo tener es mayor al que tenía allí"
articles.text:
Iker es ingeniero de software, tiene tres años de experiencia y en España cobraba 50.000 euros brutos al año. No era precisamente un mal sueldo, pero aun así decidió dejar su trabajo y marcharse a Suiza. ¿El motivo? Quería mejorar sus condiciones económicas, aunque también había otras cosas de su vida en España que no terminaban de convencerle.
"No voy a ser hipócrita, evidentemente el factor salarial fue algo bastante importante", reconoce en un vídeo de su cuenta de TikTok (@ikerdiazj), del que también se ha hecho eco El Confidencial. Iker sabía que Suiza era un país caro, pero al hacer cuentas vio que podía salir ganando. "A nivel porcentual el ahorro que puedo tener yo aquí, a pesar de los costes tan altos que hay, es mucho mayor al que yo tenía en España", explica.
El sueldo no fue lo único que le hizo marcharse
Al dinero se sumaba otra preocupación: la seguridad y la calidad de los servicios. Iker considera que ambos aspectos se habían deteriorado en España y tampoco quería quedarse únicamente por tener un salario que muchos considerarían bastante bueno.
Además, había un motivo relacionado directamente con su profesión. Como ingeniero de software, quería participar en proyectos tecnológicos que no encontraba en España. "A nivel tecnológico, en mi sector hay proyectos y empresas muy interesantes que no están en España", comenta al explicar qué le convenció para dar el paso.
Su caso tiene una particularidad: no se marchó porque estuviera desempleado ni porque cobrara el salario mínimo. Tenía un puesto bien remunerado, pero prefería probar suerte en otro mercado. Eso sí, Iker habla de su capacidad de ahorro personal, sin detallar una cifra mensual que permita comparar exactamente cuánto dinero le quedaba antes y cuánto consigue guardar ahora.

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir : pourquoi Sauron a-t-il pris cette décision surprise à la fin de la saison 3 ?
articles.text:
Celles et ceux qui ont lu ou vu Le Seigneur des anneaux le savent très bien : Sauron finit par dominer une bonne partie de la Terre du Milieu, jusqu’à ce qu’une petite bande de hobbits, aidés par d’autres peuples libres, monte une expédition courageuse au Mordor. Objectif : détruire l’Anneau unique, d’où le seigneur des ténèbres tire l’essentiel de son pouvoir.
Cela laisse peu d’options aux scénaristes de la série préquelle Les Anneaux de pouvoir. Comment, en effet, surprendre le public alors que l’on connait la destinée de la Terre du Milieu ? Heureusement, la série d’Amazon Studios peut miser sur les appendices laissés par Tolkien, afin de raconter des pans méconnus du récit.
En l’espèce, la saison 3 des Anneaux de pouvoir a donc misé sur la forge de l’Anneau unique. Logique : on savait que la série allait tôt ou tard en parler, et on vient de dépasser la moitié de l’aventure – la série a été pensée dès le départ en cinq saisons, il n’en reste donc plus que deux avant de clore cette production. Il fallait que ce grand tournant scénaristique arrive.
Or, dans le final de la saison 3, le seigneur des ténèbres fait un choix qui a de quoi surprendre les spectateurs et spectatrices, alors même qu’il a enfin l’arme ultime au doigt. Au lieu de débrider sa puissance nouvelle pour briser toute résistance face à lui, il adopte une toute autre stratégie. Est-ce qu’il s’agit d’une nouvelle liberté prise par les showrunners ?
Attention, la suite contient des spoilers.
Pourquoi Sauron choisit-il de se rendre à la fin de la saison 3 des Anneaux de pouvoir ?
Face à l’armée de Númenor, donc, Sauron fait le choix de retirer l’Anneau qu’il porte (alors même qu’il l’a obtenu de haute lutte, après bien des échecs à la forge), traverse seul le champ de bataille pour finir par s’agenouiller devant le roi Ar-Pharazôn. Ce dernier, ivre de sa puissance et de la soumission de son ennemi, rit aux éclats.
Le geste de Sauron prépare en réalité la chute de Númenor, que racontera la saison 4.
Pourquoi se rendre quand on porte l’artefact le plus puissant de la Terre du Milieu ? Patrick McKay et J.D. Payne, les deux showrunners de la série, ont répondu dans une interview à TV Insider publiée après la diffusion du final de la saison. Selon McKay, Sauron fait ses calculs, et va bientôt commencer à tirer les bénéfices de son influence sur Númenor.
Sauron considère en effet qu’une bataille pourrait être risquée, même avec sa horde d’orques et l’Anneau unique. Il risque au mieux une victoire à la Pyrrhus, si coûteuse qu’elle l’affaiblirait, et au pire une impasse. Il accepte donc de perdre la bataille pour gagner la guerre. Il recule pour mieux sauter, ce qui causera la destruction totale de Númenor.
Payne va plus loin : « Pourquoi détruire son ennemi quand on peut le récupérer, et peut-être le corrompre ? » Il rappelle que Sauron a déjà croisé Pharazôn à Númenor dans la saison 1, et qu’il sait à quel point le roi est corruptible, imbu de lui-même et calculateur. Sauron sait qu’il a l’occasion de triompher sans combattre, ce qui serait la victoire parfaite.
La scène se termine d’ailleurs sur un plan du visage de Sauron filmé depuis le sol. Lui seul « voit » ce que les autres ne voient pas, et il en sourit.
Une reddition tout droit sortie de Tolkien
Ce coup de théâtre est écrit noir sur blanc chez Tolkien. L’Akallabêth, le récit de la chute de l’île de Númenor publié en 1977 dans Le Silmarillion, raconte qu’Ar-Pharazôn débarque en Terre du Milieu avec une flotte si puissante que les serviteurs de Sauron l’abandonnent. Sauron vient alors s’humilier devant lui, en se jetant pratiquement à ses pieds.
Il se laisse emmener à Númenor comme otage et devient en peu de temps le principal conseiller du roi. Il le pousse ensuite à vénérer Melkor, l’ancien maître de Sauron, puis à envoyer sa flotte contre les terres des Valar, les puissances divines du monde de Tolkien, pour leur arracher l’immortalité. À la fin, en représailles, l’île est engloutie par la mer.
La série reprend cette mécanique presque à l’identique. Plus tôt dans l’épisode, la mort du mage Pallando a fait fuir ses fidèles et les hommes du Rhûn, et Sauron a perdu l’avantage du nombre. Pharazôn, lui, affichait ses ambitions dès la bande-annonce de la saison 3, où il lançait « Je viens anéantir un dieu ».
En outre, Pharazôn a écrit un ultimatum à Sauron pour le défier et affirmer que le seul « roi des Hommes » règne à Númenor, et qu’il ferait mieux de retourner ramper comme un ver au Mordor. Le retrait du Rhûn de l’équation et la puissance complète de Númenor ont changé les paramètres, et Sauron a donc ajusté son plan sur le moment.
Que faire d’un demi-dieu qui se rend ?
Pourquoi les Elfes et les Hommes ne l’achèvent-ils pas sur place ? « On ne peut pas le tuer », répond simplement McKay. Payne rappelle que Sauron fait partie des Maiar, des esprits presque divins. La série l’a d’ailleurs montré : quand des orques l’ont tué, il est revenu sous la forme d’une masse visqueuse noire, avant de reprendre corps.
Patrick McKay laisse entendre que la saison 4 pourrait tout à fait débuter avec ce problème : que faire d’un demi-dieu qui s’est rendu à des hommes par nature mortels. De leur côté, les Elfes présents (Galadriel, Celeborn, Gil-galad et Elrond) n’ont en tout cas pas cru à sa reddition, si l’on se fie à leur mine circonspecte.

articles.title: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts
articles.text:
The pCloud Pass password manager suffered a cyberattack, with users reporting that unknown devices had connected to their accounts even with two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled.
The incident was first reported by numerous pCloud customers who began receiving email notifications informing them that a new device had connected to their pCloud Pass accounts.
In two Reddit threads, customers worldwide reported receiving notifications warning that an unfamiliar device named "pd" connected to their account from the IP address 45.131.244.7 in Luxembourg, which users say belongs to pCloud's own infrastructure.
Several customers reported receiving the alerts despite having two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled on their accounts. However, when customers checked their accounts for connected devices, some found no unfamiliar devices listed.
Other pCloud customers reported receiving the same notifications despite never having used the company's password manager, including one who said the notification was sent to an email address associated with a pCloud storage account they had requested be deleted almost a year ago.
In response to the reports, pCloud confirmed its password manager had suffered a cyberattack, which the company says was quickly contained.
"A cyberattack targeting pCloud Pass occurred, which was promptly contained by the pCloud team," reads pCloud's statement.
"Unfortunately, a small number of pCloud Pass user email addresses were exposed and login attempts were made. Our system sends a notification automatically to each of these addresses."
pCloud says the attack was isolated to its password manager and that its cloud storage services were not affected.
The company says that passwords, notes, and other information stored in pCloud Pass have not been compromised, explaining that the data is encrypted on customers' devices and can only be decrypted using their master passwords.
However, pCloud did not disclose whether any encrypted password vaults were accessed or stolen during the attack.
This matters because threat actors who obtain encrypted password vaults could try to crack them offline without being subject to the service's login rate limits or two-factor authentication protections.
This was demonstrated in the 2022 LastPass breach, when attackers stole backups containing encrypted password vaults.
Researchers later linked the breach to cryptocurrency thefts in which attackers are believed to have cracked weak or reused master passwords to access stored cryptocurrency wallet private keys and seed phrases.
A reader who contacted BleepingComputer also noted that the "Open settings" link in the email notifications pointed to passqa1.pcloud.com, which appears to be a quality assurance (QA) environment rather than the password manager's production website.
BleepingComputer confirmed that the link pointed to the same hostname in a copy of the notification shared with us.
In its statement, pCloud also discussed how advancements in artificial intelligence are accelerating the discovery of software vulnerabilities, but did not specifically state that this was an AI-powered attack.
The company is also warning customers to watch for phishing attacks, stating that it will never ask for their master passwords or recovery words over email, phone, or chat.
The pCloud Pass incident is the latest in a series of cyberattacks impacting password managers this month.
Earlier in November, mSeven Software warned mSecure customers to change stored passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys after a hacker reportedly stole an encrypted customer database.
On Wednesday, 1Password disclosed a data breach after a threat actor compromised an employee's GitHub account and deployed malicious code to the company's backend services to steal customer data.
However, 1Password said customers' password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised.

articles.title: Amazon y Meta negocian levantar el bloqueo a Muse, el agente de IA que compra por los usuarios
articles.text:
Amazon y Meta mantienen conversaciones para que Muse, el agente de inteligencia artificial de Meta, pueda volver a comprar en la tienda de Amazon. Según informó Fortune, citando a personas al tanto del tema, las empresas se reunieron varias veces y las negociaciones continúan. La empresa bloqueó el uso del agente en su tienda en septiembre, hace dos meses.
Fortune precisó que se negocian dos puntos centrales: cómo se mostrarán los resultados de búsqueda y cómo se manejará la publicidad. Las conversaciones son cambiantes y no está claro si habrá un acuerdo ni cuándo. Cualquier pacto requeriría la aprobación de los directores ejecutivos de ambas compañías.
Por qué Amazon bloqueó a Muse
El bloqueo comenzó el 20 de septiembre. Quienes intentaban comprar con Muse veían un aviso que decía que el acceso de un agente de IA no autorizado violaba las condiciones de uso, aceptadas por sus clientes previamente.
Un portavoz de Amazon dijo a GeekWire que las aplicaciones de terceros que compran en nombre de los clientes deben operar de forma abierta y respetar las decisiones de cada comercio. La empresa sostuvo que Meta no le avisó de que Muse entraría a su tienda y que el agente no se identifica al navegar.
La compañía también afirmó que el agente parecía capturar y almacenar credenciales de clientes, lo que podría generar riesgos de privacidad y seguridad. Meta había dicho antes que Muse no ve las contraseñas ni los medios de pago, que quedan en un almacenamiento seguro.
Según Fortune, la preocupación de fondo es económica. Los anuncios son un negocio de USD 68.600 millones para Amazon, casi el 10% de sus ingresos anuales. Un agente que compra por el usuario podría evitar esos anuncios en el sitio. Los ejecutivos también temen, según recogió la revista de negocios estadounidense, que los agentes de compra debiliten su relación con los consumidores y afecten la calidad de los resultados de búsqueda.
Muse, el mayor éxito de Meta en IA para consumidores
Meta lanzó Muse en Estados Unidos en septiembre. Es un agente personalizado que el usuario puede nombrar y dirigir para revisar el correo, gestionar calendarios o reservar mesas. En octubre, más de 10 millones de personas en Estados Unidos y Canadá lo habían configurado, la mayor adopción de una IA de consumo en la historia de la empresa, según Fortune.
El presidente ejecutivo, Mark Zuckerberg, dijo que las compras son el principal uso de Muse. Meta planea cobrar a futuro una “pequeña comisión” por las transacciones. Entre sus socios figuran rivales de Amazon como Shopify, Walmart y Best Buy.
Amazon tiene su propio agente, llamado “Alexa for shopping”, que, según su presidente ejecutivo, Andy Jassy, usaron más de 400 millones de clientes en el último año. En octubre, Jassy mencionó, sin nombrar a Muse, que pocos clientes compran con agentes externos porque la experiencia no es más conveniente que ir directamente al comercio.
Este mes, en una conferencia de Semafor, el ejecutivo afirmó que la empresa no descartaba abrir su tienda a agentes externos, siempre que ofrezcan un “intercambio justo de valor”.
Las dos empresas ya colaboraron antes: desde 2023, los usuarios de Facebook e Instagram pueden comprar productos de Amazon sin salir de esas aplicaciones. Las conversaciones coinciden con el Black Friday y el Cyber Monday, y no hay fecha para una decisión.

articles.title: Supercoin’s plan to bypass the dollar in African payments
articles.text:
Supercoin, the digital payments company owned by Betway parent Super Group, plans to use a Kenyan shilling-backed stablecoin to settle payments between South Africa and Kenya without routing them through the US dollar.
The company said it has applied to the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) for a stablecoin issuance licence and plans to start serving payment companies in the first half of 2027, subject to approval.
Supercoin wants a remittance firm to take in rand in South Africa, exchange the company’s rand-backed token, ZARsc, for its proposed Kenyan shilling token, KESsc, and pay out in Kenya. A direct swap would remove the need to buy and sell dollars.
The commercial test is whether Supercoin can trade enough rand and shillings to give payment companies a better rate and deliver the money as quickly as their existing providers.
“If we can provide enough liquidity to the ZAR-KES pair in our stablecoin, then we can start selling that rail for instant payments between South Africa and Kenya,” Gideon Greaves, Supercoin’s managing director, told TechCabal in an interview.
Kenya gave Supercoin a clear route to a licence and a market where payment firms were already familiar with stablecoins, Greaves said. Supercoin plans to start with remittance companies, fintechs, and payment networks, with work on a Kenyan consumer wallet expected in the second half of 2027.
The company is entering a market where dollar-backed tokens are already widely used. According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), stablecoins accounted for an estimated $3 billion–$4 billion of about KES 740 billion ($5.7 billion) that Kenyans transacted in cryptocurrencies in 2025.
USDT, the US dollar-backed stablecoin issued by El Salvador-based company Tether, was the preferred digital currency for many Kenyan consumers paying informally and receiving remittances, according to the IMF.
Supercoin proposes that a payment firm can settle in shillings even when its customers prefer to save in dollars.
The off-ramp problem
Sending a stablecoin takes seconds, thanks to the blockchain. However, getting the money into a recipient’s local bank account or mobile wallet requires an “off-ramp.”
Without reliable off-ramps with enough local currency on hand, stablecoin issuers will struggle to persuade payment firms to use their digital tokens for remittances. Those firms need to know they can pay recipients in full and on time, even when transfer volumes spike.
If a company is sending rand-backed stablecoins to a Kenyan market, it needs an off-ramp to settle the payment and make the cash available where the recipient collects it.
“Even when there is a venue where the stablecoin exists, and someone’s making a payment from stablecoin somewhere else—let’s say to Zimbabwe, for example—for a cash collection at a kiosk, it’s settling in fiat,” Greaves said. “So it’s still going through those banking rails.”
Greaves said Supercoin has signed an off-ramp agreement with a partner in Kenya. Yet, talks about access to a mobile money off-ramp for fiat payouts—which most Kenyans use—were still exploratory. At the end of September 2026, M-PESA had 42.3 million monthly active customers in Kenya, according to Safaricom.
Supercoin plans to supply the tokens that payment companies use to settle transfers. Those companies would still need a way to pay recipients who want their money in a mobile wallet.
“The wallet is very much a secondary business for us,” Greaves said. “It’s an area of utility for the stablecoin. But our core focus on our North Star is the issuance side. So we’ll always be the rail in the background.”
Payment firms already have other ways to reach Kenyan accounts. In February, PesaLink, Kenya’s instant payment network, partnered with the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) to enable round-the-clock cross-border payments in local currencies into participating Kenyan bank and mobile money accounts.
Supercoin would have to give payment firms a reason to switch. A direct rand-to-shilling trade could remove a currency conversion, but savings could shrink if the market for the two tokens is too thin to offer a competitive rate or if payouts are expensive.
South Africa shows the other side of the problem. Since its September 2025 launch, Supercoin has grown to surpass 10 million ZARsc tokens in circulation, according to Greaves. Three of South Africa’s largest cryptocurrency exchanges, Luno, VALR, and OVEX—which have a combined 7.8 million users—serve as distribution venues for Supercoin’s ZARsc.
Yet, adopters still mainly use the stablecoin to trade cryptocurrencies. In its next phase, Supercoin wants its stablecoin embedded in corporate and merchant payments, with yield offerings and investments becoming a key part of that strategy.
In November, the stablecoin issuer launched Supercoin Mint, allowing approved businesses to deposit rand in exchange for ZARsc and redeem the tokens for rand paid into their bank accounts. The service lets large payment companies mint and redeem ZARsc as part of their day-to-day operations.
Another feature, ZARsc Borrow, lets customers on South African crypto exchange VALR borrow Supercoin’s rand-backed stablecoin using their cryptocurrency holdings as collateral.
“If we onboarded a large payment service provider, we can’t be doing minting and redemption on email,” Greaves said. “We have to do it properly, seamlessly in a safe environment where they’ve done KYB, they enter the console, they deposit the rands, they get ZARsc out and reverse.”
Supercoin’s liquidity advantage
Greaves said Supercoin currently draws on its parent’s balance sheet for liquidity. Super Group, the NYSE-listed owner of Betway and online casino business Spin, reported $602 million in cash and cash equivalents at the end of September 2026, and a profit of $142 million in Q3.
“In Kenya, we’re not concerned about the capital requirements,” Greaves said. “We see this opportunity.”
Kenya requires stablecoin issuers to have KES 300 million ($2.3 million) in paid-up capital, the highest minimum under its virtual asset rules, which took effect on November 4. Issuers must also hold reserves sufficient to cover every outstanding token.
At least 30% of the funds they receive for tokens must sit in segregated trust accounts at Kenyan commercial banks, with the balance invested in eligible assets in Kenya, including short-term government securities.
While a well-funded parent company can help an issuer clear the capital threshold, it still needs enough companies and businesses buying and selling both tokens to keep the exchange rate competitive.
Supercoin is also mulling plans for a naira-backed stablecoin, according to Greaves. He noted that the talks remain “exploratory.”
Nigeria’s central bank requires at least ₦10 billion ($7.44 million) in paid-up capital for issuers of naira-backed tokens and ₦15 billion ($11.16 million) for issuers of foreign currency-backed tokens.
Supercoin’s ZARsc is backed by the South African rand, so offering it in Nigeria would generally require a locally licenced issuer with at least ₦15 billion ($11.16 million) in paid-up capital under CBN rules.
On the other hand, issuing a naira-backed stablecoin through a licenced Nigerian subsidiary would lower that requirement.
Who earns the interest?
Issuers can earn income from eligible reserve assets backing their stablecoins, such as short-term government securities.
Passing some of that income to token holders would give customers a reason to hold balances between payments, especially when they could earn interest on the same money in a bank account. Greaves said Supercoin was working on a way for users to earn yield on ZARsc through exchanges.
“To truly benefit [from] the full power of money being on chain, you would need to have the same benefits that you have of fiat,” Greaves said. “And one of the benefits that you have of holding fiat is earning yield.”
Kenya bars stablecoin issuers from paying interest to holders and prohibits licencees from granting interest on stablecoin-related services. The ban covers benefits linked to how long someone holds a token. An issuer can earn income on its reserves, while customers have less incentive to move interest-bearing balances out of banks.
Several African regulators, including Nigeria’s central bank, are banning stablecoin yield, likely to discourage customers from moving savings out of bank deposits and into tokens that pay higher returns.
Greaves expects regulators to revisit those restrictions as the industry matures. In the meantime, stablecoin issuers like Supercoin are pitching their case as effective payment tools.
For the payments company, connecting the rails between Kenya and South Africa—and eventually to other African currencies—will enable it to build a closed-loop ecosystem that lets businesses and merchants make intra-African payments without needing the dollar.

articles.title: AMD's RDNA 5 Set for Linux Kernel 7.5 Support
articles.text:
Friday, November 27th 2026
AMD's RDNA 5 Set for Linux Kernel 7.5 Support
AMD's RDNA 5 is nearing full software support from the open-source Linux kernel maintainers, as the project prepares to officially include this support in Linux kernel version 7.5. In early November, we reported that AMD released a series of patches to add GFX13 support to the open-source AMDGPU driver. Now, we learn that AMD's software and firmware engineers plan to merge GFX13 support, also known as RDNA 5, for the upcoming Linux 7.5 kernel, bringing the launch one step closer to reality. While software enablement typically occurs months before the actual hardware launch, this development is a promising sign that RDNA 5 is approaching its release, currently rumored for the second half of 2027.
In the past, there have been interesting mentions of two specific targets, GFX 13.0.1 and GFX 13.0.4, indicating that AMD is preparing at least two graphics IP configurations. These version numbers do not correspond to any specific GPU models, so it remains unclear which products they relate to. RDNA 5 is expected to be a significant advancement over RDNA 4, requiring numerous patches to add support. Today's pull request also includes mentions of the already-covered Display Core Next 6 (DCN6) display engine, which will be exclusive to RDNA 5. Additionally, it's worth noting that the RadeonSI OpenGL and RADV Vulkan drivers in Mesa are also receiving supporting work, ensuring that open-source driver implementations will be available from day one on Linux machines.
Sources:
				AMGPU, 				Phoronix, 				via VideoCardz

articles.title: Atari feiert spätes Office-Comeback: Wie du jetzt Word und Excel auf den alten Geräten nutzen kannst
articles.text:
Atari feiert spätes Office-Comeback: Wie du jetzt Word und Excel auf den alten Geräten nutzen kannst
Die wuchtigen Heimcomputer von Atari sind heute eher in Museen zu finden. Dennoch nutzt eine große Community von Sammler:innen die Geräte nach wie vor, um in die Vergangenheit einzutauchen und beispielsweise Retro-Games zu spielen. Der Entwickler hinter XL Office verfolgt allerdings andere Pläne: Er will die Atari-Computer wieder zu Produktivitätswerkzeugen machen.
Paint, Word und Excel im Retro-Stil
Der Hersteller Atari wurde zunächst durch Spielekonsolen bekannt. Später erweiterte er sein Angebot und brachte eine Reihe von Heimcomputern auf den Markt. Die 8-Bit-Familie von Atari bestand Ende der 1970er-Jahre aus echten Pioniergeräten mit eigenen Spezialchips für Grafik und Ton. Das Unternehmen soll mehrere Millionen Geräte verkauft haben. Trotzdem stellte es die Produktion Ende 1991 ein. 35 Jahre später hat XL Office jetzt eine kostenlose Sammlung mit zehn Produktivitätsanwendungen für die Modelle XL und XE des 8-Bit-Computers von Atari herausgebracht.
Die Sammlung umfasst ein Textverarbeitungsprogramm, eine Tabellenkalkulation, eine Paint-Version mit 16 Farben, einen Browser und sogar eine Powerpoint-Alternative. Das Paket benötigt lediglich 64 Kilobyte Speicher und unterstützt sowohl PAL- als auch NTSC-Systeme. Auf der Website heißt es, es handele sich um „das Office, das Atari niemals hatte“. Mycomuapp hat XL Office als unabhängiges Projekt in 6502-Assembler für die echte Hardware geschrieben. Hinter dem Unternehmen steht der chilenische Entwickler Rodrigo Contreras Benz. Das Projekt hat keine Verbindung zu Atari selbst.
Atari-PC bekommt eine Neuauflage
Wie Heise berichtet, soll am 23. April 2027 außerdem eine originalgetreue Neuauflage des populären 8-Bit-Heimcomputers Atari 800 XL erscheinen. Das Original aus dem Jahr 1983 vereinte Rechner, Modulschacht und vollwertige Tastatur in einem flachen Gehäuse. Die neue Version soll dieses Design übernehmen, es aber durch zeitgemäße Technik ergänzen. So verfügt es beispielsweise über HDMI-Ausgänge, an die sich auch Smart-TVs anschließen lassen.
Die Neuauflage entsteht in Zusammenarbeit mit dem britischen Unternehmen Retro Games, das schon im Jahr 2024 eine Mini-Version des Atari 400 auf den Markt brachte. Standardmäßig sollen bei der geplanten Neuauflage 25 Spiele enthalten sein, darunter beliebte Atari-Klassiker. Wer noch keinen Atari-Computer in seiner Retro-Sammlung hat, kann also im nächsten Jahr zur Neuauflage greifen und darauf auch die praktischen Anwendungen von XL Office nutzen.
Retro-Geräte feiern ein Comeback
Der aktuelle Retro-Trend geht allerdings weit über Sammler:innen hinaus. Auch junge Leute beginnen, sich zunehmend für Technologie aus den vergangenen Jahrzehnten zu begeistern. Das zeigt sich nicht nur bei alten Computersystemen, sondern auch bei Analogkameras, alten Handymodellen sowie Schallplatten und CDs. Das bestätigt auch eine Umfrage, die Pringles bei dem Meinungsforschungsinstitut 3Gem in Auftrag gegeben hat.
Hier gaben 77 Prozent der insgesamt 2.000 Befragten in Deutschland an, dass sie Technik aus den 1990er- und 2000er-Jahren cool finden. Beim Gaming ist der Retro-Trend besonders stark ausgeprägt: So gaben 48 Prozent der Millennials an, dass sie lieber auf einer Retro-Konsole spielen als auf einer modernen Alternative. Auch die Gen Z äußert den Wunsch nach simpleren Geräten – oft durch einen „digitalen Burnout“ angetrieben.

articles.title: Character.AI wants to sell chat histories from more than 21 million accounts in bankruptcy, and 42 states object
articles.text:
Editor's take: Private conversations that millions of people had with AI characters are up for auction, and 42 state attorneys general want the sale stopped. Character.AI, now in Chapter 11, is trying to sell the saved chat histories of more than 21 million US accounts, 2.1 million of them registered to minors, to a buyer who would owe those users nothing.
Character.AI built its product on persistent, role-playing conversations. Users talk with characters for weeks or months, and the company stores every exchange on its servers. That archive is now one of the few valuable things left in the bankrupt company, and the attorneys general say the plan offers "no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold."
The technical value of such a trove is easy to see. Long, emotionally candid dialogue is the kind of material used to train chatbots to sound more human and keep users engaged. The same material is also sensitive in a way ordinary web data is not. Chats with a companion bot can include confessions, relationship details, and discussions of self-harm. Linked to an account, they are hard to anonymize.
Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October after years of scandals and lawsuits. These included legal challenges over teen suicides and a claim from Disney over characters that used its intellectual property. Disney later bought some of the company's assets and hired chief executive Karandeep Anand. A similarly broad coalition of attorneys general opposed that deal.
With the engineering talent and some intellectual property going to Disney, the user data became the main asset left for creditors. That is why the sale of the chat logs now draws the most scrutiny.
The states' objection is about structure more than the sale itself. As the attorneys general describe, the plan has no requirement that a buyer honor Character.AI's existing privacy policies. It gives users no way to delete their data before the transfer. It also puts no limits on what the buyer could do next, including reselling the data to another party.
In practice, a user who agreed to one set of terms could find the data under entirely different control. Privacy policies are among the main legal restraints on how stored conversations are used. If a buyer can disregard them, that restraint disappears at the moment of sale.
The identity of the first bidder adds to the concern. The entity was established earlier this month, only days before the sale drew attention. It has no listed parent company or investors. For regulators, that makes it impossible to assess how the data would be stored, secured, or used, or whether the buyer could be held accountable if something went wrong.
Nearly identical press releases from the attorneys general in California, Maryland, Connecticut, Minnesota, and other states show how coordinated the opposition is. The coalition now totals 42 states.
New York, Connecticut, California, and Colorado have passed laws governing chatbots, and those laws take effect in January 2027. Character.AI may be in violation of them once they apply. That raises the possibility that a buyer would inherit data collected under practices the new rules target, along with the compliance exposure that comes with it.
The implications of the case are unlikely to be limited to one company. AI startups hold large stores of user conversations, and many are burning cash. If one fails, bankruptcy law will treat those archives as property unless courts or regulators say otherwise. A ruling here could set a precedent for what happens to such data when an AI company collapses.
The bankruptcy court will decide whether the sale proceeds and on what terms. The attorneys general are asking for protections before any transfer, including limits on use and a way for users to remove their chats. Until the court rules, the conversations of millions of users, many of them minors, remain part of the estate.

articles.title: Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
articles.text:
Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
- Date:
  November 23, 2026
- Source:
  Universiteit van Amsterdam
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed remarkable materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially paving the way for a new generation of autonomous soft robots. They also discovered that making individual components more active can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive, challenging a long-standing principle of engineering.
- Share:
Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. But a very different category of matter can draw on its own energy to change shape and respond to outside forces in surprising ways. Known as active matter, these unusual materials are attracting growing scientific interest. Now, physicists from the universities of Amsterdam, New South Wales, and Cambridge have uncovered remarkable new behaviors that could change how future machines and robots are designed.
Everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive. They can stretch, bend, shift, or change shape when forces act on them, but the energy needed to produce those changes comes from outside the material.
Active matter works differently. It contains an internal source of energy that allows it to respond to its surroundings in ways ordinary materials cannot. Many examples occur naturally in living systems. A flock of birds, for instance, can move together as a coordinated group, adjusting its behavior in response to wind, changes in the landscape, available food, or a suitable place to rest.
Scientists can also recreate some of these remarkable properties in the laboratory. Researchers from the University of Amsterdam (The Netherlands), the University of Cambridge (UK), and the University of New South Wales (Sydney, Australia) have spent several years developing active materials from surprisingly simple components, including miniature motors, rods, and rubber bands. Their experiments have revealed unusual mechanical behaviors with potentially valuable applications, leading to two recently accepted scientific papers.
Scientists Create Materials That Can Crawl, Walk, and Dig
One of the discoveries involves two familiar mechanical behaviors known as buckling and snapping.
Imagine squeezing a paper ticket between your fingers. As the pressure increases, the ticket becomes unstable and bends to one side. If you then press against the curved surface, it initially pushes back before suddenly flipping in the opposite direction.
This is how ordinary passive materials behave. External forces supply the energy needed for the ticket to buckle and snap, and each action occurs only once in response to the applied force.
The researchers discovered that adding internal activity can fundamentally transform this behavior. They assembled a series of connected rods into a flexible chain, placing small motors at the joints where neighboring rods meet. These motors created interactions that were not symmetrical. Moving one rod could affect its neighbor in a different way than moving that neighbor would affect the original rod (by rotating over a different angle, for example).
The result was striking. When external forces acted on these active chains, they still bent and snapped, but the movement no longer had to end after a single event. Instead, the structures could repeatedly buckle and snap, producing ongoing oscillations.
The underlying physics involves a transformation of the system's critical point, where snapping normally takes place, into what researchers call a critical exceptional point. This unusual behavior makes it possible for the chains to generate movements resembling crawling, walking, and even digging.
The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, with Sami Al-Izzi of the University of New South Wales and Yao Du of the University of Amsterdam serving as joint first authors. One of the team's buckling chains was also featured on the journal's cover.
Beyond revealing unexpected physics, the discovery points toward a promising approach to building materials capable of performing multiple tasks autonomously. Such structures could be especially useful in flexible, "soft" robots, potentially allowing their bodies to produce complex movements without relying on a centralized control system.
Active Matter Challenges a Fundamental Engineering Principle
A separate investigation by the same international research team uncovered another surprising property of active materials, this time challenging a principle widely used in engineering.
Whether designing large bridges or tiny nanomechanical devices, engineers depend on established rules that connect the properties of individual components to the behavior of an entire structure.
One such rule is Le Chatelier's Principle. In the mechanical context described by the researchers, it suggests that changes made to individual parts of a system should produce corresponding changes in the overall structure. For example, making a structure's individual components stiffer would generally be expected to increase the stiffness of the entire assembly.
But the researchers found that active matter does not always follow this expectation. In some cases, increasing the activity of individual components can actually reduce the activity of the material as a whole.
To investigate this counterintuitive effect, the scientists built another structure using motors and rods. Rather than arranging the components in a chain, they connected them into a flat, two-dimensional network resembling a lattice. They then examined how the elastic behavior of the entire structure changed depending on the properties of its individual elements.
Their experiments revealed that the overall response depended on more than simply how active each component was. What mattered was whether the active elements formed connected pathways capable of transmitting mechanical responses throughout the structure.
Why More Activity Can Produce Less Response
The researchers identified a process called percolation as the key to understanding this unexpected behavior.
A useful comparison is the movement of water through ground coffee. If the coffee grounds are packed too tightly, water cannot easily travel through the entire layer. The arrangement of the grounds determines whether the water can find a continuous path.
Something similar happens inside active materials. If too many of the interconnected components have relatively low activity, they can prevent elastic responses from spreading through the structure. Even when other components are extremely active, their influence may not extend across the entire material.
This explains why making some parts more active does not necessarily produce a more active structure overall. The way the components are connected and distributed can be just as important as their individual properties.
The second study, led by first author Jack Binysh from Corentin Coulais's research group at the University of Amsterdam, was published in Physical Review X.
The researchers believe that this unexpected departure from Le Chatelier's Principle could have important implications for understanding and designing systems built from active microscopic structures. These include biological gels, epithelial monolayers, which are sheets of closely connected cells, and neuromorphic networks that mimic aspects of biological information processing.
Together, the findings reveal how dramatically materials can behave when their internal components actively consume energy and interact in unconventional ways. The discoveries could influence research across physics, soft matter science, mechanical engineering, the life sciences, and robotics, while opening new possibilities for creating adaptable materials and smarter robotic systems.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Universiteit van Amsterdam. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal References:
- Sami C. Al-Izzi, Yao Du, Jonas Veenstra, Richard G. Morris, Anton Souslov, Andreas Carlson, Corentin Coulais, Jack Binysh. Nonreciprocal buckling makes active filaments polyfunctional. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2026; 123 (11) DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2531723123
- Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, Anton Souslov. More is Less in Unpercolated Active Solids. Physical Review X, 2026; 16 (2) DOI: 10.1103/flhb-kjyd

articles.title: Texas lifts freeze on 1,800+ data center projects in Greg Abbott U-turn — companies rush for permits before Gina Hinojosa's January arrival
articles.text:
Texas lifts freeze on 1,800+ data center projects in Greg Abbott U-turn — companies rush for permits before Gina Hinojosa's January arrival
The state had paused the approval of new permits at the behest of outgoing Republican governor Greg Abbott, but the halt was short-lived.
After slamming the brakes on more than 1,800 data center projects in August, Texas has once again started approving them following a new directive from outgoing Republican governor Greg Abbott's office. The move came after the same office also paused the approval of permits, saying that Abbot's "top priority is to protect Texans’ safety and quality of life” amid concerns over the amount of power new data centers would require. At the time, the move meant that 474 gigawatts of new power requests became subject to the moratorium. But with Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa's January arrival edging ever closer, Abbott has done a 180-degree pivot, with the FT reporting that data center builders are rushing to get their approvals in before the new governor arrives. Hinojosa has already pledged to rein in new data center construction.
As recently as October, Texas suspended a further 17 data center construction permits and shut down an automated portal that was found to still be approving new permits. That system will surely be switched back on now that Abbott's office has confirmed that the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), which is in charge of the state’s electrical grid, has finished gathering the information that it needed on how data centers affect local communities.
But even with ERCOT's investigation complete, the processing of new power requests isn't one that is expected to happen quickly. With that in mind, some developers have already taken matters into their own hands, choosing to build their own power centers to reduce or eliminate their reliance on the local grid. The region's large gas supplies are helping this effort, as is what is considered to be a "lax" regulatory environment. This all means that the possibility of using gas turbines to power new data centers is a viable one, although some are looking beyond traditional gas-powered options. In Mississippi, Elon Musk's xAI installed eight converted jet engines to power its data center, despite the known health risks posed by their use.
While it remains to be seen what impact the arrival of incoming Governor Hinojosa will have on data centers in the area, there's little doubt that they will be a hot topic. Locals continue to be concerned about the environmental impact these facilities have, while increased costs associated with powering their own homes are another issue. Texas isn't alone in facing these problems, with New York announcing a year-long ban on data center projects larger than 50 megawatts that came into force earlier this year. In Northern Virginia, Amazon abandoned plans to build four new data centers after public outcry. The land will now be used for housing instead.

Oliver Haslam has written about technology of all shapes and sizes for over 15 years, both online and in print. He's fascinated by how personal computing continues to change as tower PCs give way to foldable phones and beyond.

articles.title: Cómo reunir todos tus juegos de Epic Games, GOG y Amazon en una sola aplicación para Windows, Mac y Linux
articles.text:
El juego en PC vive una época dorada en la que cuesta elegir a qué juego jugar ante tanta oferta disponible. Para bien o para mal, han proliferado tiendas de juegos digitales por doquier en las que resulta muy fácil comprar un título, descargarlo e instalarlo en tu ordenador. Además, tal es la competencia que abundan las ofertas, descuentos y, de vez en cuando, regalos en forma de juegos gratis. Así que para poner un poco de orden, han surgido lanzadores compatibles con esas tiendas, como Heroic Games Launcher. O, sencillamente, Heroic.
El otro día expliqué cómo añadir juegos a Steam de otras tiendas, como Epic Games, GOG y tantas otras. De esta manera, verás todos tus juegos en una sola biblioteca. Y te será más fácil saber qué títulos has instalado. Pero este método no es perfecto. Y puede que quieras aunar lo mejor de los lanzadores y tiendas de juegos en una sola aplicación. Muy útil tanto en PC como en Mac, Steam Deck o Steam Machine.
Una solución para no tener que instalar todos los lanzadores oficiales es Heroic Games Launcher. Se trata de un lanzador gratuito y de código abierto, compatible con la mayoría de plataformas y que te permite gestionar y unificar tus bibliotecas de Epic Games, GOG y Amazon Games. Y está repleta de sorpresas para que puedas jugar a todos tus juegos, incluso si son de Windows y tienes una máquina con Linux o macOS.
Para qué sirve un lanzador de juegos
Pero vayamos por partes. Hoy en día, la mayoría de juegos para ordenador se compran o se adquieren a través de tiendas digitales. Estas tiendas facilitan el proceso de búsqueda, compra y descarga del juego. Este último paso, gracias a que la mayoría de tiendas tienen su propio lanzador de juegos.
Un lanzador de juegos, game launcher en inglés, es una aplicación que permite organizar, gestionar, instalar, actualizar y ejecutar juegos. De esta manera, te es más fácil y cómo saber qué juegos tienes instalados, mantenerlos actualizados con los últimos parches y, lo mejor de todo, estar seguro de que se abrirán y funcionarán correctamente en tu ordenador.
Con el paso de los años, las tiendas digitales se han asegurado de tener su propio lanzador de juegos, ya que para el usuario, ambas herramientas son prácticamente indistinguibles, al estar muy ligadas una con otra. Por ello, hoy en día encontramos tiendas con lanzador como Steam, Epic Games Launcher, GOG Galaxy, EA app (antes Origin), Ubisoft Connect (antes Uplay) y otras tiendas más de nicho como itch.io.
Y ante la necesidad de unificar todas esas tiendas, han surgido lanzadores de juegos como el que te presentamos hoy, Heroic Games Launcher. Pero hay muchos más, como Lutris o Playnite. Muchos de ellos gratuitos, de código abierto y enfocados a jugar en Linux pero con versiones para Windows y macOS.
Para qué sirve Heroic Games Launcher
Como decía, Heroic Games Launcher, o solo Heroic, es un lanzador de juegos. Una aplicación que pretende sustituir a lanzadores oficiales como Epic Games, GOG y Amazon Games. Eso, de momento. Y si tienes juegos de otras tiendas, puedes añadirlos manualmente a partir de su instalador al igual que ocurre con Steam.
Entre sus muchas virtudes, Heroic es gratuito, de código abierto, funciona en Windows, macOS y Linux. Hasta puedes instalarlo en SteamOS, lo que significa que funciona en Steam Deck y Steam Machine. Y se encarga de todo. Facilita las tareas de instalar, actualizar y configurar los juegos para que funcionen correctamente en tu máquina. Además, su interfaz te permite ver las carátulas de los juegos, sus fichas con información de cada título…
Otra función muy acertada de Heroic es que permite iniciar sesión con tus cuentas de Epic, GOG y Amazon. Así verás los juegos en una sola biblioteca y, además, podrás acceder a la versión online de las tres tiendas para buscar chollos, ofertas o comprar nuevos juegos. Por lo demás, comparte con Steam la posibilidad de personalizar las carátulas de los juegos. Y también tiene un modo consola al estilo del modo Big Picture de Steam.
Cómo empezar a usar Heroic por primera vez
Instalar Heroic es muy fácil. Tiene instaladores para la mayoría de plataformas, como hemos visto. Así que no es necesario explicar el proceso. En el momento de escribir estas líneas, Heroic Games Launcher funciona en Windows 10 y Windows 11, macOS 14 y posterior, SteamOS y varias versiones de Linux, como Ubuntu 22.04, OpenSuse Tumbleweed, Fedora 37, Arch Linux y sus derivados. Y aunque necesitarás un buen ordenador para manejar los juegos más potentes, el lanzador de juegos en sí mismo solo te pide 500 MB de espacio, 2 GB de RAM y un procesador dual core de 1,8 GHz.
Lo primero que te recomiendo hacer cuando abras Heroic la primera vez es que inicies sesión en las tiendas compatibles. Es decir, Epic Games, GOG y Amazon Games. Claro está, que lo hagas o no dependerá de si tienes juegos comprados o adquiridos en esas tiendas. Y si no es así, deberías, ya que muchas veces regalan juegos de lo más variado. Para iniciar sesión, puedes ir a la Biblioteca o ir a Gestionar cuentas.
En Ajustes podrás hacer todos los cambios que necesites. Aunque también tendrás ocasión de hacer cambios en cada juego que vayas a instalar. Pero para ello deberás ir a Biblioteca y entrar en cada ficha de juego.
Instalar juegos con Heroic Games Launcher
Una vez hayas iniciado sesión con, al menos, una de tus cuentas de juego, verás que los títulos asociados a tu cuenta van apareciendo en Biblioteca, dentro de la app Heroic. Las carátulas aparecerán en blanco y negro. Y cuando instales cada juego, se verá en color, para que diferencies unos de otros.
El proceso de instalar juegos también es sencillo. Para eso están los lanzadores de juegos. Haz doble clic en el juego y se abrirá su ficha técnica. Luego, simplemente, pulsa en Instalar. Si ya tenías el juego instalado, elige la opción Importar juego. Te permitirá indicar a Heroic en qué carpeta instalaste ese juego.
La instalación es prácticamente automática. Antes de empezar, verás el tamaño necesario y el disponible en tu ordenador. Y podrás elegir en qué ruta instalarlo, aunque la ruta por defecto siempre suele ser la más indicada. Luego el asistente se encargará de descargar el instalador y los parches o complementos que necesite ese juego para funcionar.
Al terminar de instalar, ya podrás jugar. Doble clic, y el juego se abrirá sin problemas. Aunque, como ocurre en Steam, puedes entrar en Ajustes de cada título y hacer cambios, como elegir un EXE alternativo, introducir comandos de lanzamiento, ejecutar el juego sin conexión o ignorar las actualizaciones.
Cómo añadir juegos de otras tiendas
Heroic Games Launcher quiere ser tu lanzador de cabecera. Como Steam, vamos. Por eso incluye una opción para añadir o instalar juegos de otras tiendas y tenerlo también en tu Biblioteca de Heroic. Dentro de Biblioteca, haz clic en Añadir juego. Indica el título del juego, añade imágenes y selecciona el ejecutable del mismo. Y si todavía no está instalado, haz clic en Ejecutar el instalador primero para elegir el instalador.
Al terminar, verás el juego en tu biblioteca. Como un juego más. Y podrás aplicarle los mismos ajustes, como cambiar las imágenes y carátulas, introducir comandos de lanzamiento, etc. Y si tienes cualquier duda, en la documentación oficial de Heroic encontrarás ayuda para instalaciones complejas como, por ejemplo, juegos de Rockstar Games que te dan problemas y otros casos particulares.
Juegos de Windows en Mac y Linux con Heroic
Si eres usuario de Mac o Linux, Heroic Games Launcher tiene mucho que aportarte. Como ya sabrás, la mayoría de juegos para PC son solo compatibles con Windows. Y aunque eso está cambiando gracias a los esfuerzos de Apple, proyectos como Wine y CrossOver o Proton de Steam, toda ayuda es poca para jugar a juegos para Windows en otras plataformas. Y ahí, Heroic te será muy útil. Aunque, por descontado, los juegos nativos para Mac y Linux los puedes instalar tal cual.
En estas plataformas, cuando quieras instalar un juego para Windows, Heroic Games Launcher te ofrecerá varias opciones para añadir compatibilidad. El lanzador integra distintas herramientas para hacer compatible el juego en Linux o macOS. En Linux, Wine-GE, Wine-Lutris y Proton-GE. Y en macOS, puedes elegir entre Wine-CrossOver, Wine-Staging y Game Porting Toolkit. El lanzador se encargará de descargar, instalar y configurar por ti cada una de estas herramientas para que el juego cargue sin problemas.
Para poner algo de contexto, Wine es un proyecto que emula los componentes de Windows necesarios para usar apps y juegos en Linux y macOS. Más eficiente que usar una máquina virtual, que implica emular todo el PC. Wine-GE es una versión creada por GloriousEggroll específica para juegos. Ya no recibe actualizaciones, pero resulta útil especialmente para juegos antiguos o clásicos. Wine-Lutris es la versión personalizada y mantenida por el proyecto Lutris, que es otro lanzador de juegos. Y Proton-GE es una modificación de Proton, con mejoras para componentes gráficos como DXVK y VKD3D (DirectX y Vulkan).
Y en macOS, Wine-CrossOver es una versión de Wine desarrollada por CrossOver. Aunque, en honor a la verdad, CrossOver es el principal responsable de mantener el proyecto Wine. Por su parte, Wine-Staging es una versión de Wine con parches experimentales. Y Game Porting Toolkit es la herramienta que lanzó Apple para ejecutar juegos de Windows en macOS. Y que basa parte de su código en Wine.

articles.title: Un essaim de drones qui attaque Ariane 6 ? Le Centre spatial guyanais « n’est pas du tout paré », mais ne voit pas l’urgence de passer aux lasers
articles.text:
C’est une annonce qui illustre l’évolution rapide de la menace qui pèse sur les bases de lancement. Fin septembre 2026, l’US Space Force a annoncé qu’elle allait installer des lasers anti-drones à Cap Canaveral, la base de Floride d’où décollent les fusées de SpaceX et d’United Launch Alliance, après une intrusion à 2,5 kilomètres du pas de tir lunaire.
Très vite s’est posée une question évidente : qu’en est-il de la protection du Centre spatial guyanais (CSG), près de Kourou, qui constitue le principal spatioport européen ? À ce stade, personne ne prévoit de faire pareil, quand bien même le site est absolument stratégique pour lancer les fusées Ariane 6 et Vega-C.
Thierry Vallée, sous-directeur chargé de la protection, de la sauvegarde et de l’environnement au CSG, la base gérée par l’agence spatiale française, a été clair quand Numerama l’a interrogé sur place : « Pour le moment, on n’est pas du tout sur ce registre de neutralisation. » Le centre mise plutôt sur des brouilleurs et sur une très grande zone interdite de survol.
Ce choix s’explique d’abord par la géographie. Selon Thierry Vallée, le relatif isolement du Centre spatial guyanais (littéralement entre l’océan Atlantique et la jungle amazonienne) lui simplifie la tâche. La règlementation aussi : « La lutte anti-drone ici, elle est simplifiée par le fait qu’on est dans une zone qui naturellement est interdite de survol. »
La base se trouvant donc entre deux environnements difficiles d’accès et au beau milieu d’une zone où personne n’a le droit de voler sans autorisation, l’option du laser n’est « pas nécessairement étudiée en profondeur » au CSG. Thierry Vallée annonce toutefois des expérimentations en 2027 « sur la partie drone en règle générale », sans entrer dans les détails.
Par ailleurs, un autre facteur joue sans doute : la cadence d’activité. Du côté des États-Unis, Cap Canaveral a enchaîné 109 lancements orbitaux en 2025, selon DroneXL, et le colonel Brian Chatman, qui commande les opérations de lancement sur place, juge possible d’en accueillir plus de 300 par an. Près du triple, en somme.
À Kourou, on dénombrait 7 lancements en 2025, avec 4 Ariane 6 (dont le premier vol commercial) et 3 Vega-C. C’est plus de 15 fois moins. Certes, le rythme augmente (on en prévoit 9 en 2026, avec deux tirs à effectuer avant la fin de l’année), et il y a un plan pour monter en charge dans les années à venir, mais l’écart avec la Floride reste énorme.
Un brouilleur militaire et une zone interdite plusieurs fois plus grande que la base
Cela étant, le CSG n’est pas non plus sans protection.
Contre les drones, le site fait tourner le système Parade. « Le centre spatial est équipé d’un système de lutte anti-drone permanent, le même qu’il y a à l’aéroport de Paris-Charles-de-Gaulle par exemple », explique Thierry Vallée. La Direction générale de l’armement (DGA) a confié ce programme à Thales et CS Group en mai 2022.
La commande initiale de ce marché pouvant peser 350 millions d’euros sur 11 ans portait sur 6 systèmes. Chacun d’eux rassemble un radar pour détecter les objets en vol, un goniomètre (qui repère la direction d’où viennent les ondes radio d’un drone), des caméras ainsi qu’un brouilleur, qui coupe la liaison entre le drone et sa télécommande.
Surtout, la première protection du site reste quand même la fermeture de son espace aérien. La préfecture de Guyane indique que le CSG est couvert par une zone interdite de survol baptisée SOP3, placée sous l’autorité du centre de contrôle militaire. « Elle va quasiment de la commune de Macouria que vous avez traversée en venant de Cayenne jusqu’à la commune de Sinnamary, même au-delà du côté ouest », pointe Thierry Vallée.
Le périmètre est vaste : il l’estime à « au moins 2 ou 3 fois » la surface du centre spatial, voire 4 fois. Pour un site de 660 kilomètres carrés selon le CNES (Centre national d’études spatiales), cela représente entre 1 300 et 2 600 kilomètres carrés environ. L’armée de l’Air et de l’Espace la surveille 24 heures sur 24.
Ce polygone de sécurité monte aussi très haut. Thierry Vallée a évoqué un plafond qui monterait jusqu’à 27 500 pieds, environ 8 400 mètres – pas si loin des 10 000 à 12 000 mètres auxquels croisent les avions de ligne sur les vols long-courriers. On ne trouve plus beaucoup de drones pouvant évoluer plus haut.
Le survol n’est d’ailleurs pas la seule interdiction. Le secteur du centre spatial compte aussi trois zones interdites à la captation aérienne de données (ZICAD) : deux relèvent du ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et couvrent le CSG et ses installations annexes, la troisième, incluse dans la première, dépend du ministère des Armées. Filmer ou photographier la base depuis un drone demande donc une autorisation à part.
Des drones de loisir, et aucun plan contre un essaim
Selon Thierry Vallée, le système n’a pas eu à traiter de menace hostile. Interrogé sur le délai entre détection et neutralisation, il précise ne jamais avoir été confronté à cette éventualité : « Cette situation-là, on n’a pas eu à la gérer. »
En revanche, le système détecte « régulièrement » des drones de loisir, par exemple celui d’« un papa qui offre un drone à son gamin » sans savoir qu’il vit dans une zone interdite. La Pointe des Roches, à Kourou, attire particulièrement les amateurs de vidéo aérienne. Dans ces cas-là, la réponse passe par la pédagogie : « On le détecte et puis on envoie les gendarmes et on fait de la pédagogie. »
En mai 2025, le quotidien France-Guyane a raconté l’histoire d’un homme qui avait fait voler son drone depuis la Pointe des Roches 5 minutes avant un lancement de Vega-C : son drone a été saisi et il a été interdit d’accès au CSG pendant 6 mois. Pédagogie, donc, mais aussi fermeté, pour que le message passe auprès des autres amateurs.
Par ailleurs, la pédagogie n’empêche pas les poursuites. Le Code des transports (article L6232-12) punit le survol d’une zone interdite par maladresse ou négligence de 6 mois d’emprisonnement et 15 000 euros d’amende. Si le télépilote engage ou maintient volontairement son drone au-dessus de la zone, la peine monte à un an de prison et 45 000 euros d’amende. Dans les deux cas, l’appareil peut être confisqué (article L6232-13).
Il existe pourtant une voie légale : les vols ayant obtenu une dérogation (la demande passe par l’état-major interministériel de zone, en préfecture) apparaissent comme autorisés une fois le drone identifié, et on laisse l’appareil voler.
Et s’il y avait un essaim de drones se ruant sur le CSG ?
Face à un essaim, en revanche, comme ce que l’on peut voir sur la ligne de front entre l’Ukraine et la Russie, Thierry Vallée ne cache pas les limites du dispositif. En pensant aux drones utilisés pour faire la guerre aujourd’hui, il reconnaît qu’« il faut rester humble » : « On n’est pas du tout paré à faire ça. » Il compte sur le renseignement pour voir venir la menace.
Un essaim lancé depuis la mer ? « Ce bateau on le détecterait avant parce que ça serait certainement un bateau d’une entité qui a les moyens de mettre ça en œuvre » et on devine qu’il y aurait une réponse appropriée et, le cas échéant, une intervention de la gendarmerie maritime. Ou, si besoin, une réponse plus musclée encore.
Le CSG a d’ailleurs aussi une zone d’interdiction de navigation qui s’étend au large à plus de 15 kilomètres des côtes, ainsi que la présence de patrouilleurs lors des lancements. Côté continent, enfin, Thierry Vallée rappelle le travail très en amont des agences de renseignement, comme la DGSI et la DGSE, pour suivre ce qui se passe autour de la base.
Selon Thierry Vallée, l’armée de l’Air et de l’Espace utilise aussi des tireurs d’élite embarqués à bord d’hélicoptères qui pourraient, si besoin, ouvrir le feu contre des drones non coopératifs. À différents endroits de la base, des fantassins ont aussi en main des fusils antidrones qu’ils peuvent employer pour perturber les signaux de ces engins.
Autrement dit, même le scénario effrayant d’un essaim de drones est, à ce stade, nuancé. « Cela n’arriverait pas comme ça du jour au lendemain », veut croire Thierry Vallée. Et même si en aval le CSG n’est pas prêt à ce cas de figure, la parade pourrait être déclenchée plus en amont. Mais on comprend que la porte n’est pas forcément fermée aux lasers à l’avenir.

articles.title: develoPPP Ventures opens call for SA startups, offering $110k in matching funding
articles.text:
develoPPP Ventures has opened applications for its latest South African cohort, which will see selected startups receive EUR100,000 (US$110,000) in non-dilutive funding.
develoPPP Ventures has backed 178 businesses across Africa, including 11 investments in South Africa. The current call is also open in Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Egypt and Nigeria.
The 12th cohort is run by DEG Impulse, a subsidiary of German development finance institution DEG, with VC4A and Jozi Angels as partners. It is funded by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
South African startups with proof of concept and early revenues, that can demonstrate a path to operational break-even within three years, and have secured, or are in advanced talks for, funding, are invited to apply.
The funding uses a 1:1 matching model, so startups must raise at least the same amount from other qualifying sources, including private investors. Jozi Angels will connect founders with angel and venture investors to help them meet that requirement.
“Through the develoPPP Ventures programme, we equip growth-stage entrepreneurs in South Africa with catalytic matching capital and bespoke technical support,” said Tasneem Natha, chief operating officer of Jozi Angels.
Applications close on December 31 and can be submitted here.

articles.title: Meta Brings Code Review Auto-Approval More Mainstream with PyTorch GreenLight
articles.text:
GreenLight has started letting a PyTorch AI reviewer approve pull requests from its own maintainers. It is an open-source take on RADAR, the system Meta uses to land low-risk code changes without waiting on a human. The move comes as Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic and Sonar all describe ways to automate approval itself.
RADAR stands for Risk Aware Diff Auto Review. Meta described it in a paper published in May. The paper starts from a capacity problem. Significant lines of code per human-landed diff rose 105.9% year over year, and diffs per developer per month rose 51%.
Meta attributes more than 80% of that increase to agentic AI assistance. Review has not kept pace, and the share of diffs reviewed within 24 hours is dropping. The authors describe their response in narrow terms.
Rather than attempting to replace code review broadly, RADAR targets automation to diffs that satisfy conservative safety criteria.
RADAR sorts each diff by author and source before anything else. Deterministic codemods can be approved through a blanket policy and skip per-diff AI review. AI-generated codemods and automated runbooks go through a pipeline of safety checks, a Diff Risk Score and an LLM reviewer. Any failure sends the diff to a human.
RADAR pipeline for AI and bot diffs. Source: Meta, "Automating Low-Risk Code Review at Meta" (arXiv 2605.30208)
The safety checks are hard limits. Open-source code, SOX-scoped code and code that needs extra review are never eligible. Runbooks must show a clean 60-day record, with zero production incidents and low revert and rejection rates. They are also capped at up to 2,000 diffs per day.
The Diff Risk Score works as a percentile gate. Allowlisted runbooks can land diffs up to the 50th percentile of risk. Other AI and bot sources stop at the 20th. Human-authored diffs default to the 5th, and each organization can tune its own thresholds.
The last gate is the RADAR Review Agent, which reads the actual change. It looks for safe patterns such as dead code removal, refactoring without behavior change, logging additions and new tests. The paper sets a strict bar for the agent.
For a diff to be auto-accepted, ACR requires a confidence score of at least 8 out of 10, with all changes classified into safe categories.
Approved bot diffs do not land at once. They wait in a landing queue for a configurable delay, shown as 24 hours in the paper's pipeline diagram. A human can still reject a diff during that window. Meta also monitors the funnel and tunes thresholds over time.
PyTorch said in May that it would rebuild RADAR in the open. In a PyTorch devlog, Edward Yang wrote that "the RADAR approves are good" in Meta's internal use. He also set the rule that shapes GreenLight today.
RADAR is predicated on trust of the author, so RADAR approves will be limited to PyTorch maintainers who otherwise already have approval rights on the files being changed.
GreenLight follows that rule. Its cohort comes from the people listed in PyTorch's merge rules. A PR only gets a real verdict when a merge rule names its author. Everyone else is reviewed in shadow mode, and those reviews never become approvals.
A scan runs every five minutes and sends eligible PRs to a reviewer workflow. A land verdict approves the PR and labels it. A no-land verdict withdraws any earlier GreenLight approval. The README adds that "a reverted PR is dropped from every path, permanently."
OpenAI described a similar policy at QCon San Francisco 2026. Brian Yang, member of technical staff at OpenAI, said a few engineers began building ChatGPT Ads with Codex in November 2025, and the codebase has zero human-written production code.
Yang matches approval to the change. Everyday changes are auto-approved once required checks pass. Critical changes must pass sandbox validation against a copy of production traffic, and then a human decides. His target is at least 90% auto-approval for routine PRs.
The team tunes its automated reviewer every week. Engineers read past approvals, blocks and missed breakages, then test new thresholds against history. When too many bad PRs open, they fix the agent. When bad PRs keep merging, they fix the checker. Anthropic applies the same idea to the actions an agent takes while it works with its Antique code review system.
Sonar frames approval as part of what it calls the agentic software factory. Manish Kapur, VP of product marketing and developer relations at Sonar, wrote that in a well-run factory "the factory knows which changes can pass on automated evidence and which require a person to decide." Sonar's latest developer survey shows the pressure behind that. Of more than 1,000 respondents, 76% said they generate AI code faster than they can verify it, and only 39% always check it before committing.
The common thread is scoped trust. Meta and PyTorch gate approval on author trust and a calibrated risk score. OpenAI gates it on the type of change, and Anthropic on what an action could break. In each case, reverts and misses feed back into the system.
Developers interested in learning more can read the RADAR paper here and find GreenLight's source here.

articles.title: Vendu 115 euros par erreur, le Galaxy S26 Ultra a pourtant bien été livré par Amazon à quelques chanceux
articles.text:
Le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra équipé de 256 Go de stockage est soudainement passé de 239 800 yens (environ 1 371 euros) à seulement 20 185 yens, soit à peine 115 euros. Cette vente flash involontaire a rapidement disparu du site, mais plusieurs acheteurs nippons confirment avoir pu passer commande et ont déjà reçu leur Galaxy S26 Ultra à ce prix dérisoire.
Grosse erreur de Samsung sur Amazon Japon
Généralement, lorsque ce genre d’erreur se produit sur le prix d’un produit, le commerçant invoque un bug logiciel pour rembourser les clients et annuler la commande. Mais cette fois, Amazon Japon a décidé de valider les achats effectués par les clients chanceux. Une aubaine donc quand on sait que le Galaxy S26 Ultra a été lancé à 1 469 euros et qu’on le trouve aujourd’hui autour de 1 000 euros. Amazon n’a pas communiqué officiellement sur cet incident, ce qui laisse penser qu’il s’agit bien d’une erreur de leur part qu’ils ont rapidement réglée.
Difficile de faire une meilleure affaire pour le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Même lorsque le Galaxy S27 Ultra sortira, il n’y a aucune chance de trouver un Galaxy S26 Ultra neuf à ce prix. Pour rappel, le dernier smartphone haut de gamme de Samsung est équipé d’une puce Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, d’un capteur photo principal de 200 mégapixels et d’un téléobjectif de 50 mégapixels avec zoom optique 5x. Il est également certifié IP68, intègre le stylet S Pen et profite d’une batterie de 5 000 mAh qui se recharge à 60W.
Découvrez : Les meilleurs smartphones Samsung du moment
Mais la plus grande nouveauté de cette version est l’écran avec son filtre de confidentialité qui le démarque du Galaxy S25 Ultra.
