articles.title: Ukrainian 11th-grader builds AI-powered, GPS-free drone autopilot to beat frontline jamming — earns 'The Future of Ukraine' award from President Zelenskyy
articles.text:
Ukrainian 11th-grader builds AI-powered, GPS-free drone autopilot to beat frontline jamming — earns 'The Future of Ukraine' award from President Zelenskyy
That's one smart kid.
An 11th-grade student has received “The Future of Ukraine” from President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for multiple technical achievements. According to Poltava Wave, Yaroslav Sheiko, a student from Poltava, located about 190 miles to the west of Kyiv, built an AI-powered drone autopilot system, allowing uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) to reach their destination without relying on GPS signals, and an optical-electronic stabilization system. This award is just the latest among Sheiko’s achievements.
The 11th-grader has already received two presidential scholarships for his academic performance and contributions to science, as well as getting the top award twice in nationwide competitions held by Ukraine’s Junior Academy of Sciences. He has also competed internationally, receiving a gold medal in the INOVA 2025 International Inventions Show and a silver medal in the 2025 Hackathon.
Even though Ukraine relies on military assistance from its allies, it’s also working on homegrown technologies to improve its drone capabilities. Some of these breakthroughs include equipping its grounded fleet of U.S.-made Puma reconnaissance drones with domestic anti-jamming systems and using a network of “flying modems” to increase the range of its attack drones without having to use unreliable Starlink connections.
It was the first to use a heavy-lift UAV to evacuate a wounded soldier from a minefield and conduct a 12-hour, 1,500-mile strategic drone strike on Russian targets. The country is also working on anti-drone systems, like using old Android phones as an acoustic sensor network as an early warning system to spot drones and shooting down Russian jet drones using a cheap, high-powered laser air defense system.
The widespread use of drones in Ukraine also meant that other countries have started developing their own drone and anti-drone technologies and forces. China has revealed a 200-strong AI drone swarm controlled by a single soldier using an “intelligent algorithm,” while Japan is working on an ultra-cheap cardboard drone swarm that only costs $2,000 per unit. The UK is also deploying the DragonFire anti-drone laser on Royal Navy destroyers by 2027. As for the U.S., it’s training military units on both land and sea to 3D-print combat-ready drones, assemble and maintain units in-house, and even adapt them depending on the mission at hand.
Ukraine has not detailed how Sheiko’s inventions work, but what’s more important is that these innovations are crucial to Ukraine’s war effort, especially with the amount of jamming and electronic warfare present on the front lines. More than that, his skill and talent may prove to be a crucial asset for Ukraine and its defense industry, especially as Russia’s invasion has already been ongoing for 12 years, with a full-scale conflict going on since 2022.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

articles.title: Pas de Windows, pas de Linux, juste un chatbot : voici un OS réduit à l'os pour l'IA locale
articles.text:
Le programme qui pilote ce chatbot pèse moins lourd qu’une simple photo compressée en JPEG. On allume la machine virtuelle et, en moins d’un dixième de seconde, une invite « asm-llm> » attend déjà votre première question, sans Windows, sans Linux et sans la moindre bibliothèque logicielle classique.
Aux commandes des réponses, on trouve Qwen3-0.6B, le benjamin de la gamme Qwen3 d’Alibaba. Avec ses 600 millions de paramètres, il joue dans la cour des petits modèles, loin des géants du cloud et des meilleurs modèles ouverts.
Baptisé asm-llm-os, ce projet constitue le deuxième volet du dépôt llm.asm, publié sous licence libre MIT par un développeur anonyme (alesha-pro sur GitHub).
Sa particularité ? Tout est codé à la main en assembleur x86-64, le langage le plus proche du processeur, sans passer par un compilateur. Résultat : le noyau (le cœur du système qui dialogue directement avec le matériel) ne pèse que 24 252 octets. Selon les mesures de l’auteur, il affiche l’invite en 74 à 94 millisecondes et crache 134,9 tokens par seconde (un token correspondant grosso modo à un morceau de mot) sur 16 cœurs virtuels d’un processeur serveur AMD Epyc 7642, soit bien plus vite qu’un humain ne peut lire.
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
    Pour aller plus loin
IA locale sur PC et Mac : Bonsai 2.5 code presque aussi bien qu’un modèle 9 fois plus lourd
            
24 Ko de code, mais 640 Mo de modèle
Il y a évidemment une nuance de taille : ces 24 Ko ne représentent que le moteur. Le modèle d’IA lui-même pèse environ 640 Mo, ce qui porte l’image disque complète à près de 700 Mo.
Pour tourner, les exemples réservent 2 Go de mémoire vive, une exigence très modeste pour faire tourner un modèle en local, dont près de 470 Mo dédiés au cache KV, la zone mémoire qui permet au chatbot de garder le fil de la discussion sans tout recalculer à chaque mot.
Autre bémol à garder en tête : toutes les mesures ont été réalisées dans des machines virtuelles (QEMU/KVM et Proxmox).
Ce qui signifie que si le dépôt présente l’image comme démarrable sur un vrai PC, il n’y a eu aucun test sur du matériel physique. La déclinaison Linux du même moteur se vante d’être 18 à 36 % plus rapide que llama.cpp, la référence de l’IA locale, mais uniquement au moment d’écrire la réponse : contrairement à llama.cpp qui avale votre question d’un seul bloc, ce moteur la lit token par token. Le concept n’est d’ailleurs pas totalement inédit, sectorllm faisait déjà tenir un moteur Llama 2 dans 1 356 octets, et NightRun démarre des IA sans OS sur Raspberry Pi 5, mais ici l’ensemble réunit un modèle récent, une vraie conversation suivie et l’exploitation de tous les cœurs du processeur.
Comment ça tient dans si peu de place
Pour réussir cette cure d’amaigrissement extrême, le développeur a tout simplement supprimé tout ce qui n’était pas vital, à commencer par le pilote de disque dur. Au démarrage, le chargeur GRUB dépose directement le modèle en mémoire vive, et le noyau le lit sur place sans aucune copie. L’affichage se contente du bon vieux mode texte VGA, et le clavier passe par le port PS/2. Quant aux poids du modèle, ils sont quantifiés en Q8_0 (stockés sur 8 bits au lieu de 16), ce qui divise leur taille par deux pour une perte de qualité quasi imperceptible selon l’auteur.
Côté calculs, le moteur exploite les instructions AVX2 et FMA, des raccourcis matériels qui permettent au processeur de traiter plusieurs nombres en une seule opération. Sans elles, le système refuse de démarrer, ce qui met hors jeu les puces Intel d’avant 2013. En revanche, la puce IA des PC récents reste totalement inutilisée : tout repose sur le processeur principal, car exploiter le NPU des PC portables imposerait d’écrire un pilote spécifique pour chaque fabricant.
    Pour aller plus loin
NPU des PC portables : à quoi sert vraiment cette puce IA avec ses TOPS, et comment s’en servir ?
            
Comment l’essayer chez soi
Ironie de l’histoire, il faut un PC sous Linux pour compiler ce système qui s’en passe. Une machine équipée de QEMU suffit (avec un processeur compatible AVX2), et la préparation ne prend que trois étapes pour obtenir un chatbot capable de retenir 2 048 tokens de contexte, soit l’équivalent d’une très courte discussion :
- Télécharger Qwen3-0.6B depuis Hugging Face, puis le convertir avec le script Python fourni (numpy et huggingface_hub suffisent).
- Assembler le noyau avec nasm via la commande make os.
- Lancer le tout dans QEMU avec make os-run, ou générer une image ISO (make os-iso) démarrable en BIOS comme en UEFI.
Évidemment, un modèle de 600 millions de paramètres montre vite ses limites au quotidien. Pour un usage concret, mieux vaut se tourner vers un modèle plus costaud comme Inkling 2 Mini sur PC ou Mac, ou un modèle compact optimisé comme Bonsai 2.5. Et pour vérifier ce qui tient réellement dans votre mémoire vive, le guide de QUELLE IA sur quel modèle choisir pour sa machine permet de faire le tri rapidement.
    Pour aller plus loin
C’est sans doute la meilleure IA ouverte à faire tourner en local sur PC et Mac avec moins de 20 Go : voici Inkling 2 Mini

articles.title: We found 60-odd Black Friday deals we love for $100 or less
articles.text:
Between holiday travel, gifts, and the rising cost of just about everything, expenses can quickly add up during this time of year. Thankfully, you don’t have to dip too far into your savings to take advantage of some of the better Black Friday deals we’ve seen.
We found 60-odd Black Friday deals we love for $100 or less
There are still great deals on everything from noise-canceling earbuds and e-readers to the latest smart mugs.
Below, we’ve rounded up a range of great stuff currently on sale for $100 or less, from noise-canceling earbuds and portable Bluetooth speakers to pocket-sized e-readers, photo printers, games, and more. You’ll also find deals on Ember’s temperature-controlled mug, Kodak’s tiny keychain camera, and a variety of Lego sets, all of which would make great holiday gifts or simply a nice treat for yourself.
Disney Plus, Hulu Bundle
You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.
Amazon Echo Time
Although it’s not Amazon’s first bedside alarm clock, the Echo Time is focused on helping you sleep better. The camera-less Alexa speaker can detect your sleep stage via ultrasound and use smart alarms to ease you into the day, but only if you want it to.
Anker Universal Charger (100W)
Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.
HBO Max
An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.
Noco GB40 UltraSafe Jumpstarter
Noco’s Boost GB40 is a rechargeable battery with jumper cables to start six-liter gas or three-liter diesel engines. It also has USB ports so you can charge your phone, ensuring you always have a backup plan.
Apple AirTag (second-gen)
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.
Beats Studio Buds Plus
The Beats Studio Buds Plus sport an eye-catching translucent option and build upon the original with improved sound, better voice quality, and more effective ANC. They also include swappable silicone ear tips and support for native iOS and Android features. Read our review.
Liene Pearl N200 Pro photo printer
The Liene Pearl N200 Pro is a dye-sublimation photo printer that produces vivid, colorful prints for journals, scrapbooks, and more, with an easy-to-use companion app for customization. This particular bundle includes 50 sheets of photo paper and five ink cartridges, though refills are relatively affordable at around $25 for 50 sheets.
Peacock
Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and DreamWorks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.
SwitchBot Bot Rechargeable
Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.
Ember Mug 3 (14-ounce)
Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.
Paramount Plus (monthly subscription)
Paramount Plus Premium provides access to live sports as well as movies and shows from both platforms, including Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, a host of Yellowstone spinoffs, Star Trek shows, Sonic the Hedgehog 3, Twin Peaks, Dexter, and more.
Apple Pencil (USB-C)
Apple’s entry-level stylus attaches magnetically to supported iPads, though it doesn’t support magnetic charging. Instead, you pair and charge it by connecting it to your device’s USB-C port. It includes tilt sensitivity and Apple Pencil Hover support, but it doesn’t offer double-tap gestures or pressure sensitivity.
Beats Studio Pro
The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review.
Nothing Ear 3A earbuds
You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.
Zepath USB-C Li-ion AA Batteries
Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.
Samsung P9 microSD Express card
The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.
Xteink X4 Classic pocket e-reader
With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus
Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.
007 First Light
007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is one of the best action games we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.
Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver
Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.
Lego Project Hail Mary set
Outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary. And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.
Sony DualSense Wireless Controller
Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.
Apple TV (six-month subscription)
Apple TV offers ad-free streaming of original shows and movies, including shows like Severance, Silo, Slow Horses, and Pluribus. The service also features a rotating selection of films, along with live Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches.
Hoto 3.6V Electric Screwdriver Kit Pro
Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.
Moft Trackable Tripod Wallet
Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.
Govee Table Lamp 2
Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.
Sharge Icemag 3 Power Bank
The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.
Saros
Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.
TP-Link Tapo Matter-Certified Smart Plug Mini
TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.
Pixel Buds 2a
Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.
Ghost of Yōtei
Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.
Donkey Kong Bananza
Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Pauline’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.
Lego Mandalorian N-1 Starfighter
Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has re-created here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.
Twelve South AirFly SE
Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.
Catan (6th Edition)
In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.
Nothing Ear (a)
Nothing’s Ear (a) earbuds have the same general design as the company’s previous earbuds — but you can get these in a snazzy yellow. They include ANC, more than decent sound quality, and other features like multipoint for well under $100. Read our impressions.
Control Resonant
Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.
Kodak Charmera Keychain Digital Camera
The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.
Azul
Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.
CMF Headphone Pro
The market is flooded with surprisingly cheap yet good over-ear headphones with active noise cancellation. The Headphone Pro by CMF are certainly some of the best-looking out there, and they come in multiple colors.
Magna-Tile Classic 32-Piece Set
Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge, especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.
Lego Botanicals Mini Bonsai Trees set
Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.
Anker Laptop Power Bank
Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.
CMF Buds 2A
With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.
Wuben G5 rechargeable flashlight
The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.
Anker 140W 2-in-1 USB-C to USB-C Cable
No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.
Echo Dot Max
The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.
Iniu P55-E2 Power Bank (10,000mAh)
Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.
Glocusent Bookmark Style Reading Light
Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.
Vantage
Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan, but it is far more interesting.
LIFX Everyday Smart Light Bulbs (two-pack)
LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices.
Yoto Mini (2024) speaker
A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.
SwitchBot Standing Circulator Fan
A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.
Shokz OpenRun
The standard OpenRun are a lighter option than the newer OpenRun Pro 2, with a streamlined wraparound design, up to eight hours of battery life, and an IP67 rating for better water resistance. However, they don’t offer the same bass performance or USB-C charging.
JBL Go 4
The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.
Pokémon Pokopia
Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep you occupied for hours on end.
Ugreen Nexode 240W USB-C Cable with Digital Display
The proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.
Kobo Remote
The Kobo Remote lets you turn pages on a compatible Kobo e-reader with the click of a button, so you can keep reading without reaching for the screen. It connects directly over Bluetooth and features a curved, handheld design that doesn’t require clipping anything onto your e-reader.
CMF Buds Pro 2
The Buds Pro 2 offer a surprisingly robust set of features for the price, including ANC and a transparency mode that lets you tune into your surroundings. Their included charging case also features a smart dial that lets you adjust the volume, while multipoint Bluetooth support lets them connect to two devices simultaneously.
Fujifilm Instax Mini 13
Fujifilm’s Instax Mini 13 is the best instant camera if you want to spend less than $100. While it lacks more advanced features, the simple instant camera takes good-quality shots quickly and easily and offers a built-in selfie mode along with a self-timer. It’s sold in a variety of fun colors that’ll especially appeal to kids and tweens.
Tile Pro
The Tile Pro is the company’s loudest Bluetooth tracker, one that benefits from a 500-foot range. It also features a user-replaceable battery, unlike some other Tiles, and works with both iOS and Android devices.
Camp Snap 2 digital camera
Camp Snap’s latest digital point-and-shoot camera may still lack a screen and capture only 8-megapixel stills, but it offers a slimmer design, faster performance, and filters right out of the box. That, along with several other new features, makes it easier for kids to use.

articles.title: The man behind Wind Mobile is bringing a new carrier to Canada
articles.text:
The man behind Wind Mobile wants to bring a new wireless carrier to Canada amid ongoing attempts by other providers to consolidate the telecom market.
Anthony Lacavera, the founder and chairman of Toronto-based investment firm Globalive, announced plans to re-enter the Canadian wireless market with a new provider called Paradise Mobile. Backed by Globalive, Paradise Mobile currently operates in Bermuda using a “cloud-native Open RAN 5G network” using in-house AI tools to “automate network operations and improve performance.”
Notably, Lacavera cited awards from Ookla’s Speedtest, which named Paradise as Bermuda’s fastest network in 2025 and 2026. In 2025, Paradise had a median download speed of 376.6Mbps, significantly higher than Bell, often named one of Canada’s fastest networks, with an average speed of 107.5Mbps. Of course, Bermuda is significantly smaller than Canada, so these types of one-to-one comparisons shouldn’t be taken at face value.
Beyond speed, Lacavera pitched a pure wireless play, arguing that Canada’s other national carriers also sell cable, home internet, TV, and other services.
“None of them has a reason to disrupt wireless when doing so risks cannibalizing revenue from their existing customers and legacy businesses. A pure-play operator has one job: win customers with better service and lower prices. That is how Canadian prices come down to global levels,” Lacavera said.
Further, Lacavera said Canada has sky-high wireless rates, which remain among the highest in the world. He argued the only way to lower these prices is by making room for new independent players, especially if something like Quebecor’s bid to buy Telus goes through.
Freedom Mobile owner Quebecor launched an unsolicited bid to acquire the Vancouver-based telecom earlier this month. CEO Pierre Karl Péladeau argued that combining the companies would give them the strength to fight off foreign competition, such as from Elon Musk’s Starlink. Quebecor’s proposal spurred Bell to launch its own bid for Telus — which Quebecor was quick to say would harm competition, as if its own Telus takeover would be any better. And while everyone with a memory long enough to remember the Rogers-Shaw merger knows this would be a bad idea, Prime Minister Mark Carney said that oligopolies “can lead to more competition.” Yeah, sure bud.
Interestingly, Freedom Mobile was once Lacavera’s Wind Mobile before it was acquired by Shaw for $1.6 billion in 2016. As part of Rogers’ acquisition of Shaw in 2023, Freedom was sold to Quebecor for $2.85 billion. However, Lacavera pointed out that Globalive also sought to reacquire Freedom in 2022 for $3.75 billion.
Lacavera told the Globe and Mail that Globalive would attempt to reacquire Freedom Mobile from Quebecor should its bid for Telus go through. He also expressed interest in purchasing assets divested by Bell should it be the one to acquire Telus.
Globalive said its Canada re-entry strategy includes acquiring wireless assets, spectrum, customer base, and retail operations. The company also plans to explore spectrum and network-sharing arrangements and will participate in future federal spectrum auctions.

articles.title: La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal lo confirma: si un vecino o la comunidad deciden instalar cámaras en zonas comunes, puedes apelar al artículo 17.3
articles.text:
Instalar cámaras de vigilancia en las zonas comunes de un edificio no es algo que pueda decidir un vecino por su cuenta, ni siquiera la comunidad de vecinos si no hay una votación con una mayoría concreta. Así lo recoge el artículo 17.3 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, al que puedes apelar si alguien las pone sin ese respaldo.
Qué dice el artículo 17.3. Este apartado de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal incluye la vigilancia entre los servicios comunes de interés general y lo dice de esta manera: “El establecimiento o supresión de los servicios de portería, conserjería, vigilancia u otros servicios comunes de interés general, supongan o no modificación del título constitutivo o de los estatutos, requerirán el voto favorable de las tres quintas partes del total de los propietarios que, a su vez, representen las tres quintas partes de las cuotas de participación”.
Dos mayorías a la vez. Esto significa que la instalación tiene que aprobarse en la junta de propietarios y que el recuento se hace dos veces, por número de propietarios y por cuotas de participación. Vamos, que no basta con reunir a tres de cada cinco propietarios si entre todos no suman también tres quintas partes de las cuotas. Eso sí, esa mayoría es el primer requisito, pero no el único.
Hacia dónde pueden apuntar. Pero aunque la junta dé su aprobación, las cámaras no pueden grabar cualquier cosa. La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) aclara en sus preguntas frecuentes sobre comunidades que “no podrán captarse imágenes de la vía pública a excepción de una franja mínima de los accesos al inmueble”, ni tampoco “imágenes de terrenos y viviendas colindantes o de cualquier otro espacio ajeno”.
Así que, salga la idea de un vecino o de la comunidad, el paso por la junta es obligatorio, porque la ficha de la AEPD sobre cámaras en comunidades recuerda que “para la instalación de cámaras en zonas comunes será necesario el acuerdo de la Junta de Propietarios”.
Foto | Alan J. Hendry

articles.title: A near-mint 1985 Super Mario Bros. just sold for a record $96,875
articles.text:
TL;DR: Classic video games are known to sell for massive amounts of money, with sealed titles regularly fetching hundreds of thousands of dollars at major auction houses. The latest entrant on the list is an original 1985 Super Mario Bros. Nintendo game, which sold at auction for a whopping $96,875.
The complete-in-box unit of the 1985 NES classic went under the hammer at Heritage Auctions in Dallas as part of its Video Games Signature Auction on November 20 - 21. The open-box item contained the original game cartridge, user manual, and everything else Nintendo shipped with the retail pack.
The auction house noted that it's a first-production copy with a "matte sticker" and that it received a near-perfect CIB grade of 9.0 from PSA (Professional Sports Authenticator). The grading suggests the item is in "Near Mint" condition, meaning it's very well preserved with minor signs of wear and tear, despite being tucked away in somebody's attic or basement for more than four decades.
The sale reportedly broke two major records: the highest amount paid for a first-production copy of Super Mario Bros. and the most ever paid for any complete-in-box video game. In a statement announcing the records, Heritage's video game consignment director, Evan Masingill, said, "The importance of Super Mario Bros. to home console gaming is impossible to overstate."
Heritage also auctioned off another original Super Mario Bros. game at the event: a second-production copy in a sealed box with a gloss sticker and an 8.5 PSA grading. It fetched a cool $131,250 - the highest price paid for any item at last week's auction where collectors reportedly spent more than $2.5 million on classic and retro video games.
Other notable items sold at that auction include a sealed copy of Chrono Trigger for the SNES in almost perfect condition with an CGC rating of 9.8 A++ and a sealed copy of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with a PSA rating of 9.8 A++. While the former sold for $81,250, the latter went for $121,875.
The global retro gaming collectibles market is valued at an estimated $4 billion, with some exceptionally rare sealed titles in mint condition fetching millions of dollars at auction. Going by the sale prices at various auction houses, some of the most sought-after titles in the collectibles market include Super Mario Bros., Super Mario 64, Super Mario World, Tetris, The Legend of Zelda, and John Madden Football.
The highest documented auction price for a single video game is an eye-popping $3 million for a sealed second-production copy of Super Mario Bros. with a gloss sticker and a PSA grade of 9.6 A++. It was sold by Heritage last June, surpassing the $2 million record held by an early "hangtab" copy of the same title that sold privately to an unnamed collector in August 2021.

articles.title: Your Firewall Isn't Enough: The Hidden Risk of Unmanaged VMs
articles.text:
When discussing IT infrastructure security, the focus is usually on firewalls, EDR, backup, vulnerability management, and network segmentation. However, all of them are effective only under one condition — if the infrastructure itself is under control.
Incidents often begin not with the exploitation of a vulnerability or bypassing protection systems, but with shortcomings in basic infrastructure management. Every virtual machine, server, access, and IP address must have an owner, a lifetime, and a controlled path for creation and deletion.
When management processes are opaque, the infrastructure itself becomes a source of information security risks, and security tools have to operate over an unknown environment and merely contain the consequences.
This principle is equally critical for enterprise companies and service providers — regardless of whether the platform serves internal services, development teams, or external customers, a loss of control over administration can lead to the compromise of the entire environment.
Why Security Grows Out of Manageability
In modern IT infrastructure, hundreds of systems run on the same resources, and the environment itself is constantly changing — dozens of services are created, scaled, and deleted daily.
In such conditions, provisioning comes to the fore. Deploying a new virtual machine without a regulation and recording the owner leaves "forgotten" VMs in the environment. They do not receive updates, fall out of monitoring, and become an easy entry point for an attacker.
Centralized access management is no less critical. The platform must delineate the rights of users and administrators and record all operations; otherwise, excessive rights accumulate, allowing attackers to move laterally across the network.
We should not forget about the isolation of environments — the resources of different customers at a hosting provider, or internal systems, external services, and development environments in corporate IT infrastructure. If isolation is violated, an incident in the test environment can affect business-critical services.
All this is impossible without lifecycle control — linking capacity allocation to billing, quotas, and timely deletion of resources, so that outdated accounts and "abandoned" IP addresses do not remain in the network.
Finally, manageability is impossible without accurate accounting of the physical layer: the appearance, decommissioning, and movement of servers between racks and sites. Inaccurate accounting generates unaccounted servers and loss of control over security configurations.
Therefore, the foundation of information security is the transparency of resource management throughout their entire lifecycle.
Bring Virtualization and Infrastructure Management Under Control
ISPsystem brings VM management, physical infrastructure inventory, and resource lifecycle workflows together in one environment.
See how VMmanager, DCImanager, and BILLmanager help teams gain visibility and control across their IT infrastructure.
Explore ISPsystem
Migration from VMware and the Change in the Management Model
Broadcom's change in licensing policy forced companies to reconsider their infrastructure strategies and look for alternatives to VMware — for example, considering Proxmox VE, OpenStack, and other open-source solutions. However, migrating to a new platform requires more than just the correct transfer of virtual machines.
Over the years of working with VMware, many have become accustomed to perceiving it as a single whole — virtualization, resource management, access, automation, and accounting.
When migrating to another stack, it quickly becomes clear that virtualization is not equal to infrastructure management: the hypervisor is just one element, and the remaining functions have to be assembled from several independent solutions.
Proxmox and OpenStack solve virtualization tasks on their own, but without additional software, they do not cover operational processes and control over the other layers of the environment. As a result, organizations have to independently integrate equipment management systems, resource accounting, access control, and inventory.
The more individual components in the infrastructure, the harder it is to maintain unified security policies — risks arise of losing a unified RBAC, end-to-end inventory, action auditing, and automation.
Therefore, it is important to view migration from VMware not just as a change of hypervisor, but as a revision of the entire infrastructure management model: if centralized control, automation, and lifecycle management are postponed for later, over time they become a source of new risks.
Which Processes a Management Platform Must Cover
After abandoning VMware, companies face the main question — how to rebuild infrastructure management.
When choosing a replacement, it is important to look not only at the capabilities of the hypervisor itself but also at what operational and security processes the chosen solution can cover and what additional integrations will be required.
At the foundation, there should be centralized management of the entire environment from a single interface and role-based access control (RBAC).
Equally important are the isolation of environments or customers, transparent resource accounting, and control of the entire lifecycle — from the creation of a virtual machine to its deletion and the revocation of access.
Also, the platform must manage the physical layer of servers and automate routine operations.
Such an architecture can be built in different ways: assembled from separate open-source tools and independently solving the issue of their integration, or by choosing a ready-made comprehensive solution.
Regardless of the approach, it is precisely the coverage of these processes that returns the infrastructure to the transparency and manageability that the VMware ecosystem previously provided.
How to Build a Unified Management Environment
To avoid assembling infrastructure management from disparate systems, all these processes can be combined within a single ISPsystem product stack.
In this architecture, VMmanager is responsible for virtualization, DCImanager for the physical level of the infrastructure, and BILLmanager acts as the end-to-end layer for resource provisioning, quotas, accounting, and FinOps.
VMmanager automates the lifecycle of virtual machines, including deployment with a preinstalled software stack, and scales up to 60,000 VMs and 700 nodes in a single environment.
Network isolation based on VxLAN supports more than 16 million isolated segments between geographically distributed sites, and a self-service portal is provided for users.
In parallel, DCImanager provides centralized management and full inventory of the physical layer in multi-vendor environments — from servers to switches and UPSs. The platform checks equipment health and disk S.M.A.R.T. data, configures BMC, performs secure drive wiping, automatically installs the OS, monitors hardware status, and controls warranty periods.
All three products integrate seamlessly with each other and work as a single environment, and if necessary, can interact with external solutions — for example, with OpenStack. BILLmanager acts as the end-to-end layer here: it links the provisioning of IT resources with authorization and accounting, allows assembling combined services, and implements showback and chargeback mechanisms.
The built-in BI module with customizable dashboards for analyzing resource utilization deserves special attention. In a corporate environment, it helps to find "abandoned" capacity in time, which development teams forget to delete after completing tasks — such servers do not sit idle without updates and control, and the company reduces hardware and license costs.
How Implementing a Unified Management Environment Affects IT Infrastructure Security
When the processes of managing virtualization, physical equipment, and the resource lifecycle are linked into a single environment, security ceases to be just a set of protective tools and becomes the result of systemic manageability.
Information security and operations teams get a transparent picture of the entire environment — from the physical server to the virtual machine, its owner, and the history of changes, which directly reduces the number of "blind spots."
Automation of provisioning, delineation of rights, and control over resource lifetimes reduce the risk of errors in issuing access, the appearance of unaccounted servers, and the retention of "forgotten" virtual machines. This also simplifies the migration from VMware itself: companies do not just replace the hypervisor, but build a transparent and manageable operating model.
As a result, infrastructure security relies not only on individual security tools but also on the management system itself, which makes the environment predictable, controllable, and resilient to risks.

articles.title: Près de 20 ans après la sortie de ces anciennes cartes graphiques AMD, une IA aide enfin à corriger un bug qui corrompait la lecture des vidéos sous Linux
articles.text:
Près de 20 ans après la sortie de ces anciennes cartes graphiques AMD, une IA aide enfin à corriger un bug qui corrompait la lecture des vidéos sous Linux
Le développeur Ted Bullock a trouvé une solution à un bug qui touchait la lecture des vidéos sous Linux sur son ancien iMac de 2007. Et pour corriger ce problème qui concerne plusieurs cartes graphiques des séries Radeon HD 2000 et HD 3000 d'AMD, l'homme s'est fait aider par Codex, l'IA d'OpenAI.
C'est en août 2007 qu'Apple a présenté la nouvelle génération de ses iMac avec un écran de 20 ou 24 pouces et un processeur Intel Core 2 Duo. Ted Bullock utilise justement l'une de ces machines avec une Mobility Radeon HD 2400 XT et ses 128 Mo de mémoire vidéo. Sauf que voilà, les images de ses vidéos étaient corrompues sous Linux. Le développeur a donc utilisé Codex, l'IA d'OpenAI, pour corriger un problème qui touchait plusieurs cartes graphiques des séries Radeon HD 2000 et HD 3000 d'AMD.
Codex lui a permis de trouver un bug de Linux
À l'époque, l'un des arguments de vente des Radeon HD 2400 et HD 2600 fut leur décodeur vidéo appelé UVD (Unified Video Decoder). Il s'agit d'une partie de la puce graphique qui s'occupe du décodage des vidéos au format H.264 ou VC-1 à la place du processeur. L'intérêt était notamment de soulager la puce graphique pendant la lecture de films en Blu-ray.
C'est cette partie de la carte graphique qui posait problème sur l'iMac de Ted Bullock. L'homme a réalisé ses essais sous Debian, une distribution Linux, et a découvert que le problème se manifestait quand le décodeur récupérait les données vidéo dans la mémoire vive de l'ordinateur alors que la puce graphique effectuait d'autres opérations d'affichage.
Ted Bullock a constaté que les images s'affichaient correctement dès lors que les données à décoder étaient stockées dans la mémoire dédiée à la carte graphique, la fameuse VRAM. Le problème disparaissait aussi quand il interrompait les autres opérations graphiques.
L'homme a alors soumis sa proposition de correctif aux développeurs du noyau Linux. "J'ai utilisé Codex pour m'aider dans les recherches, les tests et la préparation du correctif", explique Ted Bullock dans son message. Il aura suffi d'ajouter sept lignes et d'en supprimer deux dans le code du pilote Radeon. Ted Bullock a repris une solution déjà employée pour éviter des problèmes d'affichage similaires sur d'autres anciennes puces graphiques AMD.
Linux 7.5 corrigera ce vieux bug graphique
Le correctif concerne cinq références de puces graphiques, les RV610, RV620, RV630, RV635 et RV670. Toutes partagent le même micrologiciel pour leur décodeur vidéo. Ted Bullock précise toutefois que d'autres utilisateurs devront réaliser des essais sur les références qu'il ne possède pas.
Alex Deucher, qui travaille chez AMD sur les pilotes graphiques pour Linux, a accepté le correctif le 2 novembre avant de l'inclure, dix jours plus tard, dans les modifications prévues pour Linux 7.5. Il faut savoir que si ces cartes graphiques remontent à 2007, les développeurs du pilote libre Radeon ont attendu 2014 et Linux 3.18 pour prendre en charge leur décodeur vidéo. Impossible donc de dater précisément l'apparition du bug.
AMD a arrêté depuis longtemps le développement de ses pilotes propriétaires pour ces cartes graphiques qui n'ont même pas bénéficié d'un pilote officiel du constructeur pour Windows 10. Pourtant, 19 ans après leur commercialisation, leurs propriétaires vont encore profiter d'une correction logicielle grâce au travail d'un utilisateur de Linux.

articles.title: Grafana Begins Its Biggest UI Refresh Since Version 7
articles.text:
Grafana Labs has introduced the first phase of its biggest visual refresh since Grafana 7, bringing updated themes, more consistent interface components, and improved visual hierarchy to its observability platform. Introduced as part of Grafana 13.3, the refresh is now available in public preview across Grafana Cloud and self-managed deployments.
The changes address a growing problem as Grafana has expanded: years of rapid feature development have created design inconsistencies, competing visual elements, and different interaction patterns across the platform. Rather than introducing a complete redesign, Grafana is standardising its existing interface while retaining familiar navigation and plugin compatibility.
The longer-term objective is to make the platform easier to use as observability workflows increasingly incorporate AI assistants and agent-driven interactions.
Grafana's extensive growth has brought support for a broad range of observability use cases, but this has also introduced what the company describes as design debt. Different parts of the interface have evolved independently, resulting in inconsistent visual cues, component variations, and interaction patterns.
The design refresh is intended to address these inconsistencies without slowing the platform's continued development. Grafana wants users to learn an interaction pattern once and apply that knowledge consistently across dashboards, panels, drawers, and other parts of the interface.
The work has also been influenced by the development of Grafana Assistant and Assistant Workspace, which introduced new interaction patterns for AI-powered workflows and prompted the design team to reconsider the platform's visual language.
New default light and dark themes use redesigned colour palettes intended to improve accessibility. Grafana has also reduced the number of available component variations, helping standardise how common interface elements behave.
Typography, borders, shadows and visual layering have been updated to create a clearer information hierarchy. The intention is to reduce competing visual elements and make it easier for users to identify important information when investigating incidents or exploring data.
These changes extend across fundamental interface components, including cards, panels, and drawers. Rather than simply applying a new visual style, Grafana is revisiting the underlying design primitives so that the interface remains consistent as the product evolves.
An interesting motivation behind the refresh is Grafana's view that traditional graphical interfaces will increasingly coexist with terminal-based and agentic chat interactions.
As more workflows become accessible through AI assistants, the remaining graphical interactions need to be particularly clear and predictable. Users should be able to understand the information presented, recognise important changes and move between workflows without having to relearn different interface conventions.
This makes visual consistency more than a cosmetic exercise. It becomes part of ensuring that engineers can work effectively across both traditional observability interfaces and newer AI-assisted experiences.
Grafana is deliberately introducing the refresh in phases, allowing users and contributors to adapt while providing feedback before further changes are made.
Importantly, the company describes this as a visual refresh rather than a complete redesign. Existing navigation remains unchanged, and the update introduces no breaking changes for plugins.
Self-managed users can enable the new styling through the grafana.visualDesignRefresh feature toggle and can switch back to the previous appearance if required. Grafana Cloud users can also access the public preview.
The company has encouraged feedback through its community Slack and an in-app survey, using early adoption and user responses to guide subsequent iterations.
Other observability platforms, including Datadog and New Relic, have also invested in simplifying how engineers navigate increasingly complex monitoring environments. Grafana's challenge is particularly interesting given its open-source ecosystem, where plugins and contributions introduce additional interface requirements.
The refresh reflects a broader product engineering principle: as platforms grow, maintaining consistency becomes as important as introducing new functionality.
For observability tools, where engineers often work under pressure during production incidents, reducing cognitive overhead can directly improve how quickly they find and interpret relevant information.
Grafana's refresh is therefore less about changing how the platform works and more about making its growing capabilities easier to understand and use. As AI increasingly changes how engineers interact with observability systems, a clear and consistent graphical experience remains an important part of the overall design.

articles.title: Los asistentes de IA que pagan por el usuario enfrentan su primera gran prueba en Black Friday
articles.text:
Google, Amazon, Meta y OpenAI quieren que sus asistentes de inteligencia artificial elijan los regalos de las fiestas. Según Bloomberg y Fortune, la temporada que arrancó con el Black Friday será la primera en que esos programas, capaces incluso de pagar por el usuario, se prueben a gran escala frente a un público desconfiado.
La Federación Nacional de Minoristas de Estados Unidos (NRF) prevé ventas navideñas por más de USD 1 billón en ese país. Los comercios observarán si los compradores usan la IA solo para pedir ideas o si la dejan completar la transacción, según Fortune.
Bloomberg plantea de qué asistente aceptarán consejos los compradores. El texto abre con un corredor que fotografió un anuncio de Instagram y le preguntó a ChatGPT si el producto valía su precio. El bot le sugirió una tabla de equilibrio que costaba la mitad.
Ese es el uso dominante hoy: buscar y comparar, no comprar. Una encuesta de Morning Consult para Visa, de octubre, halló que el 54% de los adultos estadounidenses ya usó IA en al menos una tarea de compra, frente al 47% del año anterior. Solo el 23% confía en que gestione pagos por ellos.
Cada empresa juega su carta
OpenAI presentó este mes una billetera digital, “Wallet”, que se conecta con American Express, Visa y Mastercard para que sus agentes cierren pagos dentro de los límites que fije el cliente, informó Fortune. Walmart anunció este año un acuerdo con Google para vender mediante Gemini, y Target permite pedir ideas de regalos dentro de ChatGPT.
Meta lanzó Muse, un agente que, según CNBC, concentra el 70% del tráfico de agentes de IA en comercios y más de la mitad de las solicitudes a páginas de pago. Datos de la firma Human Security indican que el tráfico de agentes durante la Cyber Week, del 26 al 30 de noviembre, se multiplicará por 150 respecto del año anterior.
Amazon, en cambio, bloqueó a Muse en septiembre, recogió Fortune. eMarketer añadió que la empresa estaría en conversaciones con Meta para ofrecerle un conector. Walmart eligió otro camino: dejó que Muse venda sus ofertas del Black Friday, con salvaguardas para limitar el acceso de Meta a los datos de los compradores.
Los números siguen siendo pequeños
Un análisis de Bain & Company sobre datos de Similarweb, citado por Fortune, indica que los asistentes de IA generan menos del 1% del tráfico web de los minoristas. En el primer trimestre, las visitas a tiendas estadounidenses llegadas desde la IA subieron 393% interanual, desde una base muy baja, según datos de Adobe citados por eMarketer.
El rendimiento de los agentes tampoco convence. Visa encargó este otoño a 22 agentes personales que compraran un televisor, una computadora portátil y un secador de pelo, con 15 intentos cada uno. Solo el 57% terminó en una compra adecuada o en una sugerencia apropiada, indicó Fortune. Muchos agentes no preguntaron datos clave, como si el televisor servía para videojuegos.
Los consumidores distinguen entre tipos de compra. Una encuesta de American Express halló que el 52% de los estadounidenses acepta que un agente adquiera artículos baratos, como comestibles, pero solo el 15% lo admite para electrónicos y electrodomésticos. La plataforma de marketing Zeta encontró que el 9% dejaría que la IA compre regalos sin revisarlos antes.
Quién responde si el bot se equivoca
Para Katherine Black, socia de la consultora Kearney, los clientes necesitan saber qué pasará si algo sale mal. Walmart informó en octubre que su política de devoluciones rige aunque el error sea de la IA. American Express planea lanzar una protección para cargos que un agente registrado haga en contra de las instrucciones del cliente.
Anna Marrs, directiva de American Express para comercios y redes de pago, dijo a Fortune que la IA generativa influirá más este año como herramienta de búsqueda que como comprador. “Va a crecer a la velocidad de la confianza”, afirmó.
Salesforce calcula que solo el 8% de los consumidores autorizó a un agente a comprar en su nombre y que cerca de tres cuartos no está dispuesto a darle los datos de su tarjeta.

articles.title: Gelo marinho da Antártida está desaparecendo até quando deveria avançar
articles.text:
A Antártida está enfrentando uma redução incomum na cobertura de gelo marinho. Em outubro deste ano, observações de satélite registraram níveis diários inferiores até mesmo aos observados no mesmo mês de 2023, quando a região já havia enfrentado condições extremas.
Segundo dados divulgados pela Divisão Antártica Australiana, a extensão do gelo chegou a aproximadamente 2,3 milhões de quilômetros quadrados em meados de outubro. O valor representa uma redução de 12% em relação à média histórica para o período e estabelece um novo mínimo para essa época do ano.
O recuo aconteceu depois que a cobertura atingiu seu máximo anual de inverno: 17,72 milhões de km², em 11 de setembro. Esse foi o terceiro menor pico registrado desde o início das observações por satélite, em 1979.
Nas quatro semanas seguintes, aproximadamente 1,3 milhão de km² de gelo desapareceram da cobertura marinha ao redor do continente.
Gelo está diminuindo quando deveria avançar
- A extensão do gelo marinho antártico passa por um ciclo sazonal intenso. Durante o inverno, a camada congelada avança sobre o oceano; no verão, recua novamente;
- O problema é que esse comportamento está mudando. Segundo os pesquisadores, a redução da cobertura agora também ocorre em períodos nos quais o oceano deveria estar congelando e o gelo se expandindo;
- As quatro menores extensões máximas anuais de inverno observadas desde 1979 aconteceram nos últimos quatro anos. Além disso, os dados de satélite mostram que o congelamento começa mais tarde e o derretimento acontece mais cedo em diversas regiões;
- Com isso, a temporada anual de gelo marinho ficou até três ou quatro meses mais curta em algumas áreas da Antártida;
- A mudança também deixou de ficar concentrada em regiões específicas. Se, em décadas anteriores, as menores extensões costumavam aparecer principalmente a oeste da Península Antártica, atualmente níveis reduzidos são observados ao redor de todo o continente, tanto no verão quanto no inverno.
Leia mais:
- Quebra de plataforma deixa geleira da Antártida mais vulnerável
- Buraco quase do tamanho de Portugal surge no gelo da Antártida
- Saiba como o gelo da Antártida se transformou em um detector de partículas cósmicas
Redução ameaça pinguins e outros animais
O gelo marinho tem funções importantes para o equilíbrio ambiental da Antártida. Sua superfície branca reflete a luz solar, ajuda a regular a temperatura dos oceanos e influencia as trocas de calor, umidade e gases entre a água e a atmosfera.
A camada congelada também funciona como proteção para áreas costeiras e plataformas de gelo, reduzindo o impacto das ondas. Quando essa barreira diminui, mais energia chega à costa, o que pode aumentar o risco de desprendimento de icebergs e comprometer a estabilidade dessas estruturas.
Os efeitos também atingem diretamente os animais que dependem do gelo para sobreviver.
Os pinguins-imperadores, por exemplo, utilizam plataformas estáveis de gelo costeiro para se reproduzir. Um estudo citado pela Divisão Antártica Australiana identificou que a cobertura excepcionalmente baixa no fim de 2023 provocou o rompimento dessas plataformas antes que muitos filhotes desenvolvessem penas impermeáveis. O resultado foi o fracasso reprodutivo em aproximadamente 20% das colônias da espécie na Antártida.
O krill antártico também depende do gelo marinho. Suas larvas encontram abrigo sob a camada congelada e se alimentam de algas microscópicas que crescem nesse ambiente durante o inverno.
A redução do gelo pode comprometer essa fonte de alimento e provocar efeitos em cadeia na rede alimentar do Oceano Antártico.
Cientistas ainda investigam as causas
A queda na cobertura de gelo marinho observada desde 2015 está associada ao aumento do calor nas camadas superiores do oceano, combinado a mudanças nos padrões de vento e na temperatura da atmosfera.
Apesar dos avanços nas pesquisas, os cientistas ressaltam que ainda existem dúvidas sobre os mecanismos que explicam as mudanças, sua distribuição e os impactos ambientais.
Para investigar essas questões, o Programa Antártico Australiano planeja uma expedição em 2028 à zona marginal de gelo da Antártida Oriental. A região, localizada na área de transição entre o oceano aberto e a cobertura congelada, concentra processos importantes de formação e derretimento do gelo.
Os pesquisadores pretendem estudar a influência de ondas, tempestades, calor oceânico e condições atmosféricas sobre a dinâmica do gelo, além das consequências para os ecossistemas e para a capacidade do Oceano Antártico de absorver dióxido de carbono.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Bewusstseins-Debatte bei Anthropics KI: Warum dieser Philosoph einem Trugschluss aufsitzt
articles.text:
Bewusstseins-Debatte über Anthropics KI: Warum dieser Philosoph einem Trugschluss aufsitzt
Vor seinem Börsengang am 19. November nannte Anthropic die Möglichkeit, dass Künstliche Intelligenz bewusst oder empfindungsfähig sein könnte, als Risikofaktor für jeden, der in das Unternehmen investiert. Angesichts „unserer Herangehensweise an die Empfindungsfähigkeit und den moralischen Status von Modellen“, so schrieb Anthropic – also das Unternehmen, das damit ausdrücken will, dass es diese Möglichkeit ernster nimmt als jedes andere KI-Unternehmen –, könnte es mehr Regeln und Einschränkungen einführen als seine Konkurrenten, um sicherzustellen, dass seine KI-Modelle gut behandelt werden.
Anthropic zählt eine Reihe angesehener Philosophen zu seinen Anhänger:innen, und die Argumentation des Unternehmens lautet in etwa wie folgt: Heutige KI sei vielleicht nicht bewusst, auch wenn wir das nicht mit Sicherheit wissen können. Aber die Wahrscheinlichkeit von Empfindungsfähigkeit steige, je leistungsfähiger die KI werde. Was schließlich bedeute, dass wir uns auf eine nahe Zukunft vorbereiten sollten, in der KI-Systeme nicht nur eigene Absichten und Ziele entwickeln, sondern auch „moralische Bedeutung“ haben. Somit sei es wichtig, sie vor Schaden zu schützen.
Umfragen über die strittige These, ob KI ein Bewusstsein hat
Laut einer aktuellen Umfrage glauben 33 Prozent der US-Bevölkerung, dass KI-Systeme irgendwann definitiv oder wahrscheinlich Bewusstsein entwickeln werden, und sieben Prozent geben an, dass sie bereits über Bewusstsein verfügen. In einer 2020 durchgeführten Umfrage hatten von 1.092 Philosoph:innenen 39 Prozent angegeben, dass einige zukünftige KI-Systeme bewusstseinsfähig sein werden. Zum Vergleich: Die Philosoph:innen waren sich weniger sicher, ob Würmer oder Fliegen über Bewusstsein verfügen.
Doch bei Anthropics Börsengang letzte Woche geriet die Offenheit des Unternehmens gegenüber der Frage nach dem Bewusstsein aus einer ziemlich unbequemen Quelle unter Beschuss: von einem der Philosophen, die unser Verständnis von Bewusstsein überhaupt erst geprägt haben – Thomas Nagel.

articles.title: Consiguen ejecutar GTA 6 en Mac, pero hay un detalle que cambia todo
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 no tendrá una versión para Mac, pero eso no significa que los usuarios de Apple se vayan a quedar sin probarlo. Algunos desarrolladores están desarrollando ports para macOS basándose en la versión filtrada del juego para Xbox Series X|S. El desarrollo todavía se encuentra en una fase muy temprana, aunque ya es posible ejecutar GTA 6 en una Mac.
De acuerdo con MacRumors, varios proyectos de la comunidad han logrado correr GTA 6 de forma nativa en Macs con Apple Silicon. El resultado está lejos de ofrecer la experiencia que vemos en PS5 o Xbox, ya que el juego apenas alcanza los 3 fotogramas por segundo y está cargado de errores visuales. No obstante, una de las partes más difíciles se ha conseguido y solo queda ver si Rockstar Games y Take-Two no tomarán represalias.
Actualmente existen dos proyectos que intentan llevar GTA 6 a Mac. El más conocido es VIctory-macOS, que se basa en el trabajo realizado por VIctory para ejecutar la versión de Xbox Series X|S en Mac mediante Wine, Rosetta 2 y D3D Metal. Según el repositorio de GitHub, la versión actual todavía no es jugable, pero los desarrolladores han conseguido iniciar el juego, mostrar menús y pantallas de carga y acceder a algunas partes del mapa en equipos con chips M2 Pro, M3 Max y M5 Pro.
La última actualización afirma que el rendimiento ha mejorado notablemente durante la carga, pasando de 8 fps a 26 o 30 fps en ciertos escenarios. Los desarrolladores mencionan que el principal cuello de botella es el rendimiento dentro del juego, que suele moverse a un fotograma cada dos segundos.
GTA 6 está todavía lejos de tener una versión jugable en Mac
El segundo proyecto es Halfwave: VIctory, otra bifurcación que añade optimizaciones para el Apple Silicon y que combina mejoras de distintos forks del original. En esta versión, los desarrolladores lograron ejecutar el juego, aunque corre a 3-5 fotogramas por segundo en un MacBook Pro con M4 Pro con 48 GB de memoria.
El repositorio de GitHub menciona que la actualización más reciente permite controlar a Jason. Las partidas guardadas funcionan y pueden cargarse correctamente. También se renderizan elementos como la iluminación solar, sombras, personajes, ropa y reflejos en agua y superficies metálicas. Una prueba en la primera misión del bote alcanzó los 6 fps a una resolución 1080p.
Al igual que VIctory-macOS, Halfwave no es jugable a velocidad normal y todavía existen muchos glitches en la parte visual. Por ejemplo, algunos objetos parpadean en negro, el raytracing está deshabilitado para ciertos reflejos y la iluminación nocturna todavía no coincide con lo que vemos en consola.
GTA 6 fue desarrollado para una arquitectura distinta a la de los Mac, por lo que necesita varias capas de traducción para poder ejecutarse. En los ports basados en VIctory, Rosetta 2 convierte las instrucciones del juego para que puedan ser interpretadas por los chips de Apple, mientras que CrossOver y Wine permiten correr componentes pensados para Windows. Al mismo tiempo, D3DMetal traduce las instrucciones gráficas de DirectX 12 al lenguaje Metal que utilizan las GPU de los Mac.
Es difícil saber si estas versiones conseguirán su objetivo. Take-Two ya comenzó con la cacería y hace unos días eliminó más de 3.000 repositorios. La casa matriz de Rockstar Games no descansará hasta acabar con cualquier intento no autorizado de lanzar GTA 6 en otras plataformas.

articles.title: MacBook Air OLED : Apple ne changerait pas que l’écran, mais il va falloir être patient
articles.text:
Commercialisé depuis 2022 dans son design actuel, le MacBook Air d’Apple a pris un coup de vieux depuis la sortie du nouveau MacBook PROLED XDR. Si le géant de Cupertino compte rafraîchir la gamme début 2027 avec l’intégration d’une puce M6 aux côtés d’un nouveau MacBook Neo 2, le design de cette version ne changerait pas tout de suite. Il faudra pour cela attendre la fin de l’année 2027, voire 2028.
Enfin un MacBook OLED grand public ?
Après avoir introduit des dalles OLED tactiles sur ses MacBook Pro en 2026 avec les modèles PROLED, Apple chercherait à décliner cette technologie d’affichage sur son MacBook Air. Pour rappel, l’intégration de l’OLED sur un ordinateur portable apporte des noirs profonds et un contraste infini, mais coûte également bien plus cher. Alors que le modèle Pro commence à 3 299 euros, le MacBook Air actuel commence à 1 399 euros. Pour maintenir cet écart de tarif, la marque pourrait choisir de proposer une version OLED de son MacBook Air en plus d’une version LCD plus classique.
Ce serait un saut important pour le plus populaire des ordinateurs portables d’Apple, qui a le même design depuis 2022, date à laquelle Apple avait aussi réintroduit le port MagSafe. L’ajout d’une version 15 pouces en 2023 a également été une bonne surprise, mais la gamme se contente depuis de mises à jour incrémentales.
Une mise à jour du MacBook Air avant une version OLED
Dans son podcast Power On, Mark Gurman penche davantage pour une sortie en 2028 qu’en fin d’année 2027. Une fenêtre de lancement plus éloignée s’expliquerait par des contraintes industrielles et le besoin d’amortir les technologies déjà utilisées sur la version Pro. Avant ce grand changement, le MacBook Air pourrait connaître une autre mise à jour qui introduirait la puce M6 dès le début de l’année 2027. L’écran OLED n’arriverait donc pas avant 2028 sur le MacBook Air.
Pour le moment, ces informations sont non officielles et sujettes à des changements de la part d’Apple. Comme toujours les propriétaires de MacBook Air devront arbitrer entre un nouveau modèle « simplement » plus puissant, ou attendre encore un peu plus pour profiter d’une nouvelle technologie d’écran et d’un nouveau design.
