articles.title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes give AI agents a place to run
articles.text:
AWS Nitro Sandboxes give AI agents a place to run
A coding agent has written a script and wants to run it. The script may do exactly what the developer asked. The next decision, though, belongs to humans.
The team building the system has to answer a slew of questions: Where should that code run? What should it be able to reach once it starts?
The script doesn’t get a vote.
At the recent KubeCon + CloudNativeCon conference in Salt Lake City, The New Stack’s Frederic Lardinois asked AWS Senior Product Manager Mike Stefaniak what’s keeping more teams from running agents in production.
Stefaniak said he’s seen a handful of large customers commit in a big way. Many others are still figuring out security and identity. AWS Nitro Sandboxes, announced at the conference, address one part of that problem by giving developers an isolated place to run container workloads.
Keep the image, change where it runs
Stefaniak describes Nitro Sandboxes as a way to bring the isolation of the Nitro hypervisor to multiple workloads within one EC2 instance. Each sandbox draws CPU and memory from the parent instance.
“You don’t have to change your container image.”
On EKS Auto Mode or ECS Managed Instances, Stefaniak says, a runtime configuration tells AWS to place the workload in a sandbox.
“You don’t have to change your container image.”
That’s important to a developer with an existing build pipeline who wants to change how a workload runs without rebuilding the application around a new packaging model. Teams operating standard EC2 instances can also use the sandboxes, Stefaniak says, with more setup to wire up the runtime.
The use case extends beyond agents. A SaaS provider might otherwise put customers on separate nodes or clusters to isolate their workloads. Stefaniak sees an opportunity to run multiple tenants on the same node while keeping their workloads isolated. That could mean fewer clusters to look after, a benefit that anyone who has spent an afternoon coordinating upgrades can appreciate.
Decide what can leave the sandbox
Stefaniak distinguishes between isolated and confidential modes. In confidential mode, he says, the parent instance can’t inspect what’s inside the sandbox. Attestation also opens up a distribution option for a software vendor or model provider. It can ship encrypted code or model artifacts to a customer and use policy to control where they can be decrypted and run.
“Isolation is one piece of the puzzle when it comes to running agents.”
A workload with no need for network access can run in a confidential sandbox configured without a network interface. An agent that needs to call a model or query a service raises a different set of questions.
“Isolation is one piece of the puzzle when it comes to running agents,” Stefaniak said.
Stefaniak identifies workload identity and egress controls as two other pieces. Teams need to decide what identity an agent uses and which destinations it can reach. He describes customers who want model calls to go through an approved gateway, where they can apply governance policies and track spending. AWS is exploring how to enforce that path, including a possible role for Envoy.
“I think the tipping point is close.”
The interview also gets into what AWS contributed to Linux and containerd and why the company wants Nitro Sandboxes to work with emerging open source orchestration projects.
Stefaniak says the integration with Agent Sandbox is already working and describes the Agent Substrate work as an early proof of concept. “I think the tipping point is close,” Stefaniak said.
Watch the full interview on The New Stack’s YouTube channel for Stefaniak’s take on what would make teams comfortable moving agents into production, how SaaS developers might use the same isolation, and why some of the hardest work starts when an agent needs to reach outside its sandbox.

articles.title: Wealthsimple’s changes to rates and rewards draw online backlash
articles.text:
Wealthsimple announced a series of changes to its financial products this week, including rollbacks of rewards, prompting backlash from some users.
The news: Fintech company Wealthsimple said on Wednesday that it is removing some benefits but also adding new perks across its product suite. It eliminated cash back incentives on foreign purchases made with the year-old Wealthsimple credit card, replaced its milestone rewards program with “partner offers,” and changed the eligibility for Premium status.
It also reduced interest rates across its standard and USD chequing accounts, but increased the savings account interest rates for Premium and Generation clients and introduced a new high-interest USD savings account.
From the source: Hundreds of users on social media platforms X and Reddit expressed disappointment about the changes, with some likening the move to a “bait-and-switch” strategy. One user noted it makes Wealthsimple feel more like a traditional bank.
Wealthsimple executives, like chief growth officer Simon Lejeune, responded to some of the online comments. “We tried to bundle our changes this time around to avoid [too] much back and forth. It should stabilize for a while now,” he wrote on X.
In a statement to BetaKit, a Wealthsimple spokesperson acknowledged that some of the changes “may be disappointing because some benefits are going away, but others are being added.” The spokesperson said the company’s mission to offer Canadians the “best financial experience and products possible” hasn’t changed.
The context: With more than 4 million users, Wealthsimple is serving more customers than it ever has. More financing has accompanied this strong growth. Last month, the company announced $425 million in Series F financing from existing investors at a $13.8-billion post-money valuation. It now claims to serve a quarter of Canadians aged 18 to 40 and to hold more than $169 billion in assets under administration.
In its explanation to customers, the company acknowledged that this growth and usage of certain products is part of why some of its offerings are changing. Its statement said that the company had not expected how much users would spend in other currencies using its credit card; and because it wants to offer the card to more Canadians, it had to choose between offering cash back and covering FX fees.
Final thought: Wealthsimple has positioned itself as an alternative to Canada’s big banks by offering attractive perks and doing away with monthly fees for consumers. It also successfully advocated for a ban on investment and registered account transfer fees—something that would make it less costly for consumers to transfer their holdings to Wealthsimple.
This competitive pressure appears to have reached some of Canada’s Big Six banks. This week, National Bank announced a no-fee everyday banking account for Canadians.
Disclosure: Wealthsimple vice-president of payments strategy and chief compliance officer, Hanna Zaidi, sits on BetaKit’s board of directors.
Feature image courtesy Wealthsimple.

articles.title: Researcher finds unprotected database with about 2 billion credentials, the largest he's ever seen
articles.text:
Ripple effect: Ethical security researcher Jeremiah Fowler recently uncovered a massive unsecured database containing around two billion potentially compromised account credentials. A single database was apparently hosting several collections of account credentials from multiple security incidents, and anyone could download the data before the host decided to block access.
Fowler said that the database he discovered was neither protected by a password nor encrypted in any way. Around 2 billion credentials were just sitting there, waiting for someone to grab the data and use it to launch further attacks against users. The dataset included email addresses, logins and other user IDs, passwords, and more.
The researcher probed the online database by reviewing the neatly organized data, finding additional content types such as application credentials, browser passwords, cookies, session tokens, and other "identifiers." Fowler said that this was the largest collection of compromised accounts he had ever found. The dataset was more than 13 times bigger than an exposure he previously reported and included a lot more device-specific data for potential attackers to exploit.
The database was also noteworthy for how the plaintext data was organized in thousands of different folders, with some documents grouped by country-code top-level domain. Around 400,000 documents appeared to come from advanced malware threats, as they were stored in separate folders focused on individual victims.
Based on the data he personally reviewed, Fowler provided an estimation of the services and domains that were most affected by the breach. The researcher remarked that the compromised accounts might have appeared in multiple documents, which means the database may include several duplicate accounts. Furthermore, the users likely own multiple accounts on different online services.
Fowler provided no definitive explanation for the origin of the dataset. The account collection might have come from multiple malware operations and later been stored in a single archive to be sold through underground marketplaces. The database could even be part of a large, legitimate security operation by other researchers or law enforcement agencies, with experts trying to identify and notify victims or monitor suspected criminal marketplaces.
The researcher did not provide any specific information about where the data archive was stored or which company was hosting it. He only said that he reported the breach to the hosting provider, which took a few days to finally restrict public access. While he did not download any data, Fowler had plenty of time to run queries and make a few estimations.
Massive databases containing billions of potentially compromised accounts are nothing new, and users are contributing to the ever-growing infostealing threat by not following proper opsec when they access online resources. Fowler warned that users should avoid installing unknown browser extensions, downloading unsolicited email attachments, or clicking links in suspicious messages. As the mega-database he discovered clearly demonstrates, sometimes resetting passwords is not enough to stay in the clear. In a worst-case scenario, worried users should consider factory resetting their devices before adopting secure authentication solutions such as password managers or multi-factor authentication.

articles.title: Canadian password manager 1Password has been hacked
articles.text:
Toronto-based password manager 1Password has revealed that it was the victim of a hack that compromised some customer data.
In a blog post this week, the company confirmed that a hacker was able to breach its system through an employee’s corporate GitHub account. From there, the hacker could access customer names and email addresses, as well as non-secret internal metadata about the account. However, 1Password says none of customers’ vault contents or passwords have been leaked.
The company says it’s since disabled the affected GitHub account, added tighter controls and detection tools, and brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate its efforts. It also reminds customers that 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. It adds that suspicious activity can be reported by emailing support@1password.com.
Image credit: 1Password

articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.text:
Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
- Date:
  November 16, 2026
- Source:
  University of Innsbruck
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.
- Share:
As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.
The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.
Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.
A New Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy
The breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.
Quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can quickly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.
But quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," says Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties."
Rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the new approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify important interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.
"From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy."
Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator
To evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.
After this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, showed that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.
This represents an important step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.
Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems
The next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.
"This is particularly important because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important."
The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.
Looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.
"After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," says Peter Zoller.
This shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how quickly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.
The findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.
Story Source:

Journal Reference:

Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, Peter Zoller. Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation via Hamiltonian and Lindbladian Learning. Physical Review X, 2026; 16 (3) DOI: 10.1103/s96t-n8tx

articles.title: How cutting-edge prosthetics can help probe the human mind
articles.text:
How cutting-edge prosthetics can help probe the human mind
Avi Davidson has volunteered to find out how a bionic hand that feels might alter his brain and nervous system.
Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi. He sustained a horrific injury as a teenager, which left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, he uses his own experience to guide his practice as a trauma therapist.
He’s also taking part in a clinical trial of some new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Unlike standard prosthetics, this one connects directly to nerves in Avi's arm. He literally has wires coming out of his arm to plug it in with.
Avi’s the ninth person to trial this tech. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently, for things like drinking from a cup (which is not easy) and writing (also not easy).
What struck me the most over our conversations was Avi’s outlook and approach to not just his injuries and learning to use this cutting-edge technology, but to life itself.
He has learned how to use something like seven different prosthetics in the 17 years since his accident. By taking part in this trial, he’s had to fit hundreds of hours of lab-based training and physical therapy around his demanding job. He had surgery to implant electrodes in his arm and will eventually need another to remove them. And he won’t even get to keep the latest prosthetic long term.
“While it’s unfortunate at times, and irritating at times, I do not regret what has come from [the accident], or the fact that it happened,” he told me. “I am not going to benefit from this … I wanted to be a part of this in the context of being able to help push the technology forward.”
The research team at the University of Utah that is running the trial hopes it will answer longstanding questions about the technology. How does it fare in a real-world setting, outside of the lab? What do people end up using it for? Where can improvements be made?
There may be some surprises along the way. Avi has found that his prosthetic wrist can feel sore and stiff when it’s been overused, just like his flesh-and-blood wrist. Weirdly, that feeling can be relieved by stretching it out. What’s going on here? No one really knows.
Scientists don’t know whether Avi’s brain will change as a result of using the bionic hand, either. Before the trial started, they performed brain scans to see how his missing left hand was represented in his brain. Will that change? And what might that mean for people who are born without limbs—how might a bionic limb affect their brains?
Avi will have the device until late January 2027 at the least, and potentially for another year. After that? Again, no one knows. It will depend on how the research is progressing, how Avi feels, and how much funding the team can secure. As a result, it’s not clear how long the device might even be expected to last in a person’s body.
I’ll be following this study, though, and will keep you posted.

articles.title: This purple electric Chinese minivan can go up to 559 miles on a charge
articles.text:
Electric minivans could be the ultimate in utility, with room for passengers, gear, and huge batteries. While VW’s ID Buzz only gave us 200 miles of real-world driving on a charge in 2023, China’s BYD has just announced a flagship purple peoplemover that can go an estimated 559 miles (900 km) on electricity.
This purple electric Chinese minivan can go up to 559 miles on a charge
The BYD Whale should cost around $45,000, not that you’d be able to buy one here.
It’s called the BYD Whale, and some back-of-the-napkin math suggests it lives up to the name. The van would be bigger than a Honda Odyssey, bigger than a Chrysler Pacifica, and bigger than a Toyota Sienna, at 17.3 feet (5,270mm) long, 6.5 feet (1,996mm) wide, 6 feet (1,815mm) tall, and with a 123-inch (3,130mm) wheelbase.
According to an auto-translated press release, the vehicle should have room for seven passengers and seven suitcases at a time, not that the company has shown off its interior yet. You can see a prominent sensor cluster on its forehead, though, and it’ll come equipped with LiDAR for advanced hands-free driving.
CarNewsChina points out it’s actually not the first with 900 km of CLTC battery range on board — Geely’s all electric Zeekr 009 minivan also claims to offer up to 900 km of range in one configuration. But BYD’s also claiming the can charge its battery from 10 percent to 97 percent in just nine minutes, and it get you from 10 percent to 70 percent in five minutes, according to Electrek.
The Whale will also come in a 248-mile (400 km) plug-in hybrid version as well, and the company’s planning to ship it in China in Q1 of 2027 for around 300,000 yuan. That’s roughly $45,000. As we’ve reported, Chinese cars are becoming quite competitive. Will they make it to the US?

articles.title: China encontra maneira de acessar chips de IA dos EUA mesmo com sanções
articles.text:
A disputa tecnológica entre Estados Unidos e China está avançando para além da fabricação e da comercialização de semicondutores. Com acesso limitado aos chips mais avançados do mercado, empresas chinesas encontraram uma alternativa: utilizar data centers instalados em outros países para alugar poder computacional baseado em tecnologia estadunidense, segundo a DW.
A estratégia tem impulsionado a expansão de centros de dados no Sudeste Asiático, especialmente na Malásia. O país recebeu cerca de US$ 559 bilhões (R$ 3,16 trilhões) em investimentos em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial (IA) desde fevereiro de 2025.
O Estado de Johor concentra boa parte desse crescimento. Dos 27 novos centros de dados mencionados pelo Ministério da Economia Digital malaio, 16 estão localizados na região. A infraestrutura atrai empresas internacionais por oferecer eletricidade relativamente barata e conexões com cabos submarinos que ligam o país a outras partes do mundo.
Como empresas chinesas acessam chips estadunidenses
- Os Estados Unidos impuseram restrições à exportação para a China de chips de alto desempenho, como os produzidos pela Nvidia. Também tentaram dificultar o acesso chinês a equipamentos avançados de litografia fabricados pela holandesa ASML, utilizados na produção de semicondutores;
- Diante dessas limitações, algumas companhias chinesas passaram a recorrer a uma alternativa: em vez de comprar os processadores diretamente, contratam serviços de computação em nuvem ou alugam capacidade de processamento em data centers instalados fora da China;
- Na prática, isso permite desenvolver modelos de IA utilizando GPUs estadunidenses hospedadas em outros países, sem que os chips precisem ser enviados diretamente ao território chinês.
Um levantamento do Institute for Progress (IFP), think tank sediado em Washington (EUA), apontou que o Sudeste Asiático estava se tornando um polo de infraestrutura computacional utilizado por empresas chinesas. Segundo as estimativas citadas pela DW, o acesso remoto a centros de dados estrangeiros poderia representar 24% da capacidade computacional total da China até o fim de 2026. Três quartos dessa infraestrutura estariam no Sudeste Asiático. A projeção do instituto é que essa participação chegue a 31% até o fim de 2027.
O próprio IFP ressalta, porém, que é difícil mensurar o tamanho real dessa operação. Provedores de nuvem e operadores de data centers nem sempre divulgam quem são seus clientes ou quanto de capacidade computacional cada empresa utiliza. As companhias chinesas também fornecem poucas informações sobre suas contratações.
Alibaba e Tencent ampliam presença internacional
A expansão da infraestrutura digital na região também envolve grandes empresas chinesas. A Alibaba Cloud opera seis data centers na Malásia, sendo três em Johor e outros três na região metropolitana de Kuala Lumpur. A unidade mais recente foi inaugurada em 19 de novembro.
A companhia também anunciou investimentos em centros de dados em outros mercados, incluindo Coreia do Sul, Tailândia, Filipinas e México.
Outro movimento envolveu a Tencent. No início de outubro, a empresa assinou um contrato de cinco anos com a Oracle, avaliado em US$ 7 bilhões (R$ 39,6 bilhões). O acordo permitiria acesso a uma capacidade computacional equivalente a 100 mil chips modernos voltados ao treinamento de IA.
O negócio, no entanto, foi cancelado poucas semanas depois. As empresas não divulgaram os motivos, mas relatos da imprensa apontaram pressão dos governos dos Estados Unidos e da China. Pequim busca fortalecer sua própria indústria de semicondutores, enquanto autoridades estadunidenses teriam levantado preocupações de segurança envolvendo a operação.
Leia mais:
- Chips avançados da Nvidia são encontrados em data center chinês ligado à Megaspeed
- OpenAI contra-ataca e acusa Apple de roubar segredos comerciais
- Google é obrigado a interromper construção de data center na Bélgica
EUA tentam fechar brecha nas restrições
Washington também passou a mirar o acesso remoto à infraestrutura de processamento. Na semana passada, o Bureau de Indústria e Segurança, órgão ligado ao Departamento de Comércio dos EUA, estabeleceu novas regras para o acesso a chips e servidores avançados de IA.
O objetivo declarado é impedir que determinados agentes estrangeiros utilizem poder computacional baseado em tecnologia estadunidense de maneira contrária aos interesses de segurança nacional e política externa dos Estados Unidos.
As normas atingem data centers que fornecem capacidade computacional significativa a empresas com vínculos a países classificados no grupo D:5 ou a Macau. A classificação inclui China, Rússia, Irã e Coreia do Norte, entre outros.
As empresas também deverão realizar verificações mais rigorosas sobre a propriedade e o controle de seus clientes, dificultando o uso de intermediários para ocultar quem está efetivamente contratando os serviços.
Além disso, os Estados Unidos introduziram novas exigências de licenciamento para semicondutores avançados destinados a países, como Indonésia, Malásia, Singapura, Tailândia e Brasil. Há exceções para subsidiárias de empresas estadunidenses.
A mudança amplia o alcance das medidas de Washington: além de controlar a exportação dos chips, o governo estadunidense pretende acompanhar onde os equipamentos são utilizados, quem os opera e quais empresas têm acesso à capacidade computacional.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

La cuarta entrega de la saga del arácnido, protagonizada por Tom Holland, volverá a la cartelera por tiempo limitado a partir del próximo 4 de diciembre, y lo hará con escenas eliminadas. Una de ellas tendría conexión directa con Avengers: Doomsday.
Así lo indica un reciente reporte de The New York Times (vía GamesRadar), que plantea que el reestreno de Spider-Man: Brand New Day traerá algunas sorpresas. Si bien no se ofrecen más detalles en tal sentido, al parecer habría material adicional que ayudaría a tender más puentes hacia Avengers: Doomsday, que llega el 18 de diciembre, y Avengers: Secret Wars, cuyo lanzamiento está pautado para finales de 2027.
Si la información es certera, no genera demasiada sorpresa. Después de todo, Marvel Studios viene de lanzar Avengers: Endgame Encore, que cambia la última escena de la película original para conectar con Doomsday. Asimismo, introduce tres escenas postcréditos puntualmente vinculadas con la presentación del Dr. Doom de Robert Downey Jr. Una de ellas, con el villano "recolectando" a Bruce Banner/Hulk del escondite subterráneo en el que permanecía aislado tras los eventos de Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
A esto hay que sumarle el material adicional presentado en el último capítulo de VisionQuest. Allí se observa a Doom reviviendo a Wanda Maximoff, quien parecía haber muerto en el final de Dr. Strange en el multiverso de la locura.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day vuelve a los cines para conectar con Avengers: Doomsday
Es lógico que Marvel Studios quiera aprovechar el gran éxito de Spider-Man: Brand New Day para dar aún más impulso a Avengers: Doomsday. La cinta protagonizada por Tom Holland y Zendaya se mantiene como la más taquillera de 2026, con más de 2.520 millones de dólares de recaudación mundial.
Avengers: Doomsday no solo reintroducirá a Robert Downey Jr en el Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel, ya no como Tony Stark/Iron Man, sino como Victor Von Doom, pues también traerá de regreso a Chris Evans como Steve Rogers. De hecho, el tráiler final de la película se enfoca principalmente en la familia que ha conformado el exCapitán América junto a Peggy Carter.
Lo nuevo de los hermanos Russo trabajará la temática de las incursiones, con el multiverso colapsando y distintas Tierras colisionando. En la escena postcréditos de Spider-Man: Brand New Day, aparecía el rastreador de Spidey creado por Ned mostrando al héroe en Queens, pero detectando a una variante en el espacio. Ya veremos cómo se expande esta situación con el reestreno.
Es importante mencionar que aún no está confirmado que Tom Holland repita como Peter Parker en Avengers: Doomsday. Siempre se especuló con que tras Spider-Man: Brand New Day no regresaría hasta Avengers: Secret Wars. Sin embargo, la historia podría ser diferente.

articles.title: So könnt ihr legendäre Grafik-Demos aus den 90ern im Browser starten
articles.text:
Diese Website bringt 3D-Grafikkarten-Demos aus den 90ern zurück
Nostalgie-Fans aufgepasst: Ein Entwickler hat eine Seite namens GPU Demo Gallery ins Leben gerufen, über die ihr 36 bekannte Grafik-Demos direkt im Browser starten könnt. Die Tech-Demos stammen von 3dfx, ATI und Nvidia und sind in den Jahren 1997 bis 2006 entstanden.
Historische 3D-Rendering-Demos direkt im Browser starten
„Grafikkarten, die ursprünglich zu Präsentationszwecken ausgeliefert wurden – hier anhand der Originaldateien rekonstruiert und direkt im Browser lauffähig“, ist auf der Webseite zu lesen, die Archit Khode kreiert hat.
Mit der GPU Demo Gallery ermöglicht er es Nutzer:innen, nach Hersteller und Erscheinungsjahr zu suchen und historische 3D-Rendering-Demos direkt im Browser zu starten. So können alle Interessierte eine Zeitreise in die Anfangszeit der 3D-Beschleunigung am PC machen.
Auch Claude half bei der Neuimplementierung der Grafik-Demos
Beispielsweise gibt es zwei Indy-Car-Rennwagen, die sich ein Duell auf einer Rennstrecke liefern und man kann dieses aus verschiedenen Perspektiven verfolgen.
Für die „Neuauflage“ der Grafik-Demos nutzte der Entwickler, der in Kalifornien als Software Engineer tätig ist, die Programmiersprache Rust – und griff neben den ursprünglichen 3D-Modellen, Animationen und Texturen laut Winfuture auch auf den KI-Chatbot Claude von Anthropic zurück.
Nostalgiker dürften auf ihre Kosten kommen
Diese Tech-Demos waren in den 1990er-Jahren auch ein Beweis für die Leistungsfähigkeit neuer Grafikkarten. Die berühmte „GeForce 1“ von Nvidia kam als erste Grafikkarte dieser Reihe beispielsweise 1999 auf den Markt. Und auch die Internet-Geschwindigkeit war damals noch ein großes Thema: 2003, als Nvidia vier solcher Tech-Demos für die „GeForce FX“ veröffentlichte, gab es in Deutschland DSL noch nicht flächendeckend – was die Downloads dieser Grafik-Demos erschwerte.
Die Neuimplementierung der Tech-Demos auf Khodes Webseite ist zwar noch nicht komplett (es fehlt beispielsweise der alternde Pick-up von Nvidia) und teilweise auch nicht ganz fehlerfrei. Dennoch dürften Nostalgiker voll auf ihre Kosten kommen.

articles.title: Windows 11 : le masquage automatique de la barre des tâches à gauche et à droite « arrive bientôt »
articles.text:
Il y a quelques mois, Microsoft exauçait le vœu le plus cher de millions d’utilisateurs au sein de Windows 11 : la possibilité de déplacer la barre des tâches. Cette option, déployée à grande échelle avec la mise à jour de sécurité du mois de septembre, a toutefois été accueillie avec quelques réserves.
Car si les utilisateurs ont salué l’arrivée de cette barre des tâches amovible, ils ont aussi reproché à Microsoft d’avoir oublié d’y intégrer certaines fonctionnalités. Microsoft a par exemple omis la possibilité de repositionner celle-ci à l’aide d’un simple glisser-déposer. La firme de Redmond a d’ailleurs été très claire à ce sujet : Windows 11 ne l’autorisera jamais.
L’entreprise a également oublié d’intégrer la possibilité de masquer automatiquement la barre des tâches lorsque celle-ci est positionnée ailleurs qu’en bas de l’écran. Cette absence pourrait néanmoins être très rapidement corrigée.
Le masquage automatique à gauche et à droite « arrive bientôt »
Jusqu’à présent, lorsque vous vous rendez dans le menu Paramètres > Personnalisation > Barre des tâches, l’option qui permet de Masquer automatiquement la barre des tâches ne s’applique que lorsque celle-ci est positionnée en bas de l’écran. Microsoft l’affiche d’ailleurs très clairement dans une petite alerte affichée en dessous de l’option. Mais les choses seraient visiblement sur le point d’évoluer.
Sur X / Twitter, en réponse à un tweet évoquant une nouvelle option pour afficher les fenêtres d’applications ouvertes dans une liste depuis la barre des tâches, un utilisateur a profité de l’occasion pour réclamer une option permettant de masquer automatiquement la barre des tâches lorsque celle-ci était positionnée à gauche ou à droite de l’écran.
 Coming soon!
— Tali Roth 🪟 (@TeaAndDates) November 24, 2026
La réponse n’a pas tardé à venir puisque Tali Roth, responsable produit chez Microsoft a répondu à sa missive en indiquant que la fonction « arrivait bientôt ». La fonction est donc à présent confirmée, mais aucune date de disponibilité ou de déploiement n’est pour l’instant connue. Il faudra sans doute patienter encore quelques semaines pour que celle-ci soit soumise aux tests des Insiders, avant d’arriver officiellement dans la version stable de Windows 11 au cours d’une prochaine mise à jour.

articles.title: Últimas horas de Black Friday: estos son algunos de los mejores chollos que aún puedes conseguir en Lenovo, Dyson, Apple, Pixel y más
articles.text:
En la medianoche de hoy finalizará el Black Friday de 2026. Una edición bastante larga que ha tenido lugar a lo largo de varias semanas en tiendas como PcComponentes, Amazon o MediaMarkt. Y aunque todavía queda el próximo lunes para aprovechar descuentazos, con la llegada del Cyber Monday, aún hay tiempo de aprovechar descuentazos en este 27 de noviembre:
Google Pixel 11 Pro XL
- Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry por 469 euros con cupón, un robot aspirador y fregona ahora con descuentazo
- Pixel 11 Pro XL por 949,05 euros con cupón, a precio mínimo histórico
- Kindle de última generación por 124,99 euros, el modelo más reciente que protagoniza su primera oferta
- PcCom Ready por 1.189 euros, un sobremesa gaming de PcComponentes con una relación calidad precio top
- Alexa Tablet 11 por 199 euros, una de las tablets lanzadas por Amazon hace poco, al 40%
- Mac Mini M6 por 919 euros, el modelo más actual, disponible desde hace pocas semanas, también a precio mínimo
- Lenovo Legion 5 por 1.379 euros, un portátil gaming de gama media ideal para jugar a 60 FPS con buena experiencia
- Sony WH-1000XM4C por 179 euros, el precio más bajo en Amazon en color lavanda
Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry
Dyson no se ha perdido el Black Friday 2026 y, entre sus ofertas, destacamos la del R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry: un robot aspirador y fregona rebajado de 849 euros a 499 euros. Pero que se queda en sólo 469 euros aplicando el cupón 'VFES', casi a mitad de precio. Un dispositivo que aspira, friega y limpia especialmente bien las esquinas gracias a sus mopas triangulares especialmente diseñadas para ello. Con autolavado de almohadillas a 75 grados y una potencia de succión de 21.000 Pa.
Robot aspirador y fregona Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry
Pixel 11 Pro XL
Uno de los chollos en teléfonos de gama alta la ha protagonizado durante el Black Friday de hoy el Pixel 11 Pro XL. Un teléfono reciente, generoso en pantalla y con un apartado de cámaras excelente que se queda a 949,05 euros en MediaMarkt con el código 'PIXELEXTRA5'. Si no llegamos a tiempo o se agota, Amazon también lo ha bajado a su mínimo histórico particular: 999 euros. Con 256 GB de capacidad, varios años de actualizaciones por delante y, ahora, una genial relación calidad precio.
Google Pixel 11 Pro XL
Kindle de última generación
Recientemente, Amazon subió el PVP de su familia Kindle y, poco después, renovó algunos de sus modelos. En este contexto, salió a la venta hace pocas semanas el Kindle basico de 2026 a un PVP de 154,99 euros. Ahora, poco después, encontramos la versión de 16 GB de capacidad, disponible en color negro o morado, a 124,99 euros (con publicidad). Cuenta con pantalla iluminada de 6 pulgadas y una autonomía de varias semanas con una sola carga.
Amazon Kindle (última generación)
PcCom Ready
Aunque el 2026 no es ni de lejos el mejor año para renovar hardware de PC, si compramos un equipo al completo la cosa cambia bastante. Este sobremesa de PcComponentes premontado disponible por 1.189 euros es un buen ejemplo. Una de las mejores opciones de su Black Friday, al ofrecer la RTX 5060 Ti 8 GB, el Ryzen 5 5600XT, 16 GB de RAM y 1 TB de SSD. Además, con Windows 11 Home de serie.
PcCom Ready
Alexa Tablet 11
Las tablets que Amazon puso a la venta hace sólo unos días ya se pueden conseguir a unos geniales precios. Mínimos históricos que han alcanzado durante este Black Friday:
- Alexa Tablet 8 (114 euros)
- Alexa Tablet 11 (199 euros)
- Alexa Tablet 12 Pro (379,99 euros)
Nueva Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, 8 GB de RAM, 64 GB
Y entre todas ellas destacamos el modelo de 11 pulgadas por lo equilibrada que resulta entre gasto y lo que ofrece. Una tablet con 8 GB de RAM y 64 GB de almacenamiento, pantalla con resolución 2,5K y 90 Hz y genial autonomía. Especialmente pensada para sacarle el máximo partido a Alexa+.
Mac Mini M6
La versión más reciente y actualizada del mini PC superventas de Apple tampoco se pierde este Black Friday en su versión con el chip M6: está rebajado a 919 euros en Amazon. Nada mal, teniendo en cuenta su PVP que parte de 1.069 euros y la subida de muchos de sus productos por parte Apple hace unos meses. Un equipo potente gracias a su procesador, que cuenta además con 16 GB de RAM y 256 GB de SSD. Admite varias pantallas y es perfecto para trabajar.
Apple Mac mini con Chip M6
Lenovo Legion 5
En el Black Friday de PcComponentes sigue disponible este portátil gaming de Lenovo a 1.379 euros (y mismo precio en Amazon, una alternativa muy interesante si somos miembros Prime). Un dispositivo con pantalla OLED de 15 pulgadas y un hardware formado por la NVIDIA RTX 5060, el Ryzen 7 250, 32 GB de RAM y 512 GB de SSD. Sin sistema operativo, eso sí, aunque instalarlo es muy sencillo.
Lenovo Legion 5
Sony WH-1000XM4C
Bien valorados, disponibles en tres colores diferentes y, en lavanda, a precio mínimo. Así son estos auriculares Sony rebajados a 179 euros en el Black Friday de Amazon. Una genial oferta que aprovechar si buscábamos unos cascos de diadema inalámbricos, con buena autonomía y cancelación de ruido. En oferta en otros colores, aunque ligeramente más caros (188 euros en negro y mismo precio en blanco).
Sony WH-1000XM4C

articles.text:
When will Agnikul start earning operating revenue?; How neighbourhood medical stores are becoming e-clinics
For the year ended March 31, 2026, Agnikul reported a net loss of Rs 60.22 crore, against Rs 54.79 crore in FY25.
Dear Reader,
Agnikul Cosmos’ next launch is expected in the first half of 2027, with the company indicating that it will demonstrate reusable launch-vehicle and upper-stage technologies. The company reported zero operating revenue for a fourth consecutive year. More on this later in the edition.
Meanwhile, Uber has appointed former Zomato food delivery CEO Rakesh Ranjan as President for India and South Asia as the mobility platform looks to strengthen its presence in one of its largest global markets.
The company operates in more than 225 cities across the country, offering multiple mobility options, including bikes, autos, cars and metro services. More than two million monthly active drivers earn through its platform.
Elsewhere, much like the fictional windtraps of the Dune universe that extract moisture from the dry atmosphere of Arrakis, startups such as Atoco and Ahbstra are testing machines that harvest water from air as they move towards commercial use. Based on Nobel Prize-winning science, metal-organic frameworks power these new-age machines, CNBC reports.
The idea of extracting water from air has been around, but engineering machines capable of harvesting water at a commercial scale has been elusive.
Lastly, if you struggle to stop thinking about unfinished work on weekends, then here’s an article in BBC Future that explains why our brains get stuck and how to actually let go.
Top three recommendations include: creating a transition ritual, turning off notifications and setting time-based goals.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- When will Agnikul start earning operating revenue?
- How neighbourhood medical stores are becoming e-clinics
Here’s your trivia for today: In 1975, engineer Steven Sasson built the world's first self-contained digital camera prototype—weighing nearly 4 kilograms—while working at which photography giant?
Women entrepreneurs
Transforming medical stores into clinics
With Online Chikitsa Mitra, Smriti Tandon is working to make primary healthcare more accessible by transforming neighbourhood medical stores into assisted eClinics. The model now operates in 15 states, with over 600 eClinics and 1.5 lakh consultations, bringing primary healthcare closer to underserved communities, particularly those in rural and remote areas.
Key takeaways:
- The company earns through a partnership fee charged to the shop, which can start at Rs 3,000 for six months and go up to Rs 35,000 for a branded package.
- Online Chikitsa Mitra has specialists across disciplines, including gynaecologists and psychiatrists.
- The company also focuses on free health camps organised by medical-store owners, with dedicated doctors, to raise awareness. The programmes especially cover women's health issues such as fatigue, anaemia, frequent stomach ailments, and persistent fever.

Agnikul’s commercial revenue yet to take off
While Agnikul Cosmos continues to build out the technology and infrastructure for its private launch business, its FY26 audited accounts show those efforts have yet to translate into financial returns. The Chennai-based startup reported zero operating revenue for a fourth consecutive year, even as spending and investment commitments climbed.
Key takeaways:
- For the year ended March 31, 2026, Agnikul reported a net loss of Rs 60.22 crore, against Rs 54.79 crore in FY25.
- The balance sheet points to continued investment. Capital work-in-progress increased to Rs 82.63 crore from Rs 51.30 crore, while property, plant and equipment rose to Rs 34.29 crore from Rs 16.13 crore.
- Agnikul has, however, made progress on the technology front. Its Agnibaan SOrTeD mission, launched on May 30, 2024, was a sub-orbital technology demonstration that tested its indigenous systems, including a single-piece 3D-printed engine.

articles.title: Houston, we have a networking problem: Why NTT thinks space computing is the final frontier
articles.text:
Houston, we have a networking problem: Why NTT thinks space computing is the final frontier
After cloud computing comes space computing, obviously, right? There’s a neat irony here: Real-world clouds can interfere with optical satellite links. Cloud cover (along with atmospheric turbulence) can block the laser-based connections between satellites and ground stations, limiting how much data can be brought down to the data center and cloud services waiting for it. In other words, cloud services on the ground can be held back by the weather they are named after.
Networking conglomerate NTT wants to enable a new era of communications above the clouds (literally) with a combined set of space computing and lunar infrastructure developments that draw heavily on its work in photonics and light-based computing.
The organization’s optical space communication infrastructure is now being aligned with technologies supporting observation and space datacenter creation. The company is also working on lunar surface communication and lunar energy transmission.
Our 88 constellations just got one louder
Today, the International Astronomical Union recognizes 88 constellations in the sky; the NTT C89 project was launched in 2024 to unify and scale the company’s space-related projects and create what it believes could be the 89th constellation.
Speaking to an auditorium of about 200 Japanese press and one reporter from The New Stack during his company’s annual NTT R&D Forum, NTT president and CEO Akira Shimada said that optical ground stations can be blocked by clouds or struggle to receive signals because of atmospheric turbulence.
For Shimada and team, this is why our planet’s communications infrastructure needs to reach for the stars.
“As high-resolution observation data grows, the capacity that can be sent from satellite to ground by radio becomes a challenge.”
“As high-resolution observation data grows, the capacity that can be sent from satellite to ground by radio becomes a challenge,” said Shimada. “A low Earth orbit satellite can communicate directly with a ground receiving facility only during the limited time it passes overhead. In addition to technology that compensates for turbulence, a mechanism will be developed to select which ground station and communication path to connect to according to weather, satellite position and communication conditions.”
Satellite communications crosses the (cloud) chasm
He explained that NTT is developing optical links that connect satellites to one another and to the ground, relaying data from observation satellites to other satellites. Rather than waiting for a satellite to pass over an Earth-based receiving facility, information is delivered via a satellite that can connect to the ground at that exact moment, reducing wait time.
“As connected devices and data, including video, continue to grow and increase, satellite communications need greater capacity and higher quality,” said Shimada. “This field is of growing importance because satellite communications connect places that terrestrial networks struggle to reach, such as mountainous areas, the sea and remote islands”
He further stated that satellite communications at this level also serve as a means of communication when ground facilities are unusable in a disaster. So while image resolution continues to improve, disasters and wildfires now demand real-time delivery, in time for decisions on evacuation, firefighting and recovery. Hence the need to connect more fluidly in space.
Who knew about the lunar power shadow problem?
Not content to work on communications on Earth and in the ether above our planet’s atmosphere, NTT is also looking to enable lunar surface communication and lunar energy transmission. But lunar power isn’t simple; you know about the permanent lunar shadow challenge, right?
As we look to build lunar bases and perhaps one day lunar data centers, these facilities will obviously need solar energy to power them one day. But the Moon’s craters — many of which hold water ice deposits, which will also be essential — often haven’t seen sunlight for billions of years. Lunar scientists call these permanently shadowed regions (PSRs), and they exist because the Moon’s 1.5-degree axial tilt restricts sunlight from moving across the poles, leaving deep crater floors in permanent shadow.
NTT’s work fully recognizes this challenge and also extends to power transmission operations on the lunar surface itself.
“The moon’s craters — many of which hold water ice deposits, which will also be essential [in the construction of lunar datacenters] — often haven’t seen sunlight for billions of years. It’s what lunar scientists call lunar permanently shadowed regions (PSRs).”
“With expanded lunar activity in view, NTT research now covers optical communications to connect the Earth and the Moon in a stable manner; it also extends to work to enable power supply on the lunar surface. For wireless power transmission by laser, the challenges are suppressing the spread of the light and the efficiency of conversion to electricity,” clarified Shimada.
AI processing in space
He says that the “ultimate goal” is to link inter-satellite optical communications, AI processing in space, and terrestrial data centers and optical networks, supporting the understanding of disaster conditions, monitoring of the global environment, and communications in areas where connectivity is difficult.
In June, NTT and Ireland-based MBRYONICS signed a memorandum of understanding to research and develop space optical communications technologies, a step toward launching IOWN (the Innovative Optical and Wireless Network initiative) in space. In September, NTT signed an MoU to connect France-based Cailabs‘ optical ground stations to NTT datacenters via NTT’s All-Photonics Network (APN), a pillar of the IOWN initiative.
“NTT is also working on concepts to place optical ground stations near datacentres, so that information arriving from space can be processed with low latency and delivered where it is needed.”
NTT future concepts work
NTT is also working on concepts to place optical ground stations near datacentres, so that information arriving from space can be processed with low latency and delivered where it is needed. By using datacentres and communication networks around the world, space and the ground will be connected in what the company promises is a seamless manner.
Figures to think about in this arena are the fact that low Earth orbit satellites move at approximately 8 km per second, that it is approximately 380,000 kilometers between the Earth and the Moon, and that some 230 petabytes per day is forecast to be the volume of satellite-to-ground data traffic by 2033, according to NTT.
The next crewed Artemis mission, Artemis III, is a low-Earth-orbit docking test. The first landing is penciled in for Artemis IV in 2028. Let’s hope Artemis III gets close enough to scout a nice crater for the first lunar data center.

articles.title: Les faux cheats Roblox exposent les comptes bancaires des parents
articles.text:
Roblox concentre plus de la moitié des recherches d'outils de triche dans le monde, selon une étude de Cybernews sur 17 grands jeux. Des pirates diffusent de faux logiciels de triche pour ce jeu et récupèrent les mots de passe enregistrés dans le navigateur de l'ordinateur, ceux des parents compris.
Le téléchargement de Roblox est gratuit. Dans les jeux de la plateforme, les armes puissantes, les avantages VIP et les objets rares coûtent en revanche entre 5 et 50 dollars, d'après Cybernews. Sans carte bancaire, les enfants cherchent des raccourcis gratuits sur YouTube ou Google. Pour tricher sur Roblox, il faut un exécuteur de scripts. Ce programme injecte du code dans le jeu pour automatiser des actions ou débloquer des avantages. Windows Defender affiche une alerte au lancement de ces outils, et les jeunes joueurs ont appris à l'ignorer pour accorder les droits d'administrateur à des fichiers téléchargés sur YouTube ou Discord.
Roblox, premier jeu concerné par les recherches de triche
Pour son étude, Cybernews a mesuré la fréquence des recherches d'outils de triche pour 17 grands jeux dans 184 pays, de 2018 à 2026. Ses équipes ont relevé sur Google et Yandex les expressions les plus tapées pays par pays, en anglais et dans les langues locales. Roblox arrive en tête avec plus de 22 millions de recherches. Cybernews relève 482 recherches de triche pour 1 000 joueurs de Roblox, devant Valorant (434) et Call of Duty Warzone (408). Avec 74 recherches pour 1 000 joueurs, Minecraft est six fois moins concerné.
Les pirates profitent de l'anti-triche du jeu. Roblox bloque régulièrement les exécuteurs connus dans son client, et leurs créateurs publient alors de nouvelles versions censées passer inaperçues, d'après BleepingComputer. Les escrocs reprennent cette promesse pour leurs faux outils.
Cet été, on vous a raconté comment de fausses versions « indétectables » de Xeno, un exécuteur très utilisé, circulaient sur des forums de jeu et des serveurs Discord. Avec ce logiciel espion repéré par Bitdefender, les pirates récupèrent les identifiants Roblox, les mots de passe enregistrés dans le navigateur et les jetons Discord de la victime. Ils peuvent aussi enregistrer ses frappes au clavier et capturer les images de sa webcam. En mars, un cybercriminel a mis en vente 50 millions d'identifiants Roblox prétendument volés. Selon Cybernews, ils proviennent probablement d'appareils infectés par un voleur d'informations.
Les comptes bancaires des parents exposés sur l'ordinateur familial
Si votre enfant lance un faux outil de triche sur l'ordinateur de la maison, les pirates peuvent aussi récupérer vos identifiants bancaires, votre adresse e-mail professionnelle et vos fichiers personnels. « Ce n'est pas seulement leur avatar Roblox qui est en jeu », prévient Cybernews. En France, Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr met en garde contre les voleurs d'informations diffusés sous forme de logiciels de triche et d'extensions pour les jeux vidéo, sur YouTube ou Discord.
Cybernews conseille d'abord de limiter les droits d'administrateur sur le compte Windows de votre enfant. Avec un compte standard, Windows lui demande le mot de passe d'un administrateur avant d'installer un programme. Dans le contrôle parental de Roblox, vous pouvez lier votre compte à celui de votre enfant, après avoir vérifié votre âge avec une pièce d'identité ou une carte bancaire. Vous fixez alors des limites de temps d'écran et de dépenses.
Roblox propose aussi la vérification en deux étapes et la clé d'accès pour protéger le compte. Ces protections bloquent un pirate muni d'un mot de passe volé. Votre navigateur conserve toutefois un jeton de session pour garder votre compte connecté. Avec ce jeton volé, un pirate contourne ces protections. Trois suspects arrêtés en Ukraine en avril se connectaient ainsi aux comptes Roblox de leurs victimes sans mot de passe, selon les enquêteurs ukrainiens cités par Cybernews. Ils sont soupçonnés d'avoir piraté plus de 610 000 comptes.

articles.title: Face aux barrières de l’UE, Geely va installer sa nouvelle plateforme électrique dans l’usine Ford de Valence
articles.text:
Des voitures chinoises fabriquées dans une usine Ford ? L’idée circulait dès février et elle a été rapidement matérialisée. Au printemps, Geely a négocié le rachat d’une partie de l’usine Ford de Valence, puis c’est au mois de juillet que les deux groupes ont officialisé une coentreprise sur ce site espagnol. Ford en détient 66 % et Geely 34 %. Cinq modèles doivent y sortir à partir de 2028, dont deux SUV électriques Geely.
Ce vendredi 27 novembre, Michael Yang, directeur général de Geely Auto UK, en a dit plus sur le projet à Automotive News Europe. On apprend désormais que Geely va également installer à Valence une toute nouvelle plateforme électrifiée, pensée pour le marché européen. Une partie de la future gamme européenne de Geely reposera donc sur une base produite sur place.
Michael Yang n’a pas dit quels modèles utiliseront cette plateforme. En revanche, il a confirmé l’arrivée d’un petit SUV au Royaume-Uni en 2028, en version 100 % électrique et en hybride rechargeable (PHEV). Il n’a pas voulu commenter les rumeurs selon lesquelles le Galaxy Cruiser 700, le gros SUV tout-terrain hybride rechargeable de la marque, serait produit à Valence. En Chine, ce SUV annonce jusqu’à 1 113 ch, tirés d’un moteur essence 2.0 turbo et de trois moteurs électriques, alimentés par une batterie de 47 kWh, plus grosse que celle de nombreuses citadines électriques.
Geely vend aujourd’hui trois modèles en Europe : le SUV hybride rechargeable Starray, la citadine électrique E2 (EX2) et le SUV Geely E5 (EX5). Tous les trois reposent sur GEA, l’architecture électrifiée actuelle du groupe. C’est aussi elle que la coentreprise Renault Geely va utiliser au Brésil pour ses électriques.
Ford va aussi utiliser cette architecture à Valence. Cet été, An Conghui, président de Geely Automobile Holdings, a confirmé que le futur crossover multi-énergie de Ford pour l’Europe reposerait sur GEA.
Pourquoi Geely produit dans les usines des autres
Geely cherche d’abord à éviter les barrières commerciales de l’Union européenne. Depuis le 30 octobre 2024, la Commission européenne surtaxe les voitures électriques importées de Chine. Pour Geely, la surtaxe est de 18,8 %, en plus des 10 % de douane habituels. Jusqu’ici, les hybrides y échappaient. Mais à partir de ce mardi 1er décembre, l’UE plafonne les importations d’hybrides chinoises pour 200 jours, sur la base de 350 000 véhicules par an. Or le Starray, un hybride rechargeable, est le modèle de Geely le plus vendu en Europe. D’après le cabinet d’études Dataforce, la marque en a écoulé 39 483 de janvier à octobre.
Valence ne suffira pas. Michael Yang l’a dit sans détour : « On ne peut pas produire un ou deux modèles dans l’UE et importer le reste depuis la Chine. Ça ne marche pas. » Les marques Geely et Zeekr pourront donc aussi passer par les usines européennes de Volvo, marque que le groupe chinois a rachetée à… Ford en 2010.
BYD suit la même démarche en se rapprochant de l’usine de Hambach, en France. Sur le papier, la méthode de Geely coûte moins cher qu’une usine construite de zéro. En contrepartie, Geely reste minoritaire à Valence, où Ford garde la main.
D’ici 2028, Geely veut proposer 16 modèles en Europe. Parmi les nouveaux venus prévus : un grand SUV, un SUV intermédiaire, trois petits SUV et une citadine. La coentreprise de Valence doit démarrer au premier semestre 2027, mais les premières Geely assemblées en Espagne ne sortiront pas avant 2028.

articles.title: TV Hisense et pistage audio : voici le seul réglage qui coupe vraiment l'envoi de vos données
articles.text:
Il pensait pourtant avoir fait le nécessaire en désactivant les publicités personnalisées. Le propriétaire d’un téléviseur Hisense a découvert que son écran continuait d’envoyer, toutes les 2,7 secondes, un résumé codé de ce qu’il regardait à Nexxen, une régie publicitaire israélienne.
Pour le repérer, ce Britannique a dû déchiffrer le trafic réseau de sa propre télévision, un passe-temps de week-end peu banal. Vous ne trouvez pas ? On ne jugera pas.
Contrairement à ce qu’on pourrait craindre, le micro n’est pas en cause dans son analyse : le système est beaucoup plus discret, et il tourne dès la première configuration.
En coulisses, tout passe par un programme nommé HamService qui fonctionne en tâche de fond sur Vidaa, le système d’exploitation maison de Hisense. Il embarque un SDK (un bloc de code fourni par un tiers) de Nexxen dédié à l’ACR, la reconnaissance automatique de contenus : une technologie pensée pour identifier ce que vous regardez et revendre ces données.
Le téléviseur résume le son chaque quart de seconde en une empreinte de 72 bits, puis envoie toutes les 2,7 secondes les dix dernières lignes accompagnées de son identifiant fixe, de l’heure, de l’entrée utilisée et de l’application ouverte. Ce débit minuscule (270 bits par seconde, contre 128 000 pour l’audio d’origine) ne permet pas de réécouter votre salon, mais suffit largement à reconnaître un film ou une série. Rien d’étonnant sur le plan financier : Nexxen a investi 60 millions de dollars dans Vidaa et signé en août 2025 un accès mondial exclusif à ses données ACR, ce qui éclaire d’un jour nouveau une interface qui impose ses publicités.
Immersion à 360° et design innovant : pour le Black Friday, la barre de son Samsung HW-Q995H passe à 890 € chez la Fnac, soit 600 € de remise.
    Pour aller plus loin
Téléviseurs Hisense et publicités forcées : un « test » qui a de quoi inquiéter
            
Console, box, PC : tout ce qui sort des haut-parleurs
Le plus frappant, c’est que rien ne lui échappe. HamService capte le son juste après le décodage, au moment où il part vers les haut-parleurs : il identifie donc aussi bien l’application Netflix intégrée qu’une console de jeux ou une box opérateur branchée en HDMI, du moment que le téléviseur est connecté à Internet.
Pour vérifier sa découverte, le chercheur a recalculé les empreintes du court-métrage libre Big Buck Bunny et obtenu 88 % de correspondance, contre 55 % pour un son quelconque.
Quant à la case « Publicités personnalisées », elle ne touche qu’à l’identifiant publicitaire : toutes les empreintes continuaient de partir une fois l’option coupée. Pire, lors du premier allumage, le bouton « Tout sélectionner » est mis en avant par défaut.
Hisense est loin d’être un cas isolé, comme nous l’expliquions déjà à propos de LG et du reste du secteur. En décembre 2025, le procureur général du Texas, Ken Paxton, avait d’ailleurs attaqué cinq fabricants (dont Hisense), les accusant de surveiller à leur insu ce que regardaient leurs clients, sources HDMI incluses. Il affirmait que Hisense captait sons et images toutes les 500 millisecondes, obtenant même une ordonnance temporaire pour bloquer cette collecte au Texas. Même si le travail de gwerneckp ne porte que sur l’audio, il apporte une preuve technique concrète à ces accusations texanes, que le compte International Cyber Digest a relayées sur X.
    Pour aller plus loin
Ces 5 fabricants de TV sont accusés d’enregistrer en secret ce que vous regardez
            
Le chercheur n’a étudié qu’un seul téléviseur britannique (le 55U65QEVS) sous une version précise de Vidaa (U09.60) : rien ne prouve formellement que les modèles vendus en France réagissent à l’identique, même si l’accord avec Nexxen est mondial, et sa description du calcul reste une rétro-ingénierie.
Autre détail gênant : décocher la bonne case stoppe bien les envois vers Internet, mais HamService continue d’écouter le flux audio en local et une mise à jour peut tout réactiver.
Un second processus garde aussi le micro ouvert en permanence, sans qu’aucune donnée n’ait toutefois été observée en train d’en sortir.
Comment couper l’empreinte audio sur une TV Hisense
Les intitulés ci-dessous proviennent du modèle britannique testé (les menus français peuvent varier légèrement), mais la marche à suivre reste la même.
Pensez simplement à revérifier ces deux écrans après chaque mise à jour système :
- Settings > Support > Disclaimer and Privacy > Data Sharing, Privacy and EULA : décochez « Agree to Enhanced Viewing Service » (l’interrupteur principal) ainsi que « Allow Data Sharing to see Ads relevant to you », laissez le reste coché puis validez.
- Settings > System > Advanced Settings > Enhanced Viewing Settings : désactivez les cinq interrupteurs, dont « Automatic Content Recognition ».
- Au niveau du réseau : si vous utilisez un bloqueur DNS comme Pi-hole, bloquez acr.unruly.co et ses sous-domaines (Unruly appartient à Nexxen). Une liste de blocage connue en intègre déjà une partie.
- La solution radicale : laissez le téléviseur totalement déconnecté d’Internet et confiez le streaming à un boîtier externe (Apple TV, Google TV, Nvidia Shield) branché en HDMI.
Je vous avoue qu’on n’est même plus étonné à ce stade-là. Hisense n’invente rien, et nous rappelions déjà que tous les constructeurs de téléviseurs misent désormais sur l’ACR pour rentabiliser leurs écrans.
Ce qui agace vraiment ici, c’est l’illusion du choix : un bouton « Tout sélectionner » mis en avant dès l’installation, et un réglage « Publicités personnalisées » qui rassure l’utilisateur sans rien couper d’essentiel.
Quitte à glisser des pubs forcées dans ses menus, la marque pourrait au moins rendre le vrai interrupteur facile à trouver.
